NpBFkL2BTm.one_liner: Pretrains 1B models from scratch on web text with swapped-in fiction sources to measure fiction's effect on creative writing.
NpBFkL2BTm.problem: Why book data matters for LLM pretraining, central to copyright lawsuits, remains opaque outside industry labs.
NpBFkL2BTm.method: Trains 1B-parameter models under controlled token budgets on web text alone, with public-domain books, with contemporary fiction, and with both, then examines what makes fiction distinct and whether a synthetic data recipe recovers its benefits while hampering provenance attacks.
NpBFkL2BTm.key_idea: Hold the token budget and everything else fixed while swapping the fiction component, then test whether synthetic fiction replicates the gains.
NpBFkL2BTm.evidence: 1B-parameter models pretrained from scratch on four data mixes, evaluated on creative writing (EQ-Bench and LitBench per reviews), plus membership inference and extraction attacks.
NpBFkL2BTm.claimed_gains: The abstract gives no numbers; a review cites Books3 EQ-Bench win rates of 78.6% against NoBooks and 91.1% against Institutional Books.
NpBFkL2BTm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled design (equal token budgets, one swapped fiction component per condition) answers a timely pretraining-data and copyright question clearly, with well-motivated experiments.
NpBFkL2BTm.main_concern: Creative-writing conclusions rest on LLM-judge scores with thin human validation, and synthetic books conditioned on Books3 confound the source of the synthetic gains.

KgTCtyntyy.one_liner: Applies contrastive guidance to Beckmann transport models' probability current by subtracting current toward mismatched image-label pairs.
KgTCtyntyy.problem: Beckmann Transport Models learn one-step generative maps without distillation, but their quality lags methods that rely on guidance, which a native map cannot apply because it has no velocity or score to combine.
KgTCtyntyy.method: Since the probability current defining a BTM is linear in the target distribution, CBM subtracts the current toward mismatched image-label pairs, obtained by pairing each label with another image in the batch, during training. Sampling still needs one network call.
KgTCtyntyy.key_idea: Subtract the probability current of mismatched image-label pairs from the matched current during training, which repels samples from negative pairs.
KgTCtyntyy.evidence: ImageNet 256x256 with fine-tuning of a converged BTM model, from-scratch training, a toy experiment, and continued-training and matched-pair controls.
KgTCtyntyy.claimed_gains: Fine-tuning a converged BTM with CBM for around 15% of an epoch lowers one-step FID from 20.8 to 6.7, and to 5.5 with postprocessing, on ImageNet 256x256.
KgTCtyntyy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree CBM gives clear, cheap gains with one-step sampling and no teacher or feature encoder, resting on the simple observation that probability currents add where velocities do not.
KgTCtyntyy.main_concern: The theoretically grounded variant helps only in short fine-tuning and is unstable from scratch, while the guidance scale is fixed at training time and sensitivity to batch size is untested.

gpt1K3Ia4D.one_liner: Trains a LoRA honesty adapter to confess hidden behavior or deception in transcripts, outperforming activation probes out of distribution.
gpt1K3Ia4D.problem: Activation probes trained on off-policy data are cheap deception monitors but often fail to generalize to on-policy deception outside their training distribution.
gpt1K3Ia4D.method: Trains a LoRA honesty adapter stacked on the model to report whether it showed a hidden behavior or deception in a transcript, using on-policy transcripts from 533 model organisms; the monitor score compares a forced admission against a forced denial.
gpt1K3Ia4D.key_idea: Fine-tune a LoRA adapter on on-policy model-organism transcripts to admit hidden behavior, scoring forced admission versus forced denial instead of probing activations.
gpt1K3Ia4D.evidence: Qwen3-14B and Llama-3.3-70B adapters evaluated on held-out organisms, AuditBench, and off-policy benchmarks of lies, reward hacking and hard-coded test cases, against probes and an introspection adapter.
gpt1K3Ia4D.claimed_gains: On AuditBench the Qwen3-14B adapter reaches 0.90 AUROC versus 0.74 for a probe trained on the same data and 0.66 for a probe trained on off-policy deception, with near-perfect AUROC on held-out organisms.
gpt1K3Ia4D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a meaningful, lightweight monitoring contribution with strong out-of-distribution results on AuditBench, careful data construction and ablations.
gpt1K3Ia4D.main_concern: It is unclear whether the gains come from reading the transcript rather than model internals (no text-only monitor with matched supervision), and implanted behaviors may not reflect real-world deception.

Y4A4FVeZKh.one_liner: Randomized algorithms train Gaussian SVMs in truly subquadratic time at high precision on separated finite-alphabet inputs via exact kernel-product procedures.
Y4A4FVeZKh.problem: Fast solvers for a fixed feature representation do not imply high-precision training of the original Gaussian SVM kernel objective in subquadratic time.
Y4A4FVeZKh.method: Constructs an exact kernel-product procedure whose single success event covers all real weight vectors including adaptive signed queries, uses tensor spectral bounds for fast optimization, and extends via local Taylor features and a diagonal correction to inputs with additional real coordinates.
Y4A4FVeZKh.key_idea: Exploit coordinate structure with an exact kernel-product procedure valid for all adaptive signed queries simultaneously, then turn these products into fast optimization through tensor spectral bounds.
Y4A4FVeZKh.evidence: Theoretical proofs covering hard and soft margins with or without bias, with no numerical or empirical evidence per reviews.
Y4A4FVeZKh.claimed_gains: Trains n inputs in d <= C log n dimensions to additive dual objective error exp[-(log n)^3] using n^{2-delta+o(1)} arithmetic operations for some constant delta > 0, with near-linear preprocessing and space.
Y4A4FVeZKh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the end-to-end high-precision training guarantee is a meaningful theoretical advance, covering hard and soft margins and handling adaptive queries and repeated inputs soundly.
Y4A4FVeZKh.main_concern: The result is purely asymptotic and restricted (separated finite alphabet, logarithmic dimension, few continuous coordinates), with no numerical evidence of when it beats naive quadratic solvers.

25Brkn2TKR.one_liner: Text-conditioned all-atom protein structure generation, adapting Proteina-Complexa with a 1.8M-structure captioned dataset and residue-text alignment finetuning.
25Brkn2TKR.problem: Existing protein design models need a dedicated input representation for each property, which limits the design objectives they can support.
25Brkn2TKR.method: Prompteina adapts the pretrained Proteina-Complexa through text-conditioned pretraining and finetuning that aligns residues with their corresponding text, using global and token-level text conditioning. It is trained on Prompteina-Data, 1.8M structures with 50M+ captions of structural and functional properties.
25Brkn2TKR.key_idea: Condition a pretrained structure generator on global and token-level natural-language captions, with finetuning that aligns residues to their corresponding text spans.
25Brkn2TKR.evidence: Structural control across 18 properties, binder design on 20 targets including iterative in silico feedback, caption-quality audits, and wet-lab validation against the target GM2A.
25Brkn2TKR.claimed_gains: Outperforms baselines on 15 of 18 structural properties, leads on at least 13 of 20 binder targets with 14% higher interface confidence than the strongest baseline, and its gain from iterative feedback is 57% larger than the next-best baseline on the hardest targets.
25Brkn2TKR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find natural language a useful single interface for global and residue-level protein design, and credit the large paired dataset, thorough ablations and strong results over baselines.
25Brkn2TKR.main_concern: Improved scores do not establish precise control, as reviewers cite a weak CATH verifier (47.2% per-category accuracy), modest count correlations, and natural-language conditioning performing similarly to dedicated CATH labels.

OYNwdjRvQZ.one_liner: JEPA world model trained to reproduce a similarity kernel in embedding geometry, including a temporal kernel using only observation order.
OYNwdjRvQZ.problem: It is unclear what information a latent world model should preserve, since JEPA methods rely on prediction objectives and collapse-prevention regularizers without explicit control over retained information.
OYNwdjRvQZ.method: SpecWM specifies relationships between observations through a teacher similarity kernel and trains the encoder to reproduce them in its embedding geometry, together with action-conditioned latent prediction. Kernels range from physical state information to a self-supervised temporal kernel, and the theory covers global optima, linear recoverability, nuisance invariance and a link to the successor measure.
OYNwdjRvQZ.key_idea: Train the encoder with spectral alignment so embedding similarities match a chosen teacher kernel, such as temporal proximity within trajectories, instead of leaving geometry to emerge from prediction.
OYNwdjRvQZ.evidence: CEM planning on three visual manipulation environments (OGBench Cube, OGBench Scene, CALVIN) against LeWorldModel with 100 fixed tasks per environment, plus kernel-recoverability analyses and theory on global optima.
OYNwdjRvQZ.claimed_gains: Temporal spectral alignment raises CEM planning success over LeWorldModel from 52% to 68% on OGBench Cube, 49% to 77% on OGBench Scene, and 27% to 51% on CALVIN.
OYNwdjRvQZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea of specifying the similarity structure to preserve easy to grasp and well motivated, with consistent planning improvements over LeWorldModel in three manipulation environments.
OYNwdjRvQZ.main_concern: Planning gains cannot be attributed uniquely to spectral alignment because SpecWM and LeWorldModel also differ in prediction loss (cosine versus MSE), and the successor-measure theory does not match the trained objective.

VibyhbBwVK.one_liner: Trains one hierarchical policy conditioned on cognitive parameters, then inverts it to infer subtasking strategies and cognitive profiles from behavior.
VibyhbBwVK.problem: Analyzing human behavior with bounded rationality in naturalistic tasks requires computing optimal solutions under many candidate cognitive profiles, which does not scale.
VibyhbBwVK.method: CCDIP trains a single hierarchical policy that takes cognitive parameters as input and yields tractable action likelihoods. Inverting this forward model recovers people's subtasking strategies and cognitive profiles from observed behavior.
VibyhbBwVK.key_idea: Amortize planning across cognitive profiles with one parameter-conditioned hierarchical policy, then infer parameters by inverting its action likelihoods.
VibyhbBwVK.evidence: Simulation recovering parameters of agents with known profiles, and a new driving-task dataset (N = 39 participants, about 345,000 timesteps).
VibyhbBwVK.claimed_gains: Qualitative findings only: attentional factors are needed to explain driving behavior and cognitive parameters show stable individual differences (N = 39, about 345,000 timesteps); no accuracy numbers stated.
VibyhbBwVK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the amortized, parameter-conditioned hierarchical policy a clean and scalable way to fit individual cognitive profiles, with good fit to human driving actions.
VibyhbBwVK.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing comparisons with established cognitive model-fitting methods and underspecified or inconsistent model details (four versus two conditioning parameters, trajectory-likelihood implementation).

IMLGVETBqj.one_liner: Regularizes sparse autoencoders so evolved code versions share active latent supports, enabling index reuse in code retrieval.
IMLGVETBqj.problem: Code retrieval pipelines treat each version of evolving code as an independent target, ignoring whether related versions can share stable index-facing structure.
IMLGVETBqj.method: Proposes continuality-preserved sparse coding, which augments sparse autoencoder training with two lightweight evolution-aware regularizers, including a neuron-overlap regularizer that encourages behaviorally similar variants to activate shared neurons. Evaluated on the new CODECONTINUUM-R benchmark.
IMLGVETBqj.key_idea: Encourage similar code variants to activate shared sparse latents so their discrete support signatures overlap, allowing delta updates instead of storing separate embeddings.
IMLGVETBqj.evidence: CODECONTINUUM-R, a benchmark of version families spanning surface-level rewrites, local structural edits, and refactorings built from standard code-search examples; Python only.
IMLGVETBqj.claimed_gains: Not stated in the available abstract; the TL;DR mentions significant storage savings without numbers.
IMLGVETBqj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the evolving-codebase indexing problem practical and under-explored, the three-tier benchmark systematic, and the regularizers effective at improving support overlap.
IMLGVETBqj.main_concern: The setting assumes old and new versions coexist in the codebase, evaluation is Python only, and relevance labels for evolved variants are not fully guaranteed (semantic pass rates of 88.96% and 93.43% at the upper two levels).

So6ihb3XR5.one_liner: Measures how many bits Transformers store about latent knowledge expressed in many surface forms, using a synthetic hierarchical grammar.
So6ihb3XR5.problem: Capacity results for fixed-token-form knowledge do not cover natural-language knowledge, which has many surface forms and abstraction levels.
So6ihb3XR5.method: Defines stored information as the bits saved when encoding fresh realizations of a latent knowledge piece versus a reference that knows the generating process, and applies it to the Random Hierarchy Model, where knowledge can be placed at any tree level.
So6ihb3XR5.key_idea: Treat knowledge as a latent variable expanded into many token sequences and measure its stored bits on unseen realizations, giving stored information b = rN - n Delta.
So6ihb3XR5.evidence: Controlled experiments varying model size, dataset size, and training exposure on the Random Hierarchy Model, with probes and an associative-memory model for frequency effects.
So6ihb3XR5.claimed_gains: No performance gains claimed; stored information follows b = rN - n Delta at every abstraction level, after models first learn the shared grammar and then memorize.
So6ihb3XR5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the latent-knowledge framing a useful extension of memorization studies, supported by substantial controlled experiments and interpretable analyses.
So6ihb3XR5.main_concern: Claims about the cost of abstraction are not isolated from confounds (information per piece, dataset ceiling, identification difficulty), use one grammar, and may not translate to real models.

ZpkxX0dIzD.one_liner: A process reward that checks each cited proof step against a knowledge graph's OWL 2 RL closure.
ZpkxX0dIzD.problem: Knowledge-intensive domains lack verifiers for reasoning steps, so a correct answer reached by unsound reasoning receives full credit.
ZpkxX0dIzD.method: Reasonable-RLVR verifies each cited proof step against the OWL 2 RL closure of a graph and checks that the steps establish the answer, using a relation contract and configurable coverage, with no reference proof or learned judge. Two reward forms are defined: a two-band form and a weighted sum.
ZpkxX0dIzD.key_idea: Use entailment in the knowledge graph's OWL 2 RL closure as a decidable per-step verifier for the reward, rather than outcome match or reference-path overlap.
ZpkxX0dIzD.evidence: Four knowledge-graph benchmarks including WebQSP over three seeds, compared with outcome and reference-path rewards, plus verifier feedback at inference for frontier models.
ZpkxX0dIzD.claimed_gains: Without a supervised warm-up on WebQSP, reaches 0.597 +- 0.120 correct-and-valid proofs over three seeds, while the outcome reward reaches 0.000 at 94% answer accuracy.
ZpkxX0dIzD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the step-level verification more targeted than outcome or reference-path rewards and value the independent audit of 2,000 trajectories and the analysis of reward-design failure modes.
ZpkxX0dIzD.main_concern: Gains in correct-and-valid rate may largely reflect alignment between the training reward and the evaluation criteria, and the benchmarks lack richer ontology rules, with the relation contract still derived from reference paths.

MpWfEs4E4v.one_liner: Builds domain-expert LLMs by prompting and fine-tuning and tests whether each aligns best with its matching brain system.
MpWfEs4E4v.problem: LLM-brain alignment is usually measured with one model across all regions, which ignores the functional specialization of brain regions.
MpWfEs4E4v.method: Builds expert LLM variants for six domains (sensory, spatial, numerical, reasoning, social, abstract) via prompting and fine-tuning, then uses voxelwise fMRI encoding to test whether each expert best predicts activity in its corresponding brain region.
MpWfEs4E4v.key_idea: Specializing a model toward a cognitive domain shifts regional alignment toward the brain system for that domain, measured by each expert's relative ranking within each region.
MpWfEs4E4v.evidence: Three base models, prompting and LoRA fine-tuning, three fMRI datasets, and control families including random prompts, random adapters, and surface-form interventions.
MpWfEs4E4v.claimed_gains: Each expert aligns more closely with its matching brain system than other experts do, with aggregate prediction accuracy largely unchanged; no numbers are stated.
MpWfEs4E4v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question interesting and the experiments broad, with strong control analyses showing the effect is specific to cognitive-domain interventions.
MpWfEs4E4v.main_concern: The primary displacement metric is relative with very small absolute gains (as low as the order of 1e-4 on LPP), and the domain-to-region mapping from Neurosynth is a debatable choice.

raVv5eoGMs.one_liner: Studies when test-time adaptation recovers utility lost to label differential privacy without extra privacy cost.
raVv5eoGMs.problem: Label differential privacy often degrades accuracy, and symmetric randomized-response noise contracts the label posterior toward uniform with a privacy-dependent excess clean risk.
raVv5eoGMs.method: Applies test-time adaptation, which uses only the released model and unlabeled inputs, to LabelDP-trained models and characterizes empirically when it helps, including which components (batch-norm statistics versus entropy updates) matter.
raVv5eoGMs.key_idea: Test-time adaptation is post-processing of the released model, so it adds no training-label privacy cost, and batch-norm statistic re-estimation drives much of the corruption-robustness benefit.
raVv5eoGMs.evidence: CIFAR-10/100, their corruption benchmarks, and ImageNet64 subsets across four TTA methods, with failure analysis for small batches and label-correlated streams.
raVv5eoGMs.claimed_gains: On clean CIFAR-10, TENT lowers the error of every LabelDP model, with gains growing from 0.76 to 3.76 points as privacy strengthens, up to 4.55 points more than matched label smoothing.
raVv5eoGMs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the deployment-time perspective practically relevant, the post-processing privacy argument clean, and the empirical characterization extensive across budgets, datasets, and TTA methods.
raVv5eoGMs.main_concern: The explanation for why TTA helps is not established, since symmetric randomized response preserves the Bayes decision, and the theory covers symmetric RR while the main experiments use a different mechanism (LP-MST).

XNWznBITkl.one_liner: Parameterizes each attention head as delta(gamma I + P) with learnable gamma and delta to mix attention and Laplacian.
XNWznBITkl.problem: Using both attention and Laplacian heads helps, but how to best combine the two operators is unclear.
XNWznBITkl.method: Each head's operator is delta(gamma I + P) with learnable gamma and delta. When gamma lies in (-1, 0), the convex corridor, the operator is a scaled convex combination of attention P and the negative Laplacian P - I.
XNWznBITkl.key_idea: Learn a per-head identity-attention mixture with signed gamma; trained heads mostly settle in gamma in (-1, 0), a convex blend of attention and negative Laplacian.
XNWznBITkl.evidence: Causal language-model pretraining across tested model scales, analysis of gamma and delta over training across initializations and alternative parameterizations, and ablations.
XNWznBITkl.claimed_gains: Consistently lower validation loss in causal language-model pretraining across tested model scales; no numbers are stated.
XNWznBITkl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the experiments and ablations thorough, the narrative clear, and the analysis of learned gamma and delta informative.
XNWznBITkl.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the parameterization reparameterizes the learned identity-attention mixture in Value-SkipInit, and only two model scales limit the scaling evidence.

DcVLe4srFu.one_liner: Normalization couples Fourier-sector dynamics in group-composition networks, so independent sector scoring predicts the winner exactly only at degree-matched weight 2.
DcVLe4srFu.problem: An additive objective can separate across candidate representations while the normalized dynamics that optimize it do not, so it is unclear when the selected representation can be predicted by scoring candidates independently.
DcVLe4srFu.method: In a two-layer quadratic network on a finite group's multiplication table with real Fourier sectors as candidates, the authors analyze sector-local scoring rules under a joint input sphere with metric weight omega and an output sphere of weight one, constructing paired initializations that differ only by reflecting one output block.
DcVLe4srFu.key_idea: The sphere-projection multiplier depends on the sum of all sector terms, creating cross-sector coupling even though the leading objective has no cross-sector terms.
DcVLe4srFu.evidence: Theoretical proofs (e.g., Theorem 3.1) for groups with at least three nontrivial real Fourier sectors, plus a numerically checked XOR example (0.081% Monte Carlo estimate, per reviews).
DcVLe4srFu.claimed_gains: For groups with at least three nontrivial real Fourier sectors, sector-local rules recover the leading selector almost everywhere if and only if omega = 2; at every other fixed weight their errors are bounded away from zero.
DcVLe4srFu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the exact characterization and the reflection-pair counterexample, where a never-winning sector changes which rival wins, give a clear and technically solid limit on independent scoring.
DcVLe4srFu.main_concern: The practical error magnitude of sector-local approximation at finite scale is unquantified, the motivation for exact representation prediction is thin, and the presentation is hard to follow without specialized terminology.

wlT0Oy0zY1.one_liner: Lightweight modulator predicts a frozen DINOv3's re-encoded features for a queried box from the coarse global map, distilled without labels.
wlT0Oy0zY1.problem: A vision foundation model encodes one global view into a low-resolution grid and can look closer only by re-running a crop through the backbone, and feature upsamplers do not change the scale of analysis fixed by that single global pass.
wlT0Oy0zY1.method: Conditioned on a point query, FoRE runs a lightweight modulator on the coarse map and the queried box of the same global view, predicting the features the backbone would produce by re-encoding the box at native resolution. Training distills against the backbone's own re-encodings and needs no labels or backbone updates.
wlT0Oy0zY1.key_idea: Predicts the backbone's own crop re-encoding from the existing global feature view (a remapping of encoded features, not a pixel reconstruction) instead of upsampling features.
wlT0Oy0zY1.evidence: 25 datasets, more than fifteen readouts, and three domains, with multiple backbones and feature-upsampling baselines, including transfer from aerial-only training to natural and indoor images (per reviews).
wlT0Oy0zY1.claimed_gains: Predicts re-encoded features in 2.8 milliseconds per query and almost six times more cheaply, and its features are the strongest source apart from the teacher almost everywhere, leading every upsampling baseline by wide margins.
wlT0Oy0zY1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree FoRE is well motivated and practical, cheaply reusing one global encoding for several region queries on a frozen backbone, and is evaluated broadly with strong cross-domain generalization.
wlT0Oy0zY1.main_concern: The paper is hard to read with undefined terms, a closely related method (FeatSharp) is missing, evaluation uses a crop-grid protocol rather than standard pixel-level tasks, and gains are not isolated from architecture and training changes.

na5FtbxXCy.one_liner: Proposes Sentiment and Helpfulness Consistency metrics for covert political bias and RL-based Political Consistency Training to reduce it.
na5FtbxXCy.problem: LLMs handle counterpart topics from opposing political sides asymmetrically in rhetoric, framing, and depth of engagement (covert political bias), which overt left-right preference scores miss.
na5FtbxXCy.method: The authors identify 7 categories of techniques through which covert bias operates and define Sentiment Consistency (symmetry of rhetoric and framing across paired political prompts) and Helpfulness Consistency (symmetric depth and engagement). Political Consistency Training (PCT) is an RL method with two paradigms, Sentiment Consistency Training and Helpfulness Consistency Training, targeting the two metrics.
na5FtbxXCy.key_idea: Scores asymmetry between paired opposing-side political prompts on sentiment and helpfulness, then trains with RL to make the paired scores consistent.
na5FtbxXCy.evidence: Paired political prompts (about 50 pairs per a review) scored by judge models, with cross-judge, per-template, and out-of-distribution held-out benchmark checks.
na5FtbxXCy.claimed_gains: not stated numerically: PCT preserves overall helpfulness, substantially reduces covert political bias, and generalizes to held-out benchmarks.
na5FtbxXCy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that looking beyond overt left-right scores is well motivated, with a thorough taxonomy, published judge prompts, large gains over the base model, and useful out-of-distribution checks.
na5FtbxXCy.main_concern: Construct validity is questioned: averaging single-response scores may not measure comparable help across sides, symmetric treatment is not necessarily unbiased treatment, and the 50 polarized topic pairs are narrowly chosen.

iMKJmbumOJ.one_liner: RateQuant allocates KV-cache bit-widths across layers and heads from measured attention responses using dynamic programming and remeasurement
iMKJmbumOJ.problem: KV cache compression needs precision allocation under a memory budget, but allocation is coupled through the existing attention error and inputs from earlier quantized layers.
iMKJmbumOJ.method: A rate-distortion framework measures attention responses to adjacent bit-width changes, combines them by dynamic programming into budget-preserving joint updates, and remeasures to refresh them for the next round. Full-model cross-entropy on separate calibration data selects the final allocation.
iMKJmbumOJ.key_idea: Measure how each adjacent bit-width change reinforces or cancels the existing attention error, then solve budget-preserving joint allocation updates by dynamic programming with remeasurement.
iMKJmbumOJ.evidence: Three models and two quantizers at 2-3-bit budgets, plus LongBench with five tasks, with analysis linking normalized attention distortion to task loss under bounded suffix sensitivity.
iMKJmbumOJ.claimed_gains: Lowest perplexity in all 18 settings spanning 2-3-bit budgets, with reductions of 12.6-94.5% at 2 bits and 3.2-10.3% at 2.5 bits versus each setting's strongest tested baseline, and highest three-model mean scores in all 30 LongBench evaluation settings.
iMKJmbumOJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the allocation criterion principled, accounting for the actual attention error, with clear methodology and consistently lowest reported perplexity.
iMKJmbumOJ.main_concern: Key ablations are missing (conditional distortion measurement, remeasurement, head-wise allocation, dynamic programming, simple first-layer protection) and comparison with advanced allocation methods is limited.

MI1cmK7rjZ.one_liner: Intrinsic barrier-proximal method with exponential-map Dikin exploration gives one-point bandit convex optimization on Riemannian manifolds
MI1cmK7rjZ.problem: Adversarial bandit convex optimization lacks methods for Riemannian manifolds that have no global affine structure.
MI1cmK7rjZ.method: Combines exponential-map Dikin exploration with single-step updates based on scalar logarithmic surrogates, using a squared-distance analysis that avoids aggregating tangent vectors across base points or assuming surrogate convexity. Bounds the curvature-induced estimator-to-smoothing support error under C^2 loss regularity and gives a two-point extension.
MI1cmK7rjZ.key_idea: Explore with Dikin ellipsoids pushed through the exponential map and update with scalar logarithmic barrier surrogates, analyzed by squared distance rather than by aggregating tangent vectors.
MI1cmK7rjZ.evidence: A regret theorem conditional on compact-interior iterates and uniform smooth normal-tube data, plus covariance-tracking experiments on symmetric positive definite manifolds with one- and two-point feedback.
MI1cmK7rjZ.claimed_gains: Tilde-O(T^(2/3)) one-point regret against nonanticipating adversaries, conditional on compact-interior iterates and uniform smooth normal-tube data.
MI1cmK7rjZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit this as the first self-concordant barrier approach to bandit optimization on Riemannian manifolds, with a clear separation of loss-difference estimation error from update stability.
MI1cmK7rjZ.main_concern: The main theorem assumes iterates stay in a compact interior and relies on a non-standard assumption, the role of self-concordance is unclear, and the writing is very dense.

kTuIMbhP1E.one_liner: Benchmark of nine marketplace environments and eight steering mechanisms showing computer-use agents fail to buy the user-optimal product.
kTuIMbhP1E.problem: Existing computer-use agent benchmarks cover cooperative settings or explicit attacks, not environments with their own incentives that steer agents away from the user's objective.
kTuIMbhP1E.method: CAVEAT is a controlled benchmark with matched-control episodes across nine marketplaces and a taxonomy of eight steering mechanisms. CAVEAT-Harness targets three diagnosed decision failures, and targeted post-training further improves an open-weight model.
kTuIMbhP1E.key_idea: Compare agents on matched controls with and without steering, diagnose premature narrowing, imposed priorities, and early commitment, then add a harness targeting those failures.
kTuIMbhP1E.evidence: Evaluation across six model families on nine marketplace environments, with trajectory analysis, single-mechanism and targeted ablations, and scaling across model size and reasoning.
kTuIMbhP1E.claimed_gains: Agents buy the user-optimal product in 80.9% of matched-control episodes but only 22.3% with steering enabled, and CAVEAT-Harness raises the optimal purchase rate by up to 80.0 percentage points.
kTuIMbhP1E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is timely and important, the steering mechanisms come from real practices and are ablated individually, and the evaluation is extensive across models with matched controls.
kTuIMbhP1E.main_concern: Mitigation evidence is preliminary and under-specified: the verification tool and CAVEAT-hard setup are not fully described, the harness helps GPT models but not Qwen3.5, and the Hard set has only five tasks.

rkwjB4SHlt.one_liner: Low-rank Value latent reused for tensor-parallel communication, Value-cache compression, and sparse Key-page routing in long-context LLM inference.
rkwjB4SHlt.problem: Low-rank KV-cache compression is optimized in isolation, ignoring the tensor-parallel communication cost incurred when attention is partitioned across multiple GPUs.
rkwjB4SHlt.method: Jointly fits low-rank factors across per-GPU attention partitions against the complete attention output, and ties Value compression to the output projection so one latent cuts both Value-cache width and communication. The compressed Value cache also predicts which Key pages to fetch, with a Key-specific residual for what Value cannot recover.
rkwjB4SHlt.key_idea: One low-rank Value latent, fit jointly across GPU partitions to the full attention output, serves Value caching, tensor-parallel communication, and Key page routing.
rkwjB4SHlt.evidence: Per the reviews, evaluation spans multiple model families, retention budgets, long-context benchmarks, and tensor-parallel settings on 8 L40S GPUs, compared with PaLU on perplexity and multiple-choice tasks (abstract is truncated).
rkwjB4SHlt.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is truncated before any results.
rkwjB4SHlt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing one low-rank Value representation for caching, communication, and routing is a coherent, practically motivated systems design with better quality than baselines on language modeling and long-context tasks.
rkwjB4SHlt.main_concern: Efficiency claims are not quality- or latency-matched (perplexity and accuracy degrade at the speedup setting, end-to-end speedup is modest on non-NVLink GPUs), and the PaLU comparison may be unfair.

rjGmCfxxWx.one_liner: Tests whether taxonomic hierarchy appears as nested child-in-parent subspaces in vision, language, and vision-language transformer representations.
rjGmCfxxWx.problem: It is unclear whether networks trained on hierarchically labeled data encode that hierarchy in their representations, and in what geometric form, since models are never told that a beagle is a dog.
rjGmCfxxWx.method: Defines two measurements: whether a child concept's subspace is contained in its parent's, and whether the parent's feature fires concurrently with the child's. It applies them to small transformers on synthetic tree-structured data and to pretrained vision, language, and vision-language models.
rjGmCfxxWx.key_idea: Separate the geometry of hierarchy (child subspace contained in parent subspace) from its readout (parent feature firing on the child), each tested against shuffled and held-out controls.
rjGmCfxxWx.evidence: Small transformers trained on synthetic tree-structured versus non-hierarchical data, plus pretrained vision, language, and vision-language model families, including the image encoders of the latter (CLIP, ViT, DINO).
rjGmCfxxWx.claimed_gains: not stated; this is an empirical study and the abstract reports no numeric results.
rjGmCfxxWx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controls are carefully designed (held-out parents, shuffled and firing-rate-matched controls) and that separating containment from subsumption across many model families is informative.
rjGmCfxxWx.main_concern: The measurements may not distinguish hierarchical nesting from shared variation among semantically similar concepts, and several claims (nesting at every depth, training objective determining readout) go beyond the evidence.

rLTvq1qYn6.one_liner: Self-distills the model's own with-versus-without system-prompt prediction shift, amplified, into a system-prompt-conditioned student.
rLTvq1qYn6.problem: LLMs often fail to follow system prompts, especially when they conflict with user requests or learned tendencies, and existing fixes need external supervision or extra decoding computation.
rLTvq1qYn6.method: CoSSy contrasts predictions with and without the system prompt, amplifies the resulting shift, and distills it into a student that keeps the system prompt, with no external responses or preference labels and standard decoding at inference.
rLTvq1qYn6.key_idea: Amplify the prediction shift between system-conditioned and unconditioned runs, as in contrastive decoding, and train the system-conditioned student to match it token by token.
rLTvq1qYn6.evidence: Three LLMs on general system-message following and challenging adherence benchmarks including Multifaceted-Bench and IFBench, with multi-turn evaluation and ablations.
rLTvq1qYn6.claimed_gains: Improves over the base models by 8.6% relative on average on Multifaceted-Bench and by 49.7% on IFBench Strict.
rLTvq1qYn6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple and cheap, needing no external responses or teacher, with comprehensive experiments, strong matched baselines, and no inference overhead.
rLTvq1qYn6.main_concern: The contribution is incremental over contrastive decoding (CAD), and the main results lack variance estimates while some analyses cover only one model and benchmark.

wJiybghpGY.one_liner: Searches LLM-proposed natural-language strategies, each realized as code through iterative synthesis, to find programmatic RL policies.
wJiybghpGY.problem: Synthesizing programmatic policies through environment interaction is hard because the program space is vast and small syntactic changes can cause large, unpredictable behavior changes.
wJiybghpGY.method: LLM-proposed natural language programs specify candidate strategies, and iterative Python code synthesis translates each into an executable policy, with environment feedback guiding the two-level search.
wJiybghpGY.key_idea: Search in an abstraction of program space (natural-language strategies), committing to several execution-guided code refinements per strategy before judging it.
wJiybghpGY.evidence: A large set of MiniHack tasks, with component ablations; reviews note a single environment.
wJiybghpGY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper well written, with an interesting two-level design and committed code realization that reduces randomness in turning strategies into programs.
wJiybghpGY.main_concern: Evaluation lacks simpler search-harness baselines and covers only MiniHack, with best-observed scores taken from noisy few-episode evaluations.

BD501aT6sD.one_liner: Scores anomalies by how hard randomly masked coordinates are to reconstruct under a masked diffusion model trained on nominal data.
BD501aT6sD.problem: Anomaly detection for categorical and discrete data is challenging and relatively underexplored.
BD501aT6sD.method: MaskDiff-AD trains a masked diffusion model only on nominal data and, at test time, computes anomaly scores from the difficulty of reconstructing randomly masked coordinates, without reverse-time sampling. A non-parametric variant is included, with analysis of Type-I and Type-II errors under a fixed detection threshold.
BD501aT6sD.key_idea: Average masked conditional negative log-probabilities over masking levels and random masks as a forward-only anomaly score directly on discrete state spaces.
BD501aT6sD.evidence: Fourteen tabular datasets and four text anomaly detection datasets against baselines, with runtime, probe-mask sensitivity, and matched-compute NELBO comparisons per reviewers, plus Type-I and Type-II error theory.
BD501aT6sD.claimed_gains: MaskDiff-AD attains the best overall average rank among evaluated methods on fourteen tabular datasets and competitive performance on four text datasets, with no numeric scores stated.
BD501aT6sD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that scoring directly on discrete data without reverse-time sampling is natural and practical, with broad experiments on tabular and text datasets and relevant baselines.
BD501aT6sD.main_concern: Reviewers say the score is close to existing masked-prediction anomaly detection with only modest gains over matched NELBO scoring, the theory assumes score separation that cannot be verified, and DTE-Gaussian stays stronger on mean PR-AUC.

tElW3FnYAX.one_liner: Learns a GNN target subspace where groups emerge as supernodes, then extracts them with adapted Ward clustering.
tElW3FnYAX.problem: Graph learning reduces group-level problems like money laundering and fraud rings to node-level prediction, although group members may look unremarkable in isolation.
tElW3FnYAX.method: From training groups, a GNN-parameterized target subspace is learned so unknown groups coarsen into supernodes, using a loss derived from target-subspace properties. Ward clustering is adapted with a merge score linked to coarsening error, with bounds on group-indicator distortion and supernode purity and sufficient conditions for exact group recovery.
tElW3FnYAX.key_idea: Learn from example groups a subspace in which group members coalesce under coarsening, then merge nodes with a Ward score tied to coarsening error.
tElW3FnYAX.evidence: Experiments on synthetic, financial (Elliptic++) and large community graphs (Amazon, DBLP, email-Eu-core) with transfer to unseen graphs, plus bounds and exact-recovery conditions.
tElW3FnYAX.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract says high-precision detection across synthetic, financial and large community graphs with transfer to unseen graphs.
tElW3FnYAX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating the group as the unit of prediction via learned coarsening is a well-motivated formulation, with an interpretable theory (capture and confusability) linked to Ward-style recovery.
tElW3FnYAX.main_concern: The evaluation does not establish detection: best-match group metrics ignore irrelevant output blocks, and comparisons omit closely related semi-supervised community detection methods (SEAL, CLARE, ProCom, RevTrack).

o0ZgbRKI4B.one_liner: Traces deep-search agent trajectories by whether gold evidence has surfaced and whether the gold answer has appeared.
o0ZgbRKI4B.problem: Process signals for deep-search agents score actions but ignore the information the agent has acquired, confounding what an action contributes with what the agent already knew.
o0ZgbRKI4B.method: Evidence-Answer Tracing marks two events per trajectory by comparing with the ground-truth trajectory, evidence exposure and answer surfacing, and uses them to re-evaluate existing agents on a unified footing, borrowing from resource-rational theory.
o0ZgbRKI4B.key_idea: Compare each trajectory with the gold trajectory to mark when gold documents surface and when the gold answer appears, conditioning process signals on that evidence-answer state.
o0ZgbRKI4B.evidence: Applied to 25 systems on BrowseComp-Plus, with question-level cross-fitting, question and agent fixed effects, and robustness checks (abstract truncated).
o0ZgbRKI4B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that tracking both evidence exposure and answer surfacing is a useful perspective beyond effort-based signals, supported by careful controls such as cross-fitting and fixed effects.
o0ZgbRKI4B.main_concern: Answer surfacing depends on literal answer-string matching that misses valid variants unevenly (91.4% Top5, 73.9% Mid, 37.5% Weak), and the practical value over simple gold-document recall is unclear.

xoQ0MWtjwj.one_liner: Force-conditioned video generation that first predicts velocity and visibility maps, then renders them with a trajectory-conditioned video generator.
xoQ0MWtjwj.problem: Mapping force controls directly to video supervises only per-frame appearance, so videos can look realistic without following the intended force direction or strength.
xoQ0MWtjwj.method: FoMo, given an initial frame, relative force and initial velocity, predicts initial-frame-indexed velocity and visibility maps, integrates velocities into trajectories, and passes them to a pretrained trajectory-conditioned video generator; relative 2D controls are derived from real-video motion changes and semantic physical priors are used.
xoQ0MWtjwj.key_idea: Decouple motion-state prediction (velocity and visibility maps with direct supervision) from rendering by a pretrained trajectory-conditioned generator focused only on visual synthesis.
xoQ0MWtjwj.evidence: Per the reviews, ablations compare velocity, acceleration and trajectory targets on one backbone, Goal Force is fine-tuned on the same data, and a 100-participant study evaluates final videos.
xoQ0MWtjwj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that predicting an explicit motion state as an intermediate target is well motivated and supported by ablations and human preference results.
xoQ0MWtjwj.main_concern: Control sensitivity is not tested directly: there is no direction and magnitude sweep on a fixed scene, and the relative force is derived from observed image-space motion rather than real forces.

HgoWG3GwxO.one_liner: Speculative decoding that drafts the next block during verification using predicted target hidden states and self-refining parallel drafts.
HgoWG3GwxO.problem: Speculative decoding speed depends on both the acceptance rate of drafted tokens and the cost of producing them, and drafting sits on the critical path.
HgoWG3GwxO.method: JetSpec++ combines intra-block self refinement (the draft model iteratively corrects its own parallel predictions), inter-block foresight drafting (starts the next block before the current one is verified), and pipelined drafting and verification overlap.
HgoWG3GwxO.key_idea: Predict the target's hidden states and verification outcome so the next block is drafted during verification, and train the drafter to self-refine by Jacobi iteration.
HgoWG3GwxO.evidence: Seven benchmarks on GB200 against speculative decoding baselines including DSpark; reviewers note the experiments use an 8B target model.
HgoWG3GwxO.claimed_gains: Up to 6.74× wall-clock speedup over autoregressive decoding and 1.41× over DSpark, up to 1250 TPS single-request throughput on GB200, and an average acceptance length of 7.60 across seven benchmarks.
HgoWG3GwxO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the algorithm-system co-design of foresight drafting, self-refinement and pipelining hides drafting cost and gives large speedups, with informative ablations.
HgoWG3GwxO.main_concern: The headline speedup compares 2 GPUs for JetSpec++ with 1 GPU for DSpark, and only an 8B target is evaluated, so efficiency at equal resources and scaling are unestablished.

HWvcN027fr.one_liner: Synthesizes reasoning training problems from diagnoses of a student's failed traces, pairing two diagnoses per generated problem.
HWvcN027fr.problem: Synthetic-data specifications built from task descriptions or capability labels show broad weak regions but not where the student's reasoning failed.
HWvcN027fr.method: DDS has a teacher inspect each failed solution trace and write a directive on where the reasoning broke, pairs two diagnoses via diagnostic crossover so a generator writes one problem needing both repairs, and filters candidates with a verifier before fine-tuning.
HWvcN027fr.key_idea: Use the student's incorrect trace, not a capability label, as the synthesis signal, and cross two diagnoses into a single problem requiring joint repair.
HWvcN027fr.evidence: Math reasoning on Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, plus a 7B VLM multimodal test per the reviews, compared with baselines at equal data budget.
HWvcN027fr.claimed_gains: On Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, +12.6 and +8.0 Pass@1 points on the student's failed problems, +7.54 and +8.32 on the held-out math average, and +2.82 and +3.18 over the strongest baseline at the same patch budget.
HWvcN027fr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that targeting the student's specific reasoning failures is a sensible way to build training data, and that the gains are broad and supported by extensive experiments.
HWvcN027fr.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate whether the student-specific diagnosis, the two-failure crossover, or generally useful teacher supervision drives the gains, and only small student models were tested.

lZTCitkTMi.one_liner: TRIPWIRE escalates tool actions to a fallback by expected avoidable commitment risk from failure likelihood and irreversibility.
lZTCitkTMi.problem: Selective-execution strategies for tool-using agents rely on model uncertainty or coarse action categories, ignoring how consequential and irreversible an action's failure would be.
lZTCitkTMi.method: Estimates commitment risk from predicted failure likelihood, action irreversibility and an application-dependent severity cost, combines it with expected fallback failure risk to get avoidable commitment risk, and calibrates the policy to a target level of residual irreversible harm among autonomously executed actions.
lZTCitkTMi.key_idea: Route each action by avoidable commitment risk, the expected harm escalation can prevent, computed from failure probability, irreversibility, severity and the fallback's own failure risk.
lZTCitkTMi.evidence: Multiple agent backbones (seven per a reviewer) and tool-use environments at matched escalation budgets against uncertainty-based routing and mutation gating, plus oracle analyses.
lZTCitkTMi.claimed_gains: Reduces realized irreversible harm at matched escalation budgets relative to uncertainty-based routing and mutation gating; no numbers stated.
lZTCitkTMi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important and that weighting failures by consequence and fallback value is principled and gives promising results across backbones and budgets.
lZTCitkTMi.main_concern: The risk formula is heuristic with unvalidated component estimates, failure prediction may do most of the work, and conceptual novelty over deferral work such as ReDAct and CORA is incremental.

hNX8VA0hi4.one_liner: Few high-mass keys generate attention's local low-dimensional geometry; exact computation on them closes most of the kernel-realization gap.
hNX8VA0hi4.problem: Efficient long-context attention assumes low-dimensional query-key structure yields cheap, accurate attention that preserves answers, but this chain of assumptions has not been tested link by link.
hNX8VA0hi4.method: In two frozen language models, tests the chain using local coordinates adapted to each query block, comparing an exact-exponential diagnostic with finite-state kernel summaries and with exact computation on selected keys, at matched storage and matched arithmetic.
hNX8VA0hi4.key_idea: Adapt local coordinates per query block to separate retained directions from kernel realization, then show under one percent of keys (high-mass) rebuild the geometry.
hNX8VA0hi4.evidence: Controlled diagnostics in two frozen language models (Llama and Qwen per reviewers), replicated on fresh inputs and a third model, with controls for projection error and attention sinks, plus full-model task tests.
hNX8VA0hi4.claimed_gains: A set of high-mass keys under one percent of the history rebuilds nearly all useful local geometry and exact computation on them closes most of the gap; the low-dimensional remainder pays off under matched storage but never under matched arithmetic.
hNX8VA0hi4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnostics are carefully designed with strong controls, and that the matched-storage versus matched-arithmetic comparison gives a useful empirical insight.
hNX8VA0hi4.main_concern: The conceptual advance over prior work such as Scatterbrain and LoLA is limited, and the structural analysis rests on only 20 test problems shared across models.

vH2vmp8ezT.one_liner: ToolSciVer teaches VLMs to verify scientific claims with a type-aware evidence tool suite via self-distillation then GRPO.
vH2vmp8ezT.problem: VLMs struggle to extract localized evidence from text, tables and figures and combine it through multi-step reasoning; generic crop-and-zoom tools return only pixels and prompting tool use can hurt accuracy.
vH2vmp8ezT.method: SciEviKit returns structured evidence (table rows or columns, chart values, zoomed regions). Training has two stages: On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) bootstraps tool use from reference tool calls alone, then GRPO optimizes a reward coupling accuracy with tool-call validity and efficiency.
vH2vmp8ezT.key_idea: Return structured evidence from type-aware tools instead of pixels, bootstrap tool calls with on-policy self-distillation from reference calls, then optimize accuracy, validity and efficiency with GRPO.
vH2vmp8ezT.evidence: SciVer and MuSciClaims with three backbones (Qwen, InternVL, Gemma) against five baselines covering non-tool reasoning, training-free agents and RL-based tool use, plus ablations.
vH2vmp8ezT.claimed_gains: Improves over non-tool chain-of-thought by 8.16 points on SciVer and 7.92 on MuSciClaims, and over the strongest baselines by 3.70 and 2.23 points.
vH2vmp8ezT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the type-aware structured tools and the OPSD warm-start are reasonable designs and that evaluation is broad across backbones and benchmarks with useful ablations.
vH2vmp8ezT.main_concern: Reviewers flag checkpoint selection on evaluation data (optimistic bias risk), limited novelty over known tool-use RL recipes, and chart reading delegated to a stronger frontier model.

8SkxedsVil.one_liner: ELITE self-improves coding agents without task evaluation by implementing diverse proposals independently, then merging compatible mechanisms.
8SkxedsVil.problem: Evaluate-and-select self-improving coding agents need repeated downstream task execution, which raises cost with broader exploration and may encourage benchmark-specific adaptation.
8SkxedsVil.method: Each generation proposes diverse focused improvements, implements them independently from the same parent, inspects the programs to find complementary, redundant and conflicting mechanisms, and reimplements a compatible subset as one descendant. Only deterministic structural and operational validity checks run inside the loop.
8SkxedsVil.key_idea: Inspect independently implemented child programs for complementary, redundant and conflicting mechanisms and reimplement a compatible subset as one descendant, using no task scores to guide evolution.
8SkxedsVil.evidence: SWE-bench Pro (the abstract is cut off here), with ablations, code-level examples and transfer results per reviewers.
8SkxedsVil.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract (a reviewer cites one run rising from 60.0% to 81.7% after the first accepted update and reaching 86.7%).
8SkxedsVil.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that cutting costly downstream evaluation from agent self-improvement is a compelling motivation and that the evaluation-free approach reaches comparable performance.
8SkxedsVil.main_concern: Evidence is thin: baselines have a single run with no statistics, much of the gain may come from fixing basic scaffold limits, and removing evaluation is not separated from integrating modifications.

USw9ykuPYE.one_liner: The Storage-Compression-Targets framework casts backprop, predictive coding and target propagation as rules that store, compress and align activity.
USw9ykuPYE.problem: The mechanisms behind feature learning, and behind catastrophic forgetting under distributional shift, remain poorly understood.
USw9ykuPYE.method: Defines a framework that unifies learning as storing associations, compressing representations and aligning neural activity with local targets, analyzes representation drift under storage and compression rules, and derives a replay-based correction (HOPc, per reviewers) for class-incremental learning.
USw9ykuPYE.key_idea: Compression alone can reorganize retrieval geometry to produce features but also drift, so preventing forgetting needs corrections coupled to the current sample plus replay or a generative proxy.
USw9ykuPYE.evidence: Proofs on representation drift and an empirical test of a replay-based correction on class-incremental benchmarks (Split-CIFAR-10 with DER++ per reviewers).
USw9ykuPYE.claimed_gains: The replay-based correction improves retention and sample efficiency of replay-based methods; no numbers stated.
USw9ykuPYE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework gives a unified, mathematically grounded view of learning and forgetting and that the correction term improves replay-based class-incremental learning.
USw9ykuPYE.main_concern: Empirical comparisons are weak: unequal memory budget (extra storage of about 49 samples), only older baselines such as DER++, no Split CIFAR-100, and no restoration-only control.

I0pgwz9Luw.one_liner: Controlled experiments vary demographic opinion mixtures across five SFT, DPO and GRPO post-training paths to study value-preference amplification.
I0pgwz9Luw.problem: Post-training corpora with imbalanced demographic opinions may amplify the imbalance and underrepresent some groups, and how mixtures interact with post-training paths is unclear.
I0pgwz9Luw.method: Trains with corpora of different opinion mixtures over five post-training paths (SFT, DPO, GRPO), then measures amplification, whether further post-training removes preferences, stability under interventions, and transfer to student models through distillation.
I0pgwz9Luw.key_idea: Hold prompts and corpus size fixed while varying opinion mixture and post-training path, including stage order (DPO then GRPO versus GRPO then DPO).
I0pgwz9Luw.evidence: Controlled experiments on OpinionQA-based mixtures (per reviewers) with five post-training paths, intervention tests and distillation to student models.
I0pgwz9Luw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled mixture-by-path design is systematic and useful, notably the path-order comparisons and the finding that preferences transfer through distillation.
I0pgwz9Luw.main_concern: Reversing option order or contents often reverses the observed trend, so the measurements may reflect label or position bias rather than semantic value preferences.

3CTRewjriG.one_liner: PAPF accelerates fixed-point iterations with a degree-two polynomial filter that mixes the identity and two applications of the operator.
3CTRewjriG.problem: Fixed-point iterations can converge slowly, and it is unclear when a simple filter improves the local convergence factor over the equal-cost baseline T^2.
3CTRewjriG.method: Applies S_alpha = alpha*I + (1-alpha)*T^2 (Lookahead with two inner steps), proves global convergence for firmly nonexpansive operators, gives an if-and-only-if spectral criterion for local improvement, and selects alpha from the spectrum or from residual probes.
3CTRewjriG.key_idea: Exploit the phases of dominant Jacobian eigenvalues: mixing T^2 with the identity improves the local convergence factor if and only if cos(2*theta_j) < rho^2 for each dominant eigenvalue.
3CTRewjriG.evidence: Theory (global convergence for firmly nonexpansive operators, a speedup limit, a convex parameter-selection problem) and experiments with competing accelerators, including an optimal-transport test and reported failure cases.
3CTRewjriG.claimed_gains: For firmly nonexpansive operators the asymptotic speedup in operator evaluations is limited to less than 3/2; no empirical gains are stated in the visible abstract.
3CTRewjriG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper states clearly when the filter helps and when it does not, compares by operator calls, and openly reports unfavorable results alongside competing accelerators.
3CTRewjriG.main_concern: Reviewers cite substantial overlap with prior Lookahead theory (PAPF is Lookahead with k=2), a scope limited to oscillatory spectra, and automatic parameter selection that costs about 140 extra operator calls and can fail.

5q71a1z4oO.one_liner: APEX actively probes agentic workflows, guided by a rubric tree, to localize weak units and aspects before failures occur.
5q71a1z4oO.problem: Failure attribution only analyzes already-failed runs, blames a single agent and step, and cannot say which unit (agent, channel, memory, tool) or which aspect is weak before deployment failures.
5q71a1z4oO.method: APEX adaptively and progressively runs probes that target the assertions of a dynamically generated rubric tree it is statistically least confident about. AXE records what every unit was given and changed and can perturb any unit in isolation, and AXEBench provides labeled perturbed workflows.
5q71a1z4oO.key_idea: Run probes on the rubric-tree assertions with the highest statistical uncertainty, using an engine that perturbs any single unit, to localize weak units and aspects.
5q71a1z4oO.evidence: AXEBench of perturbed workflows against VerifyMAS, DCFA, DoVer and the three Who&When methods, plus agent-only and random-probe comparisons and a repair study per reviewers.
5q71a1z4oO.claimed_gains: Outperforms existing failure attribution methods on AXEBench (abstract is cut off here); no numbers stated.
5q71a1z4oO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that localizing weak channels, memory and tools beyond agents is useful for repair and that fixed-budget comparisons with random probing isolate the benefit of adaptive testing.
5q71a1z4oO.main_concern: The main baselines can name only agents and the localizer prompt encodes the fault model, so gains on channel, memory and tool faults are not compared with a simple LLM reading the same traces.

sy983SmQYr.one_liner: TangentAttnRes aggregates past layer outputs by attention in tangent space to stabilize residual connections in hyperbolic LLMs.
sy983SmQYr.problem: Existing hyperbolic residual connections need exceedingly large layer embedding norms to change embedding directions and are not robust to larger layer outputs, which hinders scaling hyperbolic LLMs.
sy983SmQYr.method: TangentAttnRes maps features to the tangent space at the origin, aggregates them there with attention-based weighting over past layer outputs, and maps the result back to the manifold with the exponential map.
sy983SmQYr.key_idea: Aggregate past layer outputs in tangent space, so smaller norms change direction, with attention weights that dampen the impact of unstable layers.
sy983SmQYr.evidence: Hyperbolic decoder (HELM-D), hyperbolic encoders (BERT, HyTE-FH) and language Transformers across benchmarks, up to 259M decoder and 1.483B encoder parameters per a reviewer.
sy983SmQYr.claimed_gains: Improves performance over existing residual connections across models and benchmarks; no numbers stated.
sy983SmQYr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the two instabilities are clearly identified and linked to norm growth, with consistent gains across architectures and scales and little training-time overhead.
sy983SmQYr.main_concern: Scaling claims go beyond the tested sizes (largest decoder 259M parameters), and the proofs mostly follow from tangent-space convex combinations and do not bound individual layer outputs.

iuhUSzikNJ.one_liner: NBField reconstructs sharp 12MP images from handheld bursts by integrating a shared 2D neural image along SO(3) rotational homographies.
iuhUSzikNJ.problem: Burst deblurring methods assume translation-based, spatially invariant blur, but real camera motion is often rotation-dominated and strongly spatially varying at high resolution.
iuhUSzikNJ.method: Represents exposure motion in SO(3) with a single 2D implicit neural representation shared across frames. A differentiable forward model integrates the image along rotational homographies, and alternating optimization refines the image and gyroscope-initialized motion without supervised training.
iuhUSzikNJ.key_idea: Model blur as continuous camera rotation in SO(3) integrated over exposure through a shared 2D neural image field, optimizing image and gyro-initialized motion jointly without supervision.
iuhUSzikNJ.evidence: 447 in-the-wild GoPro bursts spanning severe shake blur in natural and low-light scenes, reconstructed at native 12MP.
iuhUSzikNJ.claimed_gains: Improves PSNR by an average of 5.75 dB over the best blurry input frame and 3.87 dB over the best baseline, reconstructing each burst in 2.4 minutes on a single GPU.
iuhUSzikNJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the depth-independent rotational model with a shared 2D field is physically grounded, handles spatially varying blur and is practical at 12MP.
iuhUSzikNJ.main_concern: Ablations are missing (fixed-gyro trajectory, spline parameterization, loss weighting) and the ground-truth acquisition for handheld captures, which all reported metrics depend on, is unexplained.

q1gu1Lfrx0.one_liner: REPORTER is a 22-task benchmark from massively parallel reporter assays for evaluating pretrained genomic representations on regulatory function.
q1gu1Lfrx0.problem: It is hard to assess whether pretrained genomic representations broadly capture sequences' gene-regulatory function.
q1gu1Lfrx0.method: Curates 22 transfer-learning tasks from 14 public massively parallel reporter assay experiments (over 2.5 million DNA sequences) and evaluates genomic language models and AlphaGenome as pretrained backbones.
q1gu1Lfrx0.key_idea: Evaluate pretrained genomic backbones on 22 MPRA-derived tasks spanning transcription, splicing and UTR regulation across taxa, with sequence-identity-aware train/test splits.
q1gu1Lfrx0.evidence: Benchmarks 25 gLM backbones, including six species-specific MLM baselines the authors pretrained, and AlphaGenome against models trained from scratch.
q1gu1Lfrx0.claimed_gains: The best gLMs outperform models trained from scratch on all 22 tasks but fall short of AlphaGenome on four of five mammalian transcription tasks; no single gLM dominates.
q1gu1Lfrx0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a substantial benchmark with careful biological and experimental structure, broad taxa coverage and attention to train/test contamination, with a clear evaluation.
q1gu1Lfrx0.main_concern: Reproducibility and baseline strength: code, author-trained backbones and processed data are not yet released, some normalization details are unspecified, and stronger baselines are needed.

1k4XiMcBeW.one_liner: MathAtlas is an autoformalization benchmark of 49,756 graduate-textbook entities with a dependency graph of about 167,000 relations.
1k4XiMcBeW.problem: Autoformalization benchmarks focus on olympiad or undergraduate mathematics, leaving graduate and research-level mathematics understudied.
1k4XiMcBeW.method: Extracts theorems, definitions, exercises, examples and proofs from 100 graduate textbooks with a mathematical dependency graph, evaluates single-pass, feedback-aware loop and agentic systems, and releases MA-Hard, a split of 698 entities with deep dependency depth.
1k4XiMcBeW.key_idea: Annotate each formalization target with its dependency graph so systems can be evaluated, and built to be dependency-aware, with performance tracked against dependency depth.
1k4XiMcBeW.evidence: Experiments with single-pass, feedback-aware loop and frontier agentic systems, judged by compilation and semantic faithfulness (an LLM judge with 77+% balanced accuracy on 200 samples per a reviewer).
1k4XiMcBeW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a valuable large-scale benchmark with broad textbook coverage, added dependency information, and an informative separation of compilation from semantic faithfulness.
1k4XiMcBeW.main_concern: The headline correctness scores are weakly validated: the faithfulness judge is checked on only 200 compiling outputs from one generator with no expert audit, and reference matching depends on a retrieval model's top-10 candidates.

fOAVk5j4BH.one_liner: RPSFT anchors the top-k singular-vector product block of pretrained weights during SFT to limit subspace rotation and OOD forgetting.
fOAVk5j4BH.problem: SFT improves in-domain performance but degrades out-of-domain generalization, linked to changes in dominant singular subspaces, and finding loss-sensitive subspaces with full Hessian or Fisher information is too costly at LLM scale.
fOAVk5j4BH.method: Adds a block-level regularizer that anchors the dominant top-k product block in the pretrained SVD basis, motivated by the concentration of empirical-Fisher gradient energy in leading pretrained coordinates, while keeping full-parameter training.
fOAVk5j4BH.key_idea: Penalize changes to the top-k block of the pretrained SVD product so dominant singular subspaces rotate less during fine-tuning.
fOAVk5j4BH.evidence: SFT on math and non-math adaptation across model families and sizes (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B and 3B-Instruct, DeepSeek-7B per reviewers), against SFT baselines, ablations, and as an initialization for DAPO and GRPO.
fOAVk5j4BH.claimed_gains: Improves the in-domain/OOD trade-off over standard SFT and strong SFT baselines and gives stronger initializations for downstream RL fine-tuning; no numbers stated.
fOAVk5j4BH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and technically reasonable with modest overhead, and is supported by experiments across model families and ablations.
fOAVk5j4BH.main_concern: The link between the regularizer and actual subspace rotation is weakly justified (cross-subspace updates are unconstrained), and gains over standard SFT are sometimes modest.

tPN4SMjnkU.one_liner: A learned selector picks each agent's communication radius per state in decentralized multi-agent pathfinding.
tPN4SMjnkU.problem: Fixed-range communication in learned decentralized MAPF may exclude relevant agents when coordination is needed or add redundant exchanges when local information suffices.
tPN4SMjnkU.method: Learns to adjust each agent's communication neighborhood from its local state; per reviewers, it selects among Manhattan radii of 3, 5 and 7 using offline-generated labels and plugs into three planners (MAGAT, HMAGAT, LC-MAPF).
tPN4SMjnkU.key_idea: Treat communication range as a state-dependent decision per agent and timestep, learned from local state, to build a differentiated communication topology.
tPN4SMjnkU.evidence: Three planners with distinct communication architectures across six map families and 21 map-population configurations.
tPN4SMjnkU.claimed_gains: Configuration-averaged success-rate improvement reaches approximately 13 percentage points across the evaluated planners, with reduced communication and overall runtime.
tPN4SMjnkU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is clear and relevant and that adapting communication scope gives substantial success-rate gains with less communication across three backbones.
tPN4SMjnkU.main_concern: The method is incremental and limited to three discrete radii, and comparisons mostly use default fixed ranges, so the gain over a tuned fixed range is unclear (21.9 versus 2.3 points on DM-192).

k8SHhDKBoF.one_liner: AppSci-Bench measures how well LLMs build and improve business agents across seven domains, including requirement elicitation and internal evaluation.
k8SHhDKBoF.problem: Many benchmarks assess LLM-powered agents, but few assess how good LLMs are at building them the way applied scientists do for businesses.
k8SHhDKBoF.method: Simulates an applied-scientist workflow: elicit requirements from stakeholders, explore the infrastructure, and improve the target agent by designing experiments and internal benchmarks, with held-out evaluation suites in seven domains (five new, two recast from tau^3-bench).
k8SHhDKBoF.key_idea: Score LLMs as agent builders on held-out task suites, with process-level checks on requirement elicitation and on whether their own internal evaluations are representative.
k8SHhDKBoF.evidence: Seven frontier models across seven domains, with 3 build attempts per model and task.
k8SHhDKBoF.claimed_gains: The best model, Claude Opus 5.0, reaches a mean-minimum score of 59.1% across 3 build attempts; requirement elicitation reaches only 64%, and models saturate their own evaluation 65% of the time but fail the held-out task.
k8SHhDKBoF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating LLMs as agent builders, including requirement elicitation and self-evaluation, is a meaningful and timely target and the paper is clear.
k8SHhDKBoF.main_concern: Agent-building ability is confounded with harness compatibility and token budget (the 59.1% result used roughly 2 to 5 times more tokens), and results rest on few builds and trials with no confidence intervals.

yz0fwcjvp9.one_liner: E1 estimates a model's optimized energy from unoptimized PyTorch by searching tiling and fusion schedules on an abstract accelerator.
yz0fwcjvp9.problem: Trustworthy energy numbers need an optimized implementation that arrives long after the architecture is fixed, and only for ideas well-resourced teams choose to engineer, so models are compared on accuracy alone.
yz0fwcjvp9.method: Lowers a PyTorch model to a graph of einsums, searches tiling and fusion schedules on an abstract accelerator with a finite on-chip buffer, and sums the energy of arithmetic operations and off-chip data movement.
yz0fwcjvp9.key_idea: Sum arithmetic and off-chip data-movement energy of the best tiling and fusion schedule for the einsum graph on an abstract buffered accelerator, approximating an ideally optimized implementation.
yz0fwcjvp9.evidence: Validated against energy measured on NVIDIA H100 GPUs for individual kernels, production LLM-serving kernels across implementations and two years of development, and full model forward passes.
yz0fwcjvp9.claimed_gains: E1 tracks measured energy over three orders of magnitude; optimized implementations land 1.9-6x above it and eager PyTorch about an order of magnitude higher; E1 does not move when two MoE implementations differ by 8x in measured energy.
yz0fwcjvp9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating architectural energy potential from software maturity is a useful, systematic approach, supported by evidence on remaining headroom and implementation-invariance tests.
yz0fwcjvp9.main_concern: Validation is limited to H100 hardware (despite the infrastructure-agnostic claim) and a single short regime (batch size 1, 128-token prefill), with unclear guidance on how the metric would be used.

u3QZEZZWwN.one_liner: Population-based self-play with Policy-Space Response Oracles trains LLM attackers and defenders against the Nash equilibrium of opposing populations.
u3QZEZZWwN.problem: Single-policy self-play for LLM safety plateaus, as training against only the latest opponent makes policies cycle and collapse onto narrow strategies.
u3QZEZZWwN.method: Each generation initializes a new policy from the base model and trains it against the Nash equilibrium of the entire opposing population (PSRO). A racing evaluation budget and a rollout cache make population payoff matrices tractable at 8B parameters.
u3QZEZZWwN.key_idea: Train each new policy from the base model against the Nash equilibrium mixture of all past opponents, with racing evaluation and a rollout cache to keep payoff matrices cheap.
u3QZEZZWwN.evidence: Standard safety benchmarks with an 8B model (a single abliterated Llama-3.1-8B per reviewers), ablations on single opponents, uniform weighting and warm-starting, and comparison with self-play baselines.
u3QZEZZWwN.claimed_gains: The defender reaches 95.5% average safety versus at most 89.0% for baseline self-play methods, at a moderate helpfulness cost.
u3QZEZZWwN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it transfers a mature game-theoretic method cleanly to LLM safety, with controlled ablations and practical efficiency additions that justify keeping a population.
u3QZEZZWwN.main_concern: Main results come from single runs of one base model without seeds or variance, and comparisons beyond self-play variants are few, limiting evidence for generality.

JhI7SILF1n.one_liner: Characterizes the target law MeanFlow's adaptive loss weighting selects and proposes prediction weighting that preserves the conditional mean.
JhI7SILF1n.problem: Adaptive loss weighting in MeanFlow is used as a stabilizer, but it changes which conditional target law a one-step generative model learns, and similar FID can hide class-composition shifts.
JhI7SILF1n.method: Gives necessary and sufficient conditions on radial weights for the selected conditional law to have no greater total variance, studies population flows, and introduces a prediction weighting that removes target dependence while retaining adaptive scaling and the pointwise conditional mean.
JhI7SILF1n.key_idea: Weight the loss by the model's prediction instead of the regression target, so scaling stays adaptive while the pointwise conditional-mean target is preserved.
JhI7SILF1n.evidence: Population-flow experiments with convex regression and no neural fitting, plus image experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-LT showing class-proportion shifts.
JhI7SILF1n.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says prediction weighting better matches training class proportions in unconditional generation experiments).
JhI7SILF1n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnosis that adaptive weighting changes the learned target is clear and useful, supported by thorough theory and a population-flow experiment free of neural fitting.
JhI7SILF1n.main_concern: Image results do not isolate target selection from input weighting, and on ImageNet-LT prediction weighting underperforms adaptive weighting using a recipe not tuned for it, with few comparisons to other weighting schemes.

ElDLETb4Xn.one_liner: TopKLoRA activates only the k largest adapter latents per token, so fine-tuned backdoor circuits can be found and ablated.
ElDLETb4Xn.problem: Backdoors from poisoned fine-tuning data are hard to localize and remove, and parameter-efficient adapters capture the full parameter changes but are not easily interpretable.
ElDLETb4Xn.method: An interpretable-by-design LoRA variant in which only the top-k adapter latents are active per token, trained purely on downstream loss rather than as an SAE, then used to identify and ablate circuits in sleeper-agent backdoor model organisms.
ElDLETb4Xn.key_idea: Keep only the k largest LoRA adapter latents active per token, trained on downstream loss alone, so optimization pressure favors functionally causal latents.
ElDLETb4Xn.evidence: Sleeper-agent backdoor model organisms fine-tuned from gemma-2-2b, Qwen2.5-1.5B and Qwen2.5-7B, with necessity and sufficiency tests against a dense LoRA baseline.
ElDLETb4Xn.claimed_gains: Circuits necessary and sufficient for the backdoor are up to an order of magnitude smaller than a dense LoRA baseline, allowing surgical ablation without sacrificing instruction-following performance.
ElDLETb4Xn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the sparsity-to-localization claim is well tested across models and seeds with rank-matched dense LoRA controls, and that circuit ablation gives useful behavioral editing.
ElDLETb4Xn.main_concern: The backdoor is a simple, known-in-advance tag, sufficiency is checked on the same split used to select the circuit, and the evidence supports causal localization more than mechanistic explanation.

rCzR1nYYRV.one_liner: Explains larger models' ability to learn rare tasks through capacity competition among tasks and reduced gradient interference.
rCzR1nYYRV.problem: Larger models learn tasks that smaller models do not, and the cause of this phenomenon is unclear.
rCzR1nYYRV.method: A phenomenological power-law argument, a synthetic mixture-of-tasks study with monotonic scaling curves, and pretraining of OLMo models (4M to 4B parameters) on novel tasks of varying frequency and complexity.
rCzR1nYYRV.key_idea: Small models allocate neurons to frequent or simple tasks, while large models give common tasks enough capacity that their gradients weaken and stop overwriting rare-task features.
