rCzR1nYYRV.evidence: Synthetic task mixtures and OLMo models from 4M to 4B parameters pretrained on novel tasks, with results that mirror the synthetic experiments.
rCzR1nYYRV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the data-centric explanation is simple and intuitive, with testable predictions supported by both theory and experiments on large language models.
rCzR1nYYRV.main_concern: Capacity and optimization effects are not cleanly separated, and the setting is simple (orthogonal task blocks, frequency-only experiments), leaving forward transfer versus forgetting unresolved.

bkSEyFrT8D.one_liner: Jointly scales residual width, hidden width, and depth so residual networks reach an SDE limit with feature learning.
bkSEyFrT8D.problem: Existing depth-scaling approaches force a choice between locally maximal feature learning and feature diversity across residual-stream channels.
bkSEyFrT8D.method: Fixes the limiting ratio of residual width to hidden width times depth at a positive alpha, so hidden computation can be redistributed between width and depth. A correlated initialization called Half Copy partially relaxes the resulting shape constraints.
bkSEyFrT8D.key_idea: Hold residual width over (hidden width times depth) at a fixed positive ratio so training converges to an SDE limit with maximal feature learning; Half Copy initialization relaxes shape constraints.
bkSEyFrT8D.evidence: Theory plus residual-MLP experiments support convergence to the SDE limit at fixed positive alpha, and language-model experiments compare regrouped widths and depths at fixed parameter count.
bkSEyFrT8D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theory strong and the separation of residual width, hidden width, and depth a useful structural view, with systematic experiments across optimizers and model classes.
bkSEyFrT8D.main_concern: Experiments are small (Tiny Shakespeare, CIFAR, three seeds, one seed for Half Copy) and the benefit of the SDE regime over the ODE regime is not proven.

yxn7JDdGNq.one_liner: Composes learned energy factors and revises discrete structure via energy-guided edits and backtracking to solve larger hybrid problems.
yxn7JDdGNq.problem: End-to-end models struggle on problems harder than those seen in training, while compositional methods need the problem structure specified in advance.
yxn7JDdGNq.method: CSEM learns local energy factors from small training instances and, at test time, jointly solves for discrete structure and continuous values. It samples high-energy factors, applies syntax-valid graph edits, and backtracks locally.
yxn7JDdGNq.key_idea: Infer which learned energy factors to compose, then repair the composed structure with energy-guided graph edits and local backtracking at inference time.
yxn7JDdGNq.evidence: Evaluated on task-and-motion planning, 3D scene understanding, and reconstructing physical trajectories and contact modes from sparse observations, against learning-based baselines and search controls with matched evaluation budgets.
yxn7JDdGNq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a useful approach to joint discrete-continuous reasoning, with strong generalization to larger problems and search controls that help isolate the method's contribution.
yxn7JDdGNq.main_concern: The graph-edit step is under-explained in the main text, and comparisons with existing structure-searching planners do not clearly attribute gains to the energy-guided strategy.

1mmsBjYOlx.one_liner: Learns KV codebooks aligned to attention and continuation distributions, then allocates residual stages by measured continuation KL under a budget.
1mmsBjYOlx.problem: Reconstruction error alone does not capture how residual-codebook KV-cache compression affects predictions at high compression ratios.
1mmsBjYOlx.method: With the backbone frozen, it learns Key and Value codebooks by aligning attention maps, attention outputs, and continuation distributions with the dense model. It then scores each layer-component-depth choice by induced continuation KL and allocates residual stages under a global KV-payload budget, with packed-code attention at decoding.
1mmsBjYOlx.key_idea: Align codebook learning to the dense model's attention maps, outputs, and continuation distributions, and allocate residual stages using additive continuation-KL scores under a global budget.
1mmsBjYOlx.evidence: Three LLM backbones evaluated on LongBench, RULER-32K, and GSM8K, with ablations of alignment and allocation (on Mistral) and comparisons against CommVQ variants.
1mmsBjYOlx.claimed_gains: Near-BF16 performance on LongBench, RULER-32K, and GSM8K at approximately 8x historical-KV payload compression; at approximately 16x, LongBench and RULER-32K averages stay within 0.67 and 3.96 points of BF16.
1mmsBjYOlx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that aligning compression to attention and prediction effects rather than reconstruction error is well motivated, and that the ablations and efficient kernels support the method.
1mmsBjYOlx.main_concern: Gains are not cleanly attributed to the two stated contributions, since much of the improvement over CommVQ comes from representation changes, and ablations cover only Mistral.

Bu5ySXrhu1.one_liner: Softmax-free recurrent vision backbone using gated linear attention, alternating scan directions, and SwiGLU blocks, distilled from DINOv3.
Bu5ySXrhu1.problem: The quadratic cost of global softmax attention limits the efficiency of self-attention vision backbones for dense prediction as image resolution increases.
Bu5ySXrhu1.method: Combines gated linear attention, alternating spatial scan directions, and spatially enhanced SwiGLU blocks, distilled from a detection-specialized DINOv3 teacher by final-layer patch-token alignment through a linear projection with squared l2 loss. A chunkwise CUDA operator speeds up inference.
Bu5ySXrhu1.key_idea: Replace global softmax attention with gated linear recurrent token mixing over alternating spatial scan directions, trained by final-layer patch-token distillation from a DINOv3 teacher.
Bu5ySXrhu1.evidence: COCO detection with Objects365 pre-training, transfer to instance segmentation, pose estimation, oriented detection, semantic segmentation, and monocular depth, plus RTX4090 latency and TensorRT deployment on DRIVE AGX Thor.
Bu5ySXrhu1.claimed_gains: GTR-L reaches 58.9 box AP on COCO val2017 at 1.908 ms median batch-one latency on an RTX4090; the CUDA operator is 4.0x faster than FLA v0.5.0 at 1.6K tokens; Thor latency is 2.282-8.769 ms.
Bu5ySXrhu1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written and technically sound, with credible latency measurements, a custom CUDA kernel, edge deployment, and evaluation across six dense prediction tasks.
Bu5ySXrhu1.main_concern: Limited novelty: the design largely combines existing components (GLA, ViG-style directional scanning, ConvGLU-like blocks, plain feature distillation), and baseline comparisons are not fully matched.

2v6V5lZrPm.one_liner: Advantage-shaping rule for RLVR that redistributes credit by length-normalized response surprisal and prompt pass rate to preserve exploration.
2v6V5lZrPm.problem: Group-relative objectives give equal advantages to equally rewarded responses, so aggregate credit follows sampled mode frequency, which shapes which solutions remain accessible under repeated sampling.
2v6V5lZrPm.method: ExPPO applies bounded advantage shaping from prompt-relative, length-normalized response surprisal and prompt pass rate, with shared normalization that preserves verifier polarity and roughly keeps each group's total absolute advantage mass. It reuses rollout log-probabilities and plugs into GRPO and DAPO.
2v6V5lZrPm.key_idea: Reweight group-relative advantages by prompt-relative response surprisal and pass rate, bounded and normalized to preserve verifier polarity and total advantage mass.
2v6V5lZrPm.evidence: Experiments over multiple models (largest 7B) on in-domain and out-of-domain reasoning, a controlled multi-answer evaluation, and analysis of local conditions for entropy and correct-mode discovery gains.
2v6V5lZrPm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is lightweight, easy to integrate into GRPO and DAPO, well motivated, and evaluated on a reasonably broad set of models and ID/OOD tasks.
2v6V5lZrPm.main_concern: Novelty over existing rarity-aware credit assignment such as REPO-R is thin, and accuracy does not consistently lead (33.50 vs F-GRPO's 35.51 on Qwen2.5-7B).

q4Mo3KXGKn.one_liner: Evaluates sequentially evolving LLM memory with continual-learning metrics: online utility, hold-out generalization, backward transfer, forgetting, efficiency.
q4Mo3KXGKn.problem: Existing LLM-memory evaluations rely on aggregate metrics such as final hold-out accuracy or cumulative online performance, which can hide forgetting and negative transfer.
q4Mo3KXGKn.method: SeqMem-Eval targets a test-time setting where memory is external, prompt-mediated, and updated without changing model parameters. It tracks how memory states evolve, generalize, consolidate experience, and retain useful information during sequential inference.
q4Mo3KXGKn.key_idea: Borrow continual-learning measures such as backward transfer and forgetting to score each memory state along the task sequence instead of reporting only a final or cumulative accuracy.
q4Mo3KXGKn.evidence: Experiments across diverse tasks and memory methods, covering two backbones (Qwen3 and MiniMax), programming, mathematical and domain reasoning, API use, and ALFWorld, reporting both performance and cost.
q4Mo3KXGKn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that inspecting the full evolution of memory is more informative than a single final score, and that the protocol is broad across backbones and task types.
q4Mo3KXGKn.main_concern: The metrics are mostly standard continual-learning measures, and their validity is questionable because single stochastic generations per item can create apparent forgetting.

pnCPoYk6If.one_liner: Allocates finite measurement shots across damped Picard iterations of quantum deep equilibrium models by each iteration's terminal impact coefficient.
pnCPoYk6If.problem: Finite-shot measurements perturb the numerical information that equilibrium solvers use in QDEQs, and sampling fluctuations can obscure shrinking residual differences near equilibrium.
pnCPoYk6If.method: Characterizes the measurement precision needed to resolve Broyden secant differences, then for damped Picard inference uses a locally linearized propagation model (measurement covariance, readout, state dynamics) to give each iteration a terminal impact coefficient. Calibration-averaged coefficients yield a shared shot schedule that is optimized offline, spends the budget exactly, and is frozen at test time.
pnCPoYk6If.key_idea: Weight each Picard iteration's shot budget by its linearized terminal impact on output error, using a calibration-averaged schedule computed offline and frozen at test time.
pnCPoYk6If.evidence: Ideal finite-shot simulations on the original image classification benchmarks, with comparisons of dynamics-only and full-covariance schedules and of solver choice as the budget grows.
pnCPoYk6If.claimed_gains: The schedule reduces measurement-induced terminal squared error by 25.2%-33.9% relative to uniform allocation at equal budgets.
pnCPoYk6If.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem setup clear and the theory coherent, with a formal account of quasi-Newton solver failure under finite-shot noise and improvements on the original QDEQ benchmarks.
pnCPoYk6If.main_concern: All results come from idealized finite-shot simulations, the full-covariance schedule shows no gain over dynamics-only, and offline calibration needs exact classical simulation that will not scale to large circuits.

wUJG1fFu7w.one_liner: Trains flow policies by advantage-weighted flow matching on imagined world-model rollouts, avoiding likelihoods and backpropagation through sampling.
wUJG1fFu7w.problem: Generative control policies are hard to train with RL because likelihoods are expensive and backpropagating through the sampling chain is costly and unstable, while model-free on-policy RL is sample-inefficient, especially from pixels.
wUJG1fFu7w.method: MB-FPO regresses flow policies onto imagined actions weighted by their advantages, using a latent world model to generate on-policy data cheaply in imagination. It adds temporally correlated exploration noise.
wUJG1fFu7w.key_idea: Use a latent world model to generate abundant on-policy imagined data, so likelihood-free advantage-weighted flow matching can train the flow policy.
wUJG1fFu7w.evidence: DeepMind Control and Meta-World benchmarks including pixel-based tasks, compared with prior flow policy optimization methods, model-free baselines, and a model-based Gaussian policy trained on the same world model.
wUJG1fFu7w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, builds on established components, avoids likelihoods and sampling-chain backpropagation, and shows promising results against model-free flow policy methods.
wUJG1fFu7w.main_concern: The Gaussian-versus-flow comparison is confounded (policy class, exploration noise, and actor objective all differ), so gains cannot be attributed to flow expressiveness, and the contribution over prior model-based methods is unclear.

j6mvqpKtn1.one_liner: Selects preference comparisons to label by reducing posterior variance of a linearised decision loss, a c-optimal design for training verifiers.
j6mvqpKtn1.problem: Active learning for preference data reduces uncertainty in verifier parameters but ignores which parameter directions the deployed decision rule (best-of-K, reranking, escalation) actually uses.
j6mvqpKtn1.method: DFA is a c-optimal experimental design criterion that, given a small Decision Set with known utilities, picks the comparisons that most reduce the posterior variance of a linearised decision loss. It applies to any decision operator with a differentiable surrogate and is instantiated for best-of-K selection, top-m shortlisting, and accept-or-escalate cascades.
j6mvqpKtn1.key_idea: Score each candidate comparison by how much it lowers posterior variance along the gradient of a differentiable decision-loss surrogate, rather than overall parameter uncertainty.
j6mvqpKtn1.evidence: Four datasets spanning preference reranking, code generation, and tool-use, with analyses over label budgets and decision-set size, using a low-dimensional linear verifier on frozen LLM features.
j6mvqpKtn1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the decision-targeted c-optimal acquisition criterion is well motivated and mathematically justified, with improvements across four datasets and three decision rules.
j6mvqpKtn1.main_concern: The method needs a decision set with known utilities whose cost is not counted in label efficiency, baselines do not receive that information, and standard uncertainty baselines such as BALD are missing.

DMKq4YQxu5.one_liner: Ranks RNA 3D structure candidates with an SE(3)-invariant evaluator conditioned on a frozen RNA language model's attention maps.
DMKq4YQxu5.problem: Geometry alone can confirm a packing is physically plausible but not that it is the one the sequence adopts, which makes selecting among candidates a bottleneck for long RNAs.
DMKq4YQxu5.method: SIRGE conditions the geometry of every nucleotide pair on attention maps from a frozen RNA language model used as a sequence prior. A contact-recovery objective trains the pair representations to recognise native tertiary contacts.
DMKq4YQxu5.key_idea: Judge each candidate's helix packing against what the sequence implies, by conditioning pairwise SE(3)-invariant geometry on frozen RNA-LM attention maps and training with a contact-recovery objective.
DMKq4YQxu5.evidence: Compared with seven established evaluators under two distribution shifts (CLS-1 with held-out longer RNAs, and candidates from six unseen deep-learning predictors), with ablations of the prior and contact objective and an interpretability study.
DMKq4YQxu5.claimed_gains: On CLS-1, it improves Kendall-tau alignment by 58% over the strongest baseline, and on candidates from six unseen deep-learning predictors it almost doubles the strongest baseline's top-1 hit rate.
DMKq4YQxu5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the sequence-prior motivation is biologically grounded and that matched ablations show the prior and contact objective help, with SIRGE beating the baselines on both test sets.
DMKq4YQxu5.main_concern: Evidence for the role of alignment is thin: CLS-1 has only 21 RNAs and three seeds, the base architecture already beats baselines, and Gen-OOD selection is not compared with fixed-generator strategies.

TeGoGrSIbb.one_liner: Compares segmentation-model masks across training stages with human time-to-collision and change-detection responses to find when object representations match humans.
TeGoGrSIbb.problem: Humans seem to represent objects for physical reasoning with coarse approximations that partially fill concavities, whereas segmentation models are trained for pixel-accurate masks, so it is unclear whether and when their representations resemble human physical judgments.
TeGoGrSIbb.method: Builds a pipeline and alignment metric that turn model masks into predictions for the same time-to-collision and change-detection stimuli shown to 178 and 50 human participants. It evaluates four architecture families (DINOv2, SegFormer, DeepLabV3+, UPerNet) across sizes and training times.
TeGoGrSIbb.key_idea: Convert model masks into time-to-collision and change-detection predictions and measure agreement with the human concavity effect across training checkpoints.
TeGoGrSIbb.evidence: Human data from 178 and 50 participants, four architecture families with 16 configurations and multiple training seeds, and checkpoint selection evaluated on held-out participants.
TeGoGrSIbb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is a systematic, well-controlled behavioral alignment pipeline across architectures and training stages that uses modern vision models to probe human cognition.
TeGoGrSIbb.main_concern: The findings may reflect generic coarse-to-fine learning rather than anything specific to humans, and the resource-limits interpretation is not tested with an explicit resource trade-off.

mokIZh9xT6.one_liner: Aligns clients' private class taxonomies by constrained, revisable re-clustering of concept capsules in federated few-shot class-incremental learning.
mokIZh9xT6.problem: Federated few-shot class-incremental learning assumes a shared global label space, but when clients use private, partially overlapping taxonomies the server cannot tell which client classes denote the same concept from one to five samples.
mokIZh9xT6.method: FedTaxo encodes each local class as a feature-sharing concept capsule and grows a latent concept graph by re-clustering every novel capsule each session, under the constraint that two identifiers of one client are never one concept.
mokIZh9xT6.key_idea: Re-cluster all novel concept capsules every session with a within-client cannot-link constraint, so earlier assignments stay revisable instead of being fixed greedily.
mokIZh9xT6.evidence: A Taxonomy-Free FFSCIL benchmark built from real taxonomies with synonyms, homonyms, and superclass-level labels, controlled experiments on four datasets, and a minimax-rate result for a Gaussian surrogate.
mokIZh9xT6.claimed_gains: Re-clustering recovers 85% of an oracle's novel-class gain, against 69% when the same score is assigned greedily.
mokIZh9xT6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper formulates a meaningful, realistic extension of federated class-incremental learning beyond a shared label space, with a simple, well-specified method backed by theory.
mokIZh9xT6.main_concern: Evaluation relies on simulated client taxonomies, gains are modest in some settings (typically 0.7-1.2 points), and performance degrades when cannot-link or hierarchy assumptions are violated.

kUfubnK8uY.one_liner: Adds an Unlearning Capability Evaluator to quantum architecture search so selected circuits better support later data-removal requests.
kUfubnK8uY.problem: Existing quantum architecture search selects by predictive accuracy and ignores post-deployment unlearning needs, although architecture itself can substantially affect unlearning capability.
kUfubnK8uY.method: An Unlearning Capability Evaluator scores an architecture's unlearning capability using synthetic unlearning requests. UQAS-Select picks the best-scoring architecture from an existing pool, and UQAS-Design searches for one when no pool exists.
kUfubnK8uY.key_idea: Score candidate circuits by how well unlearning on synthetic removal requests matches retraining (TV distance), then rerank an accuracy-filtered pool or evolve designs by that score.
kUfubnK8uY.evidence: Simulation and IBM quantum computer experiments across sixteen scenarios spanning four datasets and four accuracy-based QAS methods, plus an empirical study showing architectures with comparable accuracy differ in unlearning capability.
kUfubnK8uY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unlearning capability is an overlooked, relevant factor in quantum architecture design, with broad experiments including four QAS baselines and real IBM hardware.
kUfubnK8uY.main_concern: The framework description is unclear and the novelty is mostly at the objective level, and TV distance alone does not verify that training-data information was removed.

p7JrtVxUGq.one_liner: Applies existing steering directions only over a short span starting at the final prompt token, often one token.
p7JrtVxUGq.problem: Activation steering usually intervenes throughout generation, and it is unclear whether a brief intervention can influence later computation the way prompting does while preserving model capabilities.
p7JrtVxUGq.method: Prefix Steering applies existing steering directions and operators over a short span beginning at the final prompt token, with no further intervention. Under fixed-state attention assumptions, the paper also gives sufficient conditions for single- and multi-token steering to match prompt-induced attention-head outputs.
p7JrtVxUGq.key_idea: Confine existing steering directions to a brief initial span, treating steering as initiating a behavior rather than continually enforcing it, and tune duration and strength for the control-capability trade-off.
p7JrtVxUGq.evidence: Four models and five tasks, including final-answer formatting after reasoning, compared with prompting and alternative steering-strength policies, plus attention-level theory.
p7JrtVxUGq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that short-span steering is a simple, useful design choice that keeps much of full steering's control while preserving more capability, and that the formatting-task test is informative.
p7JrtVxUGq.main_concern: Comparisons with alternative steering schedules depend on insufficiently documented tuning, and the attention-matching theory has unclear explanatory value for the practical method.

zeBo7Z6VRz.one_liner: Fixed-point neural sampler for discrete unnormalized distributions trained on Gibbs soft labels, extending to transport between arbitrary distributions.
zeBo7Z6VRz.problem: Existing discrete neural samplers are prone to mode collapse, lack convergence guarantees when trained by fixed-point iteration, and are often tied to a specific reference process such as masked or uniform diffusion.
zeBo7Z6VRz.method: DIG-IN trains a generative model from density evaluations alone, using fixed-point iterations with Gibbs soft labels. Besides masked diffusion, the framework extends to transport between arbitrary distributions.
zeBo7Z6VRz.key_idea: Supervise the sampler with Gibbs-conditional soft labels computed from the unnormalized density inside a fixed-point iteration, which reduces per-site variance and keeps the target as a fixed point.
zeBo7Z6VRz.evidence: Ising and Potts models, an amortized sampler over thermodynamic conditions, alloy phase diagrams, biomolecular Boltzmann distributions, and solvation and conformational free energy estimation, with controls for Gibbs labels and importance weighting.
zeBo7Z6VRz.claimed_gains: Mitigates mode collapse on Ising and Potts models and learns a single amortized sampler over thermodynamic conditions on lattices of up to 2,500 sites.
zeBo7Z6VRz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Gibbs-supervision construction is principled, with variance-reduction and consistency results, and that it outperforms recent baselines in controlled lattice experiments.
zeBo7Z6VRz.main_concern: The paper lacks a detailed main-text comparison with MDNS and PDNS, which share its fixed-point iteration and weighted loss, and mode collapse is not analyzed rigorously on small lattices.

0GNVXa2YUA.one_liner: Trains three multi-agent LLM workflows with GRPO under shared versus per-role policies to isolate where multi-agent RL gains come from.
0GNVXa2YUA.problem: The payoff of outcome-reward RL on multi-agent LLM workflows is hard to predict because the reward does not credit individual roles and a shared policy trades pooled data against specialization.
0GNVXa2YUA.method: Trains three workflows (Eval-Opt, Voting, Orch-Workers) with GRPO on math and code at three Qwen3 scales, with one policy shared by all roles (SP) or one per role type (IP). It then analyzes role-level outputs, gradients, and training stability.
0GNVXa2YUA.key_idea: Separate solver quality from workflow structure by comparing with single-agent RL, then diagnose shared versus per-role policies via token-averaged loss gradient share and post-peak instability of a single role.
0GNVXa2YUA.evidence: Three workflows trained on math and code at three Qwen3 scales, compared with untrained workflows, single-agent RL, and three-sample single-agent voting, with role-level analysis and control experiments.
0GNVXa2YUA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the role-level analyses and comparators such as single-agent RL and multi-sample voting clarify where workflow gains come from and give valuable diagnoses of policy-sharing tradeoffs.
0GNVXa2YUA.main_concern: The scope is narrow (three fixed workflows, math and code, small Qwen3 models, one training seed per setting) and the causal explanations lack targeted controls.

vhVUssaO4u.one_liner: A benchmark of 718 clinician-authored crisis conversations scored by weighted clinician rubrics across seven dimensions of crisis support.
vhVUssaO4u.problem: Existing safety benchmarks score models mainly on refusal, but for suicide and self-harm disclosures the needed behavior is a substantive supportive response.
vhVUssaO4u.method: DistressBench has 718 English conversations with clinician-authored user turns spanning 23 SSH subcategories, each paired with a task-specific rubric of weighted atomic criteria across seven dimensions and a clinician reference response. A model's score is the share of scenario-weighted criteria its reply satisfies.
vhVUssaO4u.key_idea: Score replies against clinician-written, scenario-weighted atomic criteria instead of refusal, which exposes a gap between recognizing a crisis and taking resource actions.
vhVUssaO4u.evidence: 25 frontier models evaluated with three independent runs each, LLM judges calibrated against independent clinician annotations, and dimension-level analyses.
vhVUssaO4u.claimed_gains: The best model satisfies 88.4% of weighted criteria and the median model 71.4%, against 98.7% for clinician references; in 35.3% of conversations where a model met every recognition criterion, it missed at least one resource action.
vhVUssaO4u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark evaluates concrete, clinician-validated crisis-support behaviors beyond refusal, with broad coverage of 25 models, uncertainty estimates, and judge calibration.
vhVUssaO4u.main_concern: Score interpretation outruns the measurement: higher rubric scores may not mean better clinical support (they may favor longer replies, score only the final turn, and overstate the recognition-action gap).

n057WRwQxp.one_liner: Self-speculative decoding with an any-order image model drafting and verifying tokens at widely spaced positions, sampling the exact distribution.
n057WRwQxp.problem: Autoregressive image models generate one token per forward pass, and in left-to-right self-speculative decoding adjacent drafted positions are strongly dependent, leaving large drafter-target disagreement.
n057WRwQxp.method: DSD uses an any-order model as its own drafter and verifier along an order whose consecutive positions are far apart. It requires no additional training and samples from the exact target model's distribution.
n057WRwQxp.key_idea: Order generation so consecutively drafted positions are far apart, since drafter-target disagreement shrinks with distance between draft tokens, and use the any-order model as its own drafter.
n057WRwQxp.evidence: Three families of any-order image models on class-conditional ImageNet at 256 or 1,024 tokens, with ablations running existing self-speculative samplers along the dispersed order.
n057WRwQxp.claimed_gains: Samples the exact distribution with 10-12x fewer forward passes than sequential decoding on three families of any-order image models (TL;DR: up to 11.7x).
n057WRwQxp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and well motivated by a diagnostic of drafter-target disagreement, and that the ablation isolating order from sampler shows the gain comes from the dispersed order.
n057WRwQxp.main_concern: Scope is narrow: it applies only to any-order autoregressive models and is tested only on class-conditional ImageNet, with a single long-sequence model.

mlIb0gn3DJ.one_liner: Estimates teacher reliability and response-selection probabilities from coherence of student gradients over a teacher-prompt bipartite graph, without external judges.
mlIb0gn3DJ.problem: In multi-teacher distillation, teacher responses vary in quality and suitability, and existing student-based selectors rely on familiarity (token probabilities), which does not indicate learning benefit, or on gradients that need extra backward passes.
mlIb0gn3DJ.method: SURE measures coherence among student gradients from different teachers' responses to the same prompt without backpropagating through the frozen student. It models this evidence over a teacher-prompt bipartite graph to iteratively refine teacher reliability and response-selection probabilities.
mlIb0gn3DJ.key_idea: Treat agreement among final-hidden-state student gradients of different teachers' responses as evidence, and propagate it on a teacher-prompt bipartite graph to jointly refine reliability and selection probabilities.
mlIb0gn3DJ.evidence: Fine-tuning four pretrained students from two model families, evaluated on instruction-following benchmarks including IFEval and length-controlled AlpacaEval, with ablations of teacher centering and reliability estimation and a runtime analysis.
mlIb0gn3DJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining prompt-level coherence with cross-prompt teacher reliability is a practical design that yields consistent downstream gains, especially in instruction following, with small overhead over forward-only selectors.
mlIb0gn3DJ.main_concern: Ablations and baselines are incomplete (no test of the learned teacher prior alone, no comparison with gradient-based selectors such as GRACE, a single fine-tuning seed), so the source of the gains is unclear.

7snyG2MgiV.one_liner: Causal interventions on Llama 3.1 405B Instruct show two independent mechanisms, proactive and retroactive, for in-context compositional inference.
7snyG2MgiV.problem: It is unclear how language models combine new in-context relations, such as 'Tom's father is Steve' and 'Jim's father is Tom', into unstated inferences like 'Jim's grandfather is Steve'.
7snyG2MgiV.method: Applies causal interventions to Llama 3.1 405B Instruct to separate a proactive mechanism that generalizes as soon as information appears in context from a retroactive one that reasons only when needed to predict the next token. It then tests when the model uses the proactive mechanism and what depth it supports.
7snyG2MgiV.key_idea: Causal interventions separate a proactive mechanism that composes relations as soon as they appear in context from a retroactive one that composes them only when needed for the next token.
7snyG2MgiV.evidence: Causal interventions on Llama 3.1 405B Instruct with synthetic relational prompts, plus 70B and 8B results where the proactive mechanism is less pronounced.
7snyG2MgiV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the causal-intervention design is careful and gives stronger mechanistic evidence than correlational analyses for two distinct compositional-inference mechanisms.
7snyG2MgiV.main_concern: Generality is limited: the main findings rest on one 405B model and tightly controlled synthetic templates, and the explanation of why two mechanisms exist rests on thin evidence.

LJWHVaj90d.one_liner: Separates graded pairwise relation preservation (Local representation) from cluster formation (Global representation), using relative grade ordering for supervision.
LJWHVaj90d.problem: Pairwise constrained clustering usually uses binary supervision, whereas graded relations can mean weak evidence, mixed membership, or coarse-level agreement, and the same intermediate grade can imply different cluster structures.
LJWHVaj90d.method: Graded DualPair (GDP) separates roles across Local and Global representations, coordinating their pairwise relations while using relative grade ordering for direct Global supervision. GDP-Hier extends this across prescribed hierarchy resolutions.
LJWHVaj90d.key_idea: Preserve graded relations in a Local representation and form explicit clusters in a Global one, supervised by relative grade ordering rather than calibrated co-membership probabilities.
LJWHVaj90d.evidence: Theory giving sufficient conditions for multi-resolution hierarchy recovery, plus experiments on diverse image and text benchmarks with recalibration tests and component ablations.
LJWHVaj90d.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating relation preservation from partition formation is well motivated, and that the evaluation is extensive across supervision semantics, datasets, recalibration tests, and ablations.
LJWHVaj90d.main_concern: Representation dimensions are not matched across methods, and one ablation shows an unexplained gap between two runs of the same nominal configuration.

J6n03E7oYK.one_liner: Training-free test-time framework that probes which action a reasoning model would take next and stops reasoning only when probes agree.
J6n03E7oYK.problem: Agentic reasoning models deliberate at length before acting, and efficiency-oriented early stopping can end reasoning before a necessary tool call, causing severe performance degradation.
J6n03E7oYK.method: OPERA uses hierarchical action probing to assess whether the model is ready to take the next action, and identifies potential verbosity on the fly to estimate when to probe. It terminates reasoning only when probes consistently support the same action.
J6n03E7oYK.key_idea: Probe the model's next action (tool call versus answer, then content) at adaptively timed points, and stop deliberation only when probes agree on the same action.
J6n03E7oYK.evidence: Knowledge-intensive benchmarks such as NQ with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, compared with baselines including Dynasor-Agentic and REFRAIN, with component ablations.
J6n03E7oYK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that action-aware early stopping is a practical, training-free idea that reduces token use on knowledge-intensive tasks while addressing premature stopping before tool calls.
J6n03E7oYK.main_concern: Advantages over simpler alternatives and over REFRAIN are unclear, with small average EM gains and accuracy drops on some benchmarks.

szce9zSCPS.one_liner: Proposes algorithm-agnostic design patterns that prevent hyperparameter collusion between exploration, policy improvement, and optimization components of deep RL.
szce9zSCPS.problem: Asynchronous interactions between exploration, policy improvement, and network optimization drive sensitivity and instability in deep RL, with known vulnerabilities arising when a sub-optimal choice in one component masks inadequacies in another.
szce9zSCPS.method: Draws an analogy to concurrent software systems and proposes algorithm-agnostic design patterns that ensure the correctness of each RL component. The patterns are applied as a combined recipe to PPO and SAC.
szce9zSCPS.key_idea: Treat RL components as concurrent processes and fix each so that no hyperparameter must compensate for a defect in another, removing hyperparameter collusion.
szce9zSCPS.evidence: PPO and SAC agents on continuous-control environments (Brax), with cumulative ablations of the recipe components.
szce9zSCPS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clear, that hyperparameter collusion is a useful concept, and that the recipe improves PPO and SAC with cumulative ablations supporting its components.
szce9zSCPS.main_concern: Concepts such as side effects and hyperparameter collusion lack quantitative definitions, and the recipe changes many factors at once, which blurs attribution.

7YNtn4Tlbj.one_liner: Minimax-optimal RL for a leader facing myopic quantal-response followers, analyzed under state-only versus marginal observation of the population.
7YNtn4Tlbj.problem: A leader in a Stackelberg mean-field game must learn a commitment policy against a large boundedly rational population while observing only the state distribution, and possibly the action marginal but not the state-action correspondence.
7YNtn4Tlbj.method: Develops an optimistic RL algorithm with linear function approximation that evaluates candidate follower responses using observed leader rewards and transitions. It proves a matching lower bound under state observation (SO) and compares with marginal observation (MO).
7YNtn4Tlbj.key_idea: Optimistically evaluate candidate follower responses from observed leader rewards and transitions, with regret governed by an effective dimension d_SO = min{d_F, A-1, X(B-1)}.
7YNtn4Tlbj.evidence: Theoretical analysis: a minimax regret rate under state observation with a matching lower bound, plus a characterization of when marginal observation helps.
7YNtn4Tlbj.claimed_gains: Under state observation the minimax regret is Theta-tilde(T^((d_SO+1)/(d_SO+2))) over T episodes for fixed structural parameters, with d_SO = min{d_F, A-1, X(B-1)}.
7YNtn4Tlbj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives a tight, rigorous minimax characterization whose effective-dimension formula shows how the learning bottleneck shifts, and that the SO versus MO distinction is meaningful.
7YNtn4Tlbj.main_concern: The setting is narrow (finite-dimensional linear, fully myopic, boundedly rational followers) and the algorithm's computational practicality is not shown.

sUzaZTsvLQ.one_liner: Ties low-frequency RoPE pairs into isofrequency groups so cross-pair rotations commute with RoPE and fold into Q/K weights.
sUzaZTsvLQ.problem: Post-RoPE per-token low-bit KV-cache quantization is sensitive to large activations, and general cross-pair rotations that reduce outliers do not commute with RoPE and cannot be folded into Q/K projection weights.
sUzaZTsvLQ.method: Isofrequency Commutant Expansion selectively ties nearby low-frequency RoPE pairs, enlarging the exact RoPE-commuting transformation space from pair-wise to cross-pair rotations. ROKI uses this space to redistribute Q/K activations and applies transformation-aware mixed-precision key quantization, with all transformations optimized offline.
sUzaZTsvLQ.key_idea: Tie nearby low-frequency RoPE pairs so cross-pair rotations commute exactly with RoPE, letting outlier-redistributing rotations fold offline into Q/K weights, with importance-aware mixed-precision keys.
sUzaZTsvLQ.evidence: LongBench-E on three Llama/Qwen models at an average 3-bit KV-cache budget against quantized baselines, plus decode speed measured against low-bit baselines.
sUzaZTsvLQ.claimed_gains: At an average 3-bit KV-cache budget, ROKI has the highest average LongBench-E score among evaluated quantized baselines on three Llama/Qwen models while staying close to FP16, with up to 4.27x decode speedup over the evaluated low-bit baselines.
sUzaZTsvLQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that expanding the RoPE-commuting transformation space by tying frequencies is a new, well-motivated idea that avoids separate online transformation kernels.
sUzaZTsvLQ.main_concern: Efficiency evidence is limited (decode latency on one model and GPU at batch size 1, no calibration time reported), and weight folding for Qwen3 and long-context validation need clarification.

EbihLCFzfD.one_liner: Forecasts sustained persona drift before generation by comparing hidden states with a learned stable-behavior reference plus recent state history.
EbihLCFzfD.problem: Detecting persona drift after a response is generated leaves no chance to inspect the risk first, and a changed answer is not evidence of drift when new task information justifies it.
EbihLCFzfD.method: Learns the internal state expected when the persona is maintained under the current dialogue and task conditions, with its normal variation. It combines deviations from this reference with recent state history and available dialogue to predict future drift, followed by a rule-based alarm.
EbihLCFzfD.key_idea: Model the internal state expected under a maintained persona and forecast drift from deviations from that reference plus state history, keeping justified updates separate from violations.
EbihLCFzfD.evidence: Experiments on three sizes of Qwen2.5-Instruct and Gemma-3-4B-it against text and raw-state baselines, under a one-turn-advance warning requirement, with checks under a separate behavioral assessment and changes in dialogue order and wording.
EbihLCFzfD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the task is carefully specified, separating justified updates from persona violations, which allows testing forecasting without penalizing legitimate adaptation.
EbihLCFzfD.main_concern: The pipeline is complex with many design choices, and the improvement over the strongest nonlinear baselines appears modest and incompletely established.

1PjReQCtIa.one_liner: Proves finite energy-probe features, computable by a fixed-weight GNN, let combinatorial optimization values transfer to larger bounded-degree graphs.
1PjReQCtIa.problem: GNNs are trained on small graphs and deployed on larger ones, and it is unclear which graph information must be preserved for combinatorial optimization values to transfer across sizes.
1PjReQCtIa.method: Establishes size-transfer guarantees for normalized graph optimization values using finite collections of energy features, where task-value differences for affine objectives are controlled by discrepancies in normalized scalar energy probes. For general Lipschitz objectives an extra representation error appears that vanishes on hyperfinite families but not on expanders, and the features are realized with a fixed-weight GNN.
1PjReQCtIa.key_idea: Bound transfer error by discrepancies in normalized ground-state energy probes via Shapley-Folkman bounds, so a size-independent finite energy representation suffices for affine tasks and, on hyperfinite families, Lipschitz tasks.
1PjReQCtIa.evidence: Theory with Shapley-Folkman bounds including a dimension-free l2 regime, prediction guarantees and statistical generalization bounds, plus experiments using exact energy probes from dynamic programs followed by ridge regression.
1PjReQCtIa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the research question is well posed and that the affine-versus-Lipschitz distinction, with an expander counterexample and sharpness examples, clarifies what energy probes preserve.
1PjReQCtIa.main_concern: A gap remains between theory and practice: guarantees for learned predictors are conditional, and experiments use exact dynamic-programming probes rather than the constructed GNN encoder.

bJqdLHRD6b.one_liner: Finds a linear difference-in-means direction in LLM activations that mediates whether a model attempts to interpret corrupted prompts.
bJqdLHRD6b.problem: Sufficiently corrupted prompts can make models stop attempting to interpret the user's intent, and it is unclear whether this behavior is linearly represented in activation space.
bJqdLHRD6b.method: Builds a contrastive dataset by corrupting questions until models switch from interpretation to non-interpretation, extracts candidate directions via difference-in-means, and selects one by its behavioral effect during steering.
bJqdLHRD6b.key_idea: Take the difference of mean activations between interpreted and non-interpreted corrupted prompts, select the direction by steering effect, and project it out of or add it to the residual stream.
bJqdLHRD6b.evidence: Nine instruction-tuned models from three families on held-out corrupted TriviaQA, with transfer to SimpleQA, word-level omission and OCR corruptions, six utility benchmarks, and comparisons with random, refusal, and unrelated directions.
bJqdLHRD6b.claimed_gains: Projecting the direction out increases attempted interpretation by 39 to 70 percentage points on held-out corrupted TriviaQA questions across nine models, while six utility benchmarks change by a mean absolute 0.74 percentage points.
bJqdLHRD6b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the empirical evidence is consistent across nine models and corruption settings, with strong baselines (random, refusal, unrelated directions) and preserved general capabilities.
bJqdLHRD6b.main_concern: The claim of separability from the refusal direction is overstated given overlap in the results, and the gain in attempted interpretation far exceeds the gain in correct reconstruction or answers.

n9BD1pFKkk.one_liner: 12K-pair real-image editing benchmark scored by Active Elo, routing close comparisons to experts and clear ones to a VLM judge.
n9BD1pFKkk.problem: Existing instruction-guided image editing benchmarks give uneven coverage of the diverse real-image tasks in professional workflows, and evaluating at scale needs selective expert supervision.
n9BD1pFKkk.method: CV-Arena has 12K high-resolution real-image instruction pairs across 16 task types, built with CogRetriever, a retrieval-and-curation pipeline. Active Elo uses CV-Judge, a logic-gated multi-dimensional VLM evaluator, to resolve clear comparisons, routes close ones to expert raters, and aggregates both with reliability-weighted Elo updates.
n9BD1pFKkk.key_idea: Let a logic-gated VLM judge settle clear pairwise comparisons and send only close, high-quality comparisons to human experts, aggregating both with reliability-weighted Elo updates.
n9BD1pFKkk.evidence: Evaluation of 21 image-editing systems, a budget-matched routing study against human-only and judge-only protocols, and a proposed CV-Agent baseline evaluated on the benchmark.
n9BD1pFKkk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark fills a gap with real, high-resolution professional editing tasks, and that routing close comparisons to humans is a practical use of limited annotation budget.
n9BD1pFKkk.main_concern: Rankings change sharply across evaluation protocols (the authors' CV-Agent is first under Active Elo but fifth under human-only), raising evaluator-bias doubts, and dataset and instruction construction details are thin.

U9WMEU4Zac.one_liner: Audits the Jacobian lens's workspace-band signatures and occupancy estimator across open-weight model families.
U9WMEU4Zac.problem: Claims of a mid-depth verbalizable workspace band at roughly 38% of depth rest on an instrument whose measurements have not been validated.
U9WMEU4Zac.method: They test five measurements (four band signatures and one occupancy estimator) with planted-direction tests, fit-corpus changes, and centering controls across seven families and 22 screened model-lens artifacts.
U9WMEU4Zac.key_idea: Validate each J-lens measurement with planted-direction gates and corpus and unembedding-centering controls before using it to locate a band.
U9WMEU4Zac.evidence: Planted-count tests (25 versus 40 directions), fit-corpus sensitivity, centering controls, a causal patching probe on one model, and effective-dimensionality onsets across seven families and 22 model-lens artifacts.
U9WMEU4Zac.claimed_gains: The surviving J-lens effective-dimensionality transition has an onset ranging from 28.6% to 78.7% of depth across seven families, and excess kurtosis changes sign between two fits of one model.
U9WMEU4Zac.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the planted-count tests, corpus-sensitivity analysis, and centering controls identify concrete measurement dependencies and separate supported from unsupported conclusions.
U9WMEU4Zac.main_concern: The surviving effective-dimensionality onset is a spectral property of the lens rather than of what the model represents, and the functional evidence is narrow, leaving the positive meaning of the measure limited.

CwOUM2ZHcN.one_liner: Derives and fits a scaling law for reward optimization jointly in preference-data size M and KL budget K.
CwOUM2ZHcN.problem: Existing research does not cleanly identify how performance jointly scales with the amount of preference data used to train the proxy reward model and the policy's divergence budget.
CwOUM2ZHcN.method: An information-theoretic model proves an upper bound on performance that a constructive procedure tightly achieves, and experiments use a 70B gold reward model to generate feedback and proxy reward models trained from 0.6B to 4B models.
CwOUM2ZHcN.key_idea: Model optimization as choosing among i.i.d. Gaussian rewards inferred from noisy comparisons, giving performance of order sqrt(min{log M, K}).
CwOUM2ZHcN.evidence: An information-theoretic upper bound with a constructive achievability proof, and controlled experiments with a 70B gold reward model and proxy reward models from 0.6B to 4B parameters.
CwOUM2ZHcN.claimed_gains: Performance scales roughly as Theta(sqrt(min{log(M), K})), and the fitted law has R^2 from 94.7% up to a value cut off in the available abstract.
CwOUM2ZHcN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is useful and the theory is clean, with carefully controlled experiments using a shared comparison stream, initialization, and evaluation pools.
CwOUM2ZHcN.main_concern: The theory does not explain the experiments: rewards are modeled i.i.d. across responses so the predicted gain on unseen responses is zero, while the observed gain must come from reward-model generalization.

rbj566AWUq.one_liner: Shows in a toy superposition model that increasing width drives a continuous partial-to-full representation phase transition.
rbj566AWUq.problem: It is poorly understood how model width and data statistics set the configuration of representation vectors and the loss when the number of features and the width are both large.
rbj566AWUq.method: They study Anthropic's toy model of superposition and derive a partial random projection approximation that predicts the critical width, then check the predictions experimentally.
rbj566AWUq.key_idea: A partial random projection approximation shows only a subset of features gets representation vectors below a critical width that grows linearly with active features.
rbj566AWUq.evidence: Theory plus experiments in Anthropic's toy model of superposition; a reviewer notes the experiments use a single feature count (n = 10,000).
rbj566AWUq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the partial-representation phase sharp and stable across seeds and the toy model relevant to regimes where features outnumber hidden dimensions.
rbj566AWUq.main_concern: The transition and the critical-width scaling are tested at a single feature count (n = 10,000), and the analytic derivation relies on an assumption that fails near the transition.

bDUxsUR8MG.one_liner: Appends a shared-operator cascade across scales to existing networks so fine scales are predicted from coarse ones via self-similarity.
bDUxsUR8MG.problem: Neural networks for natural signals learn coarse scales but blur or miss fine scales, causing missing detail and rollout drift.
bDUxsUR8MG.method: They formalize self-similarity as a recurrence with a shared operator across scales, prove when it can be parameterized with parameter count independent of the number of fine scales, and build self-similar cascade decoders as small add-on modules. The instantiations are a Fourier version (S3C) and a wavelet version (S2WC).
bDUxsUR8MG.key_idea: Predict each finer scale from the coarser one with a single shared operator, giving a parameter count independent of the number of fine scales.
bDUxsUR8MG.evidence: Turbulent Navier-Stokes forecasting across backbones, resolutions, and time horizons (S3C) and deterministic image super-resolution against strong baselines (S2WC).
bDUxsUR8MG.claimed_gains: S3C improves turbulent Navier-Stokes forecasting by up to 54% across backbones, resolutions, and time horizons while contributing 0.1% of total parameters.
bDUxsUR8MG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation meaningful and the compact cross-scale module practically useful across several backbones and rollout horizons, with a coherent formulation linking Fourier, wavelet, and transposed-convolution views.
bDUxsUR8MG.main_concern: The implementation departs from the theory (S3C keeps backbone phases and interpolates amplitudes), and experiments neither isolate the dilation-based design nor compare against other spectral-bias remedies.

9XFlJl0lZc.one_liner: Trains tool-using vision-language agents with RL to write weather forecast reports, rewarded by a rubric plus claim entailment.
9XFlJl0lZc.problem: RL is hard when outputs, like natural-language weather forecast reports, have many valid answers and cannot be checked against a known ground truth.
9XFlJl0lZc.method: Zephyrus-R1 optimizes a reward that combines a meteorological rubric with bidirectional claim entailment against National Weather Service reference reports, in a simulated tool-calling environment with curriculum learning. Agents gather and analyze forecast evidence across regions and lead times before writing a report.
9XFlJl0lZc.key_idea: Reward reports with a meteorological rubric plus bidirectional claim entailment against NWS reference reports, and train tool-using agents with curriculum RL.
9XFlJl0lZc.evidence: A simulated tool-calling weather environment scored against NWS reference reports, with annotations from four meteorologists used to audit the reward and LLM judges used for evaluation.
9XFlJl0lZc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem of training on open-ended scientific reports is practical and that the paper provides a fairly complete pipeline covering tool interaction, reward design, and curriculum training.
9XFlJl0lZc.main_concern: It is unclear what the key new contribution is beyond combining existing tool-use, LLM-scoring, and curriculum RL ideas, and evaluation relies on LLM judges and reference-report matching.

NUv6o17T6r.one_liner: Process reward learning as a regularized-Nash game over reasoning candidates, with coverage-optimized online pair allocation for multi-hop KGQA.
NUv6o17T6r.problem: Bradley-Terry process reward models break when several paths are correct, leaving steps without a clear better or worse, and when chained preferences place one sample in contradictory positions.
NUv6o17T6r.method: Preference learning is cast as a game over reasoning candidates with a regularized Nash equilibrium objective, so samples without clear preference receive similar exploration probabilities. CO-OIPO allocates comparison pairs within a sampled candidate pool to use a limited comparison budget, with a proof under sufficient sampling coverage, an expressive policy model and full optimization in each round.
NUv6o17T6r.key_idea: Replace Bradley-Terry pairwise ranking with a regularized Nash-equilibrium objective over candidates and choose which pairs to compare by coverage optimization within a sampled pool.
NUv6o17T6r.evidence: Theoretical analysis plus experiments on two multi-hop knowledge-graph QA datasets, with an LLM judge (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, per reviews) supplying online pairwise preferences.
NUv6o17T6r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the game-theoretic formulation as novel and mathematically well grounded, with a complete pipeline from candidate generation to sampling correction.
NUv6o17T6r.main_concern: Evaluation is narrow (two multi-hop QA datasets) and depends on an LLM judge and many unablated hyperparameters, with no matched-compute cost comparison.

v1m4YAnbyI.one_liner: Linear-program analysis shows block verification is optimal with off-path probabilities, motivating greedy multi-path block verification for speculative decoding.
v1m4YAnbyI.problem: Block verification is shown optimal only among on-path verifiers with a single draft path, leaving open how much multi-path drafts and off-path probabilities can improve speculative decoding.
v1m4YAnbyI.method: An information-agnostic linear program shows block verification stays optimal even with off-path probabilities and extends to multiple candidate paths. Because the optimal multi-path algorithm is intractable, a stricter greedy class yields an efficient method, greedy multi-path block verification (GBV).
v1m4YAnbyI.key_idea: Verify multiple draft paths greedily with a ranking rule that accounts for the proposal distribution induced by selecting among drafts, derived from the LP framework.
v1m4YAnbyI.evidence: LP-based optimality proofs and a canonical decomposition of optimal multi-path verification, plus walltime and block-efficiency experiments on OPT, Qwen, and Llama models per reviews.
v1m4YAnbyI.claimed_gains: Improves block efficiency over block verification in the multi-path setting; no numbers visible in the truncated abstract.
v1m4YAnbyI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the LP formulation and optimality results for single- and multi-path verification are rigorous and insightful, and that GBV is an implementable approximation.
v1m4YAnbyI.main_concern: Practical gains are inconsistent: GBV is slower than block verification in several Qwen and Llama settings, and the greedy rule has no approximation or non-degradation guarantee.

qvg8Lqz3Vy.one_liner: Extends Meta Flow Maps to discrete and joint discrete-continuous data for inference-time reward steering of DNA and molecule design.
qvg8Lqz3Vy.problem: Multimodal generative methods for biological design are hard to adapt at inference time to meet design constraints.
qvg8Lqz3Vy.method: Adapts Meta Flow Maps to discrete (dMFM) and multimodal (multiMFM) settings, steering a single trained backbone with estimated reward gradients to design DNA with a target mechanical property and molecules (QM9, GEOM-Drugs) with a given physical property.
qvg8Lqz3Vy.key_idea: Use a one-shot flow-map sampler's accurate reward-gradient estimates to steer generation at inference time, with continuous relaxation of categorical variables, reusing one backbone across rewards.
qvg8Lqz3Vy.evidence: DNA sequence design with a target mechanical property and molecule design on QM9 and GEOM-Drugs, compared with fine-tuning methods adapted to each task.
qvg8Lqz3Vy.claimed_gains: Steering achieves high accuracy with a single trained backbone, outperforming fine-tuning methods adapted for task-specific ends; no numbers stated.
qvg8Lqz3Vy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find reusing one pretrained model across reward functions practical and the extension to discrete and multimodal biological data a useful application.
qvg8Lqz3Vy.main_concern: Reward gradients for discrete variables are inexact and weakly validated (low cosine similarity with reference gradients, no discrete posterior check), and comparisons with related guidance methods and baselines are insufficient.

DVcLTSQnQp.one_liner: Trains a reasoning LLM's question selection with expected-information-gain rewards computed by an external generative model, amortizing sequential experimental design.
DVcLTSQnQp.problem: LLMs struggle to adaptively gather information in experimental design tasks despite extensive pretraining knowledge and strong reasoning.
DVcLTSQnQp.method: The paper amortizes sequential Bayesian experimental design into an LLM by training the reasoning that guides action selection with information-gain rewards, with the experimental generative model specified independently of the LLM's own beliefs. It studies generative-model construction, reward estimation, hypothesis-space specification, multi-step objectives, and compute costs.
DVcLTSQnQp.key_idea: Decouple the policy from the generative model that scores hypotheses, and reward the policy's reasoning-plus-question outputs with expected information gain under that external model.
DVcLTSQnQp.evidence: Twenty Questions, including unseen domains, against inference-time and training-time BED baselines, plus transfer to the Medi-Q clinical dialogue benchmark; reviewers note GPT-5 as the external likelihood model and a single training seed.
DVcLTSQnQp.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports qualitative improvements in information acquisition and task performance at substantially lower computational cost than BED baselines.
DVcLTSQnQp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling the acting LLM from the generative model used to score information gain is sensible and well motivated, with experiments showing benefits and generalization to new domains.
DVcLTSQnQp.main_concern: The comparison does not isolate the benefit of decoupling from that of using a stronger external model (GPT-5) for the training signal, which is also the evaluation model, and only one training seed is used.

pX0kMHM0Y3.one_liner: LLM agents run in-silico conditioning experiments on a whole-brain Drosophila connectome spiking model to teach and diagnose memory.
pX0kMHM0Y3.problem: Whole-brain connectome models make in-silico behavioural experiments possible, and the paper tests how language-model agents can experiment on one as an experimenter would.
pX0kMHM0Y3.method: A leaky integrate-and-fire network of the adult Drosophila brain (FlyWire, 138,639 neurons) with dopamine-gated plasticity at Kenyon-cell output synapses serves as the environment. Agents present odours, pair them with sugar or shock, and measure approach valence in open-loop teaching and closed-loop diagnosis tasks, including GRPO training.
pX0kMHM0Y3.key_idea: Use a connectome simulator with exact ground truth as an environment and reward source, so agents' protocols and diagnoses are scored exactly and can drive reinforcement learning.
pX0kMHM0Y3.evidence: Simulated teaching and diagnosis tasks (60 test flies and 74 teaching configurations per reviewers) with GRPO-trained agents and a frontier model, plus a test of surrogate exploitation.
pX0kMHM0Y3.claimed_gains: In open-loop teaching one pairing per target meets 0.80 of targets (doing nothing meets 0.71), surrogate-optimised teachers score 0.99 predicted versus 0.75 measured, and in diagnosis Claude Sonnet 5 scores 0.832 against 0.793 for a thresholding rule (0.846 with the prior).
pX0kMHM0Y3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the connectome environment with exact ground truth is new and useful for evaluating agents and as a reinforcement learning reward source, with a clear surrogate over-optimisation result.
pX0kMHM0Y3.main_concern: The evaluation scale is small (60 test flies, 74 teaching configurations, single runs) and the hand-tuned model is not validated against real flies, so several comparisons are borderline.

9HUfUL91I3.one_liner: Self-supervised representation learning on star-shaped bundles of integral curves, with stencil-symmetry architecture and rotation-consistency objective, for vortex detection.
9HUfUL91I3.problem: Individual trajectories carry limited information, while the relevant flow structure lies in the collective deformation of neighboring trajectories and should not depend on spatial orientation.
9HUfUL91I3.method: Each neighborhood is a star with a center curve and symmetrically seeded neighbors. StarVortex combines an architectural bias from the sampling stencil's discrete symmetry with a representation-level objective enforcing consistency under continuous rotations, plus reconstruction and variance-covariance regularization.
9HUfUL91I3.key_idea: Enforce discrete stencil symmetry in the architecture and continuous rotation consistency in the latent space on local integral-curve bundles, without velocity or vorticity inputs.
9HUfUL91I3.evidence: Label-free vortex-region discovery and supervised recognition of vortex regions, corelines, and hairpin vortices across pathlines and streamlines, with ablations and domain-generalization experiments for the supervised tasks.
9HUfUL91I3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning vortex structure directly from neighboring integral-curve geometry, with symmetry and rotation-consistency objectives, is a well-motivated approach that improves on geometric clustering baselines.
9HUfUL91I3.main_concern: Evaluation validity is questioned: self-supervised vortex detection is not tested on unseen flows, checkpoints were chosen on the test set, and baselines use fewer neighboring curves.

vilp2gofUS.one_liner: Proves that group-invariant word co-occurrence statistics make learned embeddings matrix elements of the group's irreducible representations.
vilp2gofUS.problem: Circle and Pringle geometries in language-model representations were traced only to translation symmetry in co-occurrence statistics, leaving more general symmetries unexplained.
vilp2gofUS.method: For arbitrary finite groups, compact groups and homogeneous spaces, it proves that if a word family's co-occurrence statistics are invariant under G, the learned embeddings are irrep matrix elements (Fourier modes for cyclic G). It checks the prediction on word-embedding analogies, dihedral-group structure in major and minor triads, and a celestial setting.
vilp2gofUS.key_idea: Co-occurrence statistics invariant under a group G force embeddings to be matrix elements of G's irreducible representations, with Fourier modes arising for cyclic groups.
vilp2gofUS.evidence: Proofs plus three experimental settings (word analogies, music triads under a dihedral group, and sky or celestial representations); reviewers note all embeddings come from eigendecomposing an idealized co-occurrence matrix rather than trained models.
vilp2gofUS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives a clean, general group-theoretic extension of prior work that unifies months, chords and sky-sphere geometry under one theory.
vilp2gofUS.main_concern: No embeddings trained on real corpora are analysed (all come from eigendecomposing an idealized co-occurrence matrix), so the link to real training dynamics and autoregressive LLMs is not established.

zHMqXlU4Le.one_liner: Robustifies IV moment conditions by perturbing the treatment operator and outcome moment with a shared score, yielding operator-robust worst-case criteria.
zHMqXlU4Le.problem: Instrumental variable regression needs its moment conditions to hold, but weak identification, invalid instruments, and distribution shifts increase error or violate the moment restrictions.
zHMqXlU4Le.method: Instead of protecting against perturbations of the data distribution, the method traces joint distributional perturbations through the identifying moments to derive a common score that jointly perturbs the treatment operator and outcome moment while preserving their relationship. This pushforward construction gives an operator-robust worst-case criterion and tractable convex average-case surrogates, with a special case that is a nonparametric operator analogue of k-class regularization.
zHMqXlU4Le.key_idea: Push joint distributional perturbations through the moment restrictions to get one score that perturbs the treatment operator and outcome moment together, preserving their relationship.
zHMqXlU4Le.evidence: Theory on how score robustness changes identification and preserves the causal target, with error bounds in terms of identification strength, estimation error, and robustness-induced bias; experiments on synthetic, semi-synthetic, and real-world settings.
zHMqXlU4Le.claimed_gains: Improves over existing IV estimators under weak identification, invalid instruments, and distribution shift; no numbers stated.
zHMqXlU4Le.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analysis of the trade-off between robustness and structural-function bias is interesting, the operator-ambiguity-set formulation is well founded, and the experiments are broad.
zHMqXlU4Le.main_concern: The paper is hard to follow and never clearly states the concrete estimator it proposes, and its novelty over existing maximum-moment-restriction and DRO work and k-class estimators is questioned.

6zvO5PZttx.one_liner: History-conditioned flow matching with differentiable geometric refinement generates protein conformational rollouts under temperature as a controllable action.
6zvO5PZttx.problem: Molecular dynamics is too expensive for systematic experiments, and existing generative models give plausible trajectories that do not depend on dynamical history, represent stochastic futures, or respond to perturbations.
6zvO5PZttx.method: The model infers predictive state from conformational history and generates stochastic future trajectories under temperature actions, trained on multi-temperature mdCATH. It combines history-conditioned flow matching with differentiable geometric refinement to produce temporally coherent, geometrically valid multi-step rollouts; reviewers note temperature enters through AdaLN.
6zvO5PZttx.key_idea: Condition flow matching on conformational history and a temperature action, then refine each generated step with differentiable geometry so rollouts stay valid and temperature can be intervened on.
6zvO5PZttx.evidence: Trained and evaluated on multi-temperature mdCATH, compared with persistence and matched history-ablated controls, with ablations on temporal ordering and temperature-intervention branching experiments.
6zvO5PZttx.claimed_gains: Captures trajectory distributions and dynamical observables more accurately than persistence and history-ablated controls, and temperature interventions give physically consistent changes in flexibility and structure; no numbers stated.
6zvO5PZttx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formulation (multi-step stochastic prediction from history under temperature control) is important, the evaluation is careful and controlled, and results are consistently good across metrics.
6zvO5PZttx.main_concern: The 'temperature as an action' claim is not distinguished from ordinary temperature-conditioned generation, the matched-MD-branch protocol is under-specified, and baselines such as TEMPO and DynaMode are missing.

4bP6tTSih9.one_liner: Calibrated hidden-state probes audit whether process rewards track changes in predicted scientific-task success.
4bP6tTSih9.problem: Math-trained process reward models may penalize useful scientific exploration because local step correctness differs from progress toward a scientific conclusion.
4bP6tTSih9.method: SciPRI estimates per-step VIG as the change in calibrated task-success log-probability from a probe over frozen hidden states. It audits reward alignment across domains and evaluates InfoPRM for candidate selection and reward-guided search.
4bP6tTSih9.key_idea: Compare process rewards with probe-estimated changes in task-success log-probability to detect reversed reward alignment on scientific steps.
4bP6tTSih9.evidence: Evaluations include a math control, BLADE, gold-step validation on 102 ScienceAgentBench tasks, alternative observers and generators, perturbations, and selection and search experiments.
4bP6tTSih9.claimed_gains: Qwen2.5-Math-PRM shifts from length-controlled partial correlation ρ=+0.209 and slope β_I=+0.0094 (p<10^(-29)) on math to ρ=−0.170 and β_I=−0.0101 (p=3 × 10^(-42)) on scientific tasks.
4bP6tTSih9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical scientific-agent supervision problem and the broad diagnostic evaluation of reward misalignment.
4bP6tTSih9.main_concern: VIG has weak independent validation as scientific step value, making it difficult to distinguish reward-model errors from probe-estimation errors.

8dPblNkCHj.one_liner: Paired simulation code, configurations, and videos compare explicit physics reconstruction with video-diffusion extrapolation on identical scenes.
8dPblNkCHj.problem: Physical-dynamics inference from video needs controlled evaluation of how executable simulations and direct video generation fail during extrapolation.
8dPblNkCHj.method: MPMWorlds pairs executable 2D Material Point Method simulations with scene configurations and rendered videos. The study varies physically relevant side information to compare code generation and video diffusion on the same scenes.
8dPblNkCHj.key_idea: Pair executable physics programs and videos for identical scenes, then vary side information to compare reconstruction and extrapolation failure modes.
8dPblNkCHj.evidence: Experiments cover deformable objects, fluids, kinematic objects, and emitters across three VLMs and three video diffusion models, including a sample-matched comparison.
8dPblNkCHj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the paired code-configuration-video resource and the meaningful comparison of simulation-based and direct video prediction.
8dPblNkCHj.main_concern: Experiments restricted to synthetic 2D simulations do not establish whether the findings transfer to real videos or 3D physics.

1Qq8yrS6QI.one_liner: Reward annealing reweights complete responses while target-preserving suffix regeneration progressively refines candidate particles.
1Qq8yrS6QI.problem: Best-of-N does not share reward information between candidates, while tokenwise SMC can discard promising responses using unreliable partial rewards.
1Qq8yrS6QI.method: APC runs sequential Monte Carlo along increasing reward strength with complete responses as particles. Predictor steps reweight particles, and corrector steps regenerate suffixes and select candidates through transitions preserving the current intermediate target.
1Qq8yrS6QI.key_idea: Anneal reward strength over complete-response particles, alternating reward reweighting with target-preserving suffix regeneration.
1Qq8yrS6QI.evidence: Experiments cover two mathematical-reasoning datasets and IFEval, with generation-and-reward FLOP accounting and ablations of annealing and correction.
1Qq8yrS6QI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a favorable quality-versus-computation trade-off and appreciate theoretically grounded sampling and component ablations.
1Qq8yrS6QI.main_concern: The comparisons and ablations do not fully isolate the sampler and corrector's contribution from other pipeline choices and added computation.

YbbgdY1klS.one_liner: Critical-error trajectory repair teaches small agents to request brief LLM guidance while executing their own trajectories.
YbbgdY1klS.problem: Small-agent assistance policies may request help at the wrong step, ignore capability limits, or delegate too much execution to larger models.
YbbgdY1klS.method: BeaconAgent replaces a teacher-identified first critical error with an ASK_HELP step and uses the repaired successful trajectory for supervised fine-tuning. A subsequent reinforcement-learning stage trains help seeking while the small model retains execution and receives guidance only as an observation.
YbbgdY1klS.key_idea: Insert explicit help requests at the first critical failure in training trajectories and provide brief guidance without handing over agent execution.
YbbgdY1klS.evidence: Experiments span 11 benchmarks in QA, mathematics, and coding, including unseen coding transfer and comparisons of intervention positions and assistance forms.
YbbgdY1klS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value improving small-agent reliability while limiting large-model use and report encouraging results across tasks.
YbbgdY1klS.main_concern: Missing related help-seeking baselines and matched ordinary-RL controls leave the specific policy and reward design's added value unclear.

ug6avwOfLy.one_liner: Individual similarity judgments personalize perceptual targets used to fine-tune visual brain encoding representations.
ug6avwOfLy.problem: Brain-response prediction accuracy does not ensure that an encoder's representations reflect a particular person's perceptual similarities.
ug6avwOfLy.method: The approach adapts a generic perceptual similarity model separately for each participant and uses it to infer similarity structure over encoder-training images. It fine-tunes matched encoder initializations with either generic or personalized similarity targets.
ug6avwOfLy.key_idea: Personalize perceptual similarity targets from individual judgments, then align each participant's brain encoder to those targets.
ug6avwOfLy.evidence: Experiments use similarity judgments on 100 images from 8 Natural Scenes Dataset participants, repeated held-out-image cross-validation, and paired nonparametric tests.
ug6avwOfLy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear personalization question, simple method, and empirical evaluation of perceptual alignment.
ug6avwOfLy.main_concern: Personalization gains remain confounded with adaptation to the shared judgment task and image set.

n2DYZiI8gz.one_liner: Prior-information cards and noise tiers structure comparisons of differential-equation discovery methods.
n2DYZiI8gz.problem: Equation-discovery results rarely disclose or control how much prior information different methods receive.
n2DYZiI8gz.method: DiffEqDiscoveryBench standardizes ODE and PDE systems and supplies prior cards at three information levels in each method's native form. It crosses these levels with noise tiers and measures exact structural recovery alongside held-out prediction error.
n2DYZiI8gz.key_idea: Vary disclosed equation priors through explicit cards, translate them into method-native inputs, and evaluate structural recovery separately from numerical fit.
n2DYZiI8gz.evidence: The benchmark includes 337 systems, with 332 reference equations and five unlabeled CFD blood-flow fields, and evaluates seven methods across three prior levels and four noise tiers.
n2DYZiI8gz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value treating prior information as an explicit experimental variable across multiple equation-discovery families.
n2DYZiI8gz.main_concern: Unequal effective priors, side information, tuning, and compute budgets confound cross-method comparisons.

Dqj6aHeBKu.one_liner: Periodic prompt-admission budgets regulate active requests to control memory growth during LLM decoding.
Dqj6aHeBKu.problem: Unknown decode lengths make request memory grow unpredictably, risking overflow and serving instability.
Dqj6aHeBKu.method: The framework limits how quickly prompts enter the active set through flow-controlled admission budgets. It characterizes periodic-policy stability for known lengths and derives necessary and sufficient conditions alongside finite-horizon overflow analysis for unknown lengths.
Dqj6aHeBKu.key_idea: Regulate prompt admission with periodic budgets so active decoding requests remain within memory and stability constraints.
Dqj6aHeBKu.evidence: The paper proves known-length stability results and evaluates throughput and latency against common scheduling strategies, including Vidur simulations.
Dqj6aHeBKu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the structural stability theory and the simplicity of the admission policy.
