Dqj6aHeBKu.main_concern: Known-length and zero-prefill assumptions limit the practical guarantees, while finite-horizon overflow bounds do not establish stability after repeated unknown-length evictions and restarts.

qGwEACj2xh.one_liner: Online instrumental-variable effect estimates detect changing causal relationships and guide adaptive-tree updates.
qGwEACj2xh.problem: Conventional drift detectors monitor distribution or error proxies, often need labels, and give little explanation of changing data-generating mechanisms.
qGwEACj2xh.method: The framework uses an initial causal graph to identify instruments and monitors causal effects with the Wald estimator. IVDD compares successive estimates without ground-truth labels, while IVAT uses local effect heterogeneity and monitoring for targeted tree adaptation.
qGwEACj2xh.key_idea: Track online Wald estimates for graph-selected instrumental variables to localize causal-effect changes and guide local model adaptation.
qGwEACj2xh.evidence: Empirical evaluations use synthetic structural causal models and real-world data streams.
qGwEACj2xh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers consider causal analysis of concept drift a relevant direction for understanding when and how stream models should adapt.
qGwEACj2xh.main_concern: The experiments do not clearly establish that monitored effect changes distinguish causal-mechanism drift from covariate or confounder shifts.

8CHQF1evy4.one_liner: A simulated enterprise warehouse hides ground-truth state to test data agents on analytical decisions and actions.
8CHQF1evy4.problem: Existing benchmarks lack realistic enterprise-scale workflows that combine multi-table reasoning, statistical analysis, and consequential actions.
8CHQF1evy4.method: Argo-Bench simulates a New York City food-delivery platform and projects its state into an Oracle E-Business Suite-style warehouse. Agents reconstruct facts from the warehouse and file actions, with executable reference solutions establishing solvability.
8CHQF1evy4.key_idea: Expose only a warehouse projection of a simulated business world, requiring agents to reconstruct hidden facts before submitting operational actions.
8CHQF1evy4.evidence: The benchmark contains 210 tasks over 235 tables and 7.49 billion rows, with diverse model evaluations and failure analyses.
8CHQF1evy4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value evaluating complete enterprise analytical workflows and the business consequences of agent decisions beyond query correctness.
8CHQF1evy4.main_concern: Ambiguous task descriptions and mismatches between prompts and graders undermine interpretation of some benchmark scores.

JXOlrC0vGU.one_liner: Auditing contextual-integrity benchmarks quantifies data-quality problems, evaluation variance, and sensitivity to privacy metrics.
JXOlrC0vGU.problem: Missing artifacts, reproducibility issues, and incomparable metrics make contextual-integrity evaluation claims difficult to interpret.
JXOlrC0vGU.method: The paper systematizes limitations of contextual-integrity benchmarks and critically audits three open-source benchmarks with available data. It examines synthetic data quality, evaluation variance, and how metric choices alter reported privacy and utility.
JXOlrC0vGU.key_idea: Audit benchmark data, variance, and alternative privacy metrics to separate sources of uncertainty in contextual-integrity evaluation.
JXOlrC0vGU.evidence: Quantitative analyses of three open-source benchmarks examine inconsistent synthetic profiles, labeling disagreements, and privacy-metric differences.
JXOlrC0vGU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value scrutinizing privacy-benchmark measurement validity and quantifying concrete synthetic-data quality issues.
JXOlrC0vGU.main_concern: Differences between metrics that measure distinct constructs do not by themselves establish misleading evaluation for a specified deployment objective.

T2sw3QfYe5.one_liner: Evaluating weight, activation, and lookup-table quantization under finite-field provers characterizes zero-knowledge LLM proving costs.
T2sw3QfYe5.problem: Conventional low-bit quantization does not directly reduce zero-knowledge proof generation costs for private verifiable LLM inference because ZK provers operate over finite fields dominated by nonlinearities and lookup constraints.
T2sw3QfYe5.method: The paper formalizes ZK-friendly quantization and systematically sweeps weight, activation, and nonlinear lookup-table precision across language models, measuring both predictive utility degradation and realized finite-field prover costs.
T2sw3QfYe5.key_idea: Benchmark weight, activation, and nonlinear lookup-table bit-widths against finite-field arithmetic and lookup constraints in zero-knowledge LLM proof generation.
T2sw3QfYe5.evidence: Utility experiments cover nine language models including Qwen2.5-14B and MoE Qwen3-30B-A3B alongside operator-level RMSNorm diagnoses and actual prover measurements on GPT-2 and 14B linear projections.
T2sw3QfYe5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that studying quantization through realized finite-field proof costs rather than inference bit-width is practically valuable, praising the nine-model precision study and operator-level nonlinear diagnostics.
T2sw3QfYe5.main_concern: All three reviewers note that full-model proving runs only on small GPT-2 models lacking RMSNorm rather than modern 14B models end-to-end, while the B16 RMSNorm failure stems from naive uniform-grid range discretization.

eiZIgH3WFy.one_liner: Aligned-domain fine-tuning experiments expose context confusion when learned behaviors transfer into contexts where they become inappropriate.
eiZIgH3WFy.problem: Filtering individually misaligned training examples may fail to prevent domain-specific misalignment after fine-tuning.
eiZIgH3WFy.method: The study fine-tunes models on aligned examples and tests inappropriate transfer across contextual boundaries. It compares general and targeted alignment data, in-context examples, and representational shifts to examine causes and mitigations.
eiZIgH3WFy.key_idea: Train an appropriate behavior in one context and test whether its transfer violates alignment requirements in another.
eiZIgH3WFy.evidence: Experiments span gender equality, privacy, and physical safety, with reviewers reporting consistent effects across four models and synthetic training data.
eiZIgH3WFy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the finding that individually aligned training samples can produce context-dependent post-training safety failures.
eiZIgH3WFy.main_concern: Small synthetic datasets designed around predefined transfer patterns may amplify the effect and do not establish generalization to realistic fine-tuning mixtures.

Gr6ScOllUc.one_liner: DataMemo stores extracted web records in a relational database and tracks coverage to reuse data across analytical requests.
Gr6ScOllUc.problem: Repeated analytical requests waste time reacquiring shared web records, while unstructured histories obscure retained data coverage and interpretation.
Gr6ScOllUc.method: DataMemo incrementally builds relational storage for acquired records, reuses it across questions, and collects more data when coverage is insufficient. DataMemoBench evaluates successive analytical queries over shared sources.
Gr6ScOllUc.key_idea: Persist extracted records with schema and coverage information so agents can query existing data before acquiring more.
Gr6ScOllUc.evidence: DataMemoBench contains 3,799 questions across eight domains, with GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.8 comparisons against continued-session and other memory baselines.
Gr6ScOllUc.claimed_gains: DataMemo reduces token cost by 36–46% and wall-clock time by 6–13%, with a 5.8–11.8% relative accuracy improvement over the strongest baseline.
Gr6ScOllUc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value relational memory for reducing repeated web acquisition and the substantial benchmark for evaluating reuse.
Gr6ScOllUc.main_concern: LLM-driven schema design and coverage decisions lack sufficiently explicit reliability criteria and failure analysis.

e49RXNVfRz.one_liner: GSS clusters weight groups by distributional shape and fine-tunes shared sketches indexed by 4-bit weight codes.
e49RXNVfRz.problem: Spatially fixed sketch tables prevent similar weight groups at different locations from sharing compressed adaptation parameters.
e49RXNVfRz.method: GSS clusters normalized weight-group distributions within each matrix and assigns shared learnable sketches across arbitrary positions. Each weight stores a 4-bit sketch index, while adaptation updates only shared sketch entries.
e49RXNVfRz.key_idea: Share trainable quantization sketches among weight groups with similar normalized distributions regardless of matrix position.
e49RXNVfRz.evidence: Six diffusion transformers spanning 2B to 20B parameters undergo quantization, text-to-image, subject-personalization, and paired-editing evaluations.
e49RXNVfRz.claimed_gains: GSS achieves competitive adaptation quality against full fine-tuning while using over 100× fewer trainable parameters.
e49RXNVfRz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find distribution-based global sketch sharing simple and practically motivated, with useful integration of compression and adaptation.
e49RXNVfRz.main_concern: Small trainable-parameter counts do not establish practical efficiency given incompletely reported metadata costs and unfavorable speed or inference-memory comparisons.

Oyda560aPn.one_liner: FlashSampling fuses tiled Gumbel-Max sampling into the LM-head matmul to avoid materializing full logits.
Oyda560aPn.problem: Large-vocabulary categorical sampling adds memory traffic and kernels after language-model output projection.
Oyda560aPn.method: The kernel computes logits on chip, adds Gumbel noise, retains per-tile maxima, and reduces those maxima into exact samples. Tensor-parallel variants replace logits all-gather with streaming peer-to-peer writes that overlap communication and computation.
Oyda560aPn.key_idea: Fuse Gumbel-Max and tile-wise argmax reduction into output projection, retaining only local winners instead of the full logits tensor.
Oyda560aPn.evidence: Exactness proofs accompany H100, H200, B200, and B300 benchmarks, tensor-parallel microbenchmarks up to 8 GPUs, and end-to-end vLLM tests.
Oyda560aPn.claimed_gains: FlashSampling reduces time per output token by up to 10% in the tested end-to-end vLLM configurations.
Oyda560aPn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clear exact-sampling design, implementation, and hardware evaluation.
Oyda560aPn.main_concern: The implementation omits top-k and top-p sampling, leaving its benefit for common production decoding configurations untested.

fcgty83J6c.one_liner: ReLope trains a separate LoRA-adapted decision layer with a KL bottleneck to route multimodal queries.
fcgty83J6c.problem: Correctness is harder to predict from image-conditioned hidden states than caption-conditioned states, limiting multimodal routing.
fcgty83J6c.method: Attention Probe first learns to pool frozen token states for correctness prediction. ReLope instead adapts a copied model layer with LoRA and a KL-penalized stochastic bottleneck, sharing frozen lower layers while preserving the answer-generation branch.
fcgty83J6c.key_idea: Adapt one copied transformer layer for correctness prediction through LoRA and a KL-regularized stochastic bottleneck.
fcgty83J6c.evidence: Probe AUC, HSIC, and label CKA analyses accompany routing evaluations across 15 dataset–backbone combinations with three seeds reported by reviewers.
fcgty83J6c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the separate decision branch and consistent low-overhead improvements in multimodal correctness prediction.
fcgty83J6c.main_concern: The specific contribution beyond prior adapted correctness estimators and bottleneck probes remains insufficiently isolated.

IqJxWIbfR5.one_liner: Visual-symbol interventions compare VLM behavioral steering with explicit interpretation and symbol-based communication.
IqJxWIbfR5.problem: VLMs' interpretations and production of visual meaning may not predict how symbols influence their behavior.
IqJxWIbfR5.method: The study inserts simple symbols into unrelated tasks and compares behavioral effects with direct interpretations and reasoning traces. Model-to-model games test generated visual cues for abstract concepts and stories.
IqJxWIbfR5.key_idea: Inject simple visual symbols and compare their behavioral effects with verbal interpretations and symbols generated for communication.
IqJxWIbfR5.evidence: Reviewers describe tests of 288 symbols across models and tasks, caption and noise controls, visual perturbations, and communication games.
IqJxWIbfR5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find systematic, model-specific behavioral steering by simple visual symbols convincing and interesting.
IqJxWIbfR5.main_concern: Aggregate steering effects cannot justify labeling individual reasoning traces faithful or unfaithful.

LQo7Gpcyy3.one_liner: StairDrop progressively drops and restores tokens across transformer depth, fusing skipped information at each restoration.
LQo7Gpcyy3.problem: Token-sparse diffusion training saves compute but leaves the organization of information across network depth underexplored.
LQo7Gpcyy3.method: StairDrop uses hierarchical participation levels with skip fusion at restoration stages and assigns depth across those stages. Training uses sparse participation, while inference runs all tokens through the full backbone with fusion layers retained.
LQo7Gpcyy3.key_idea: Progressively reduce and restore token participation across depth with skip fusion at each restoration stage.
LQo7Gpcyy3.evidence: Controlled SiT-B/2 and SiT-XL/2 experiments on ImageNet 256×256 vary participation stages and depth allocation under guided sampling.
LQo7Gpcyy3.claimed_gains: StairDrop matches FID-50K of 1.96 at half the strongest token-dropping system's training compute and reaches 1.47 versus 1.55 at equal compute.
LQo7Gpcyy3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the simple hierarchical design and controlled experiments on token participation and depth allocation.
LQo7Gpcyy3.main_concern: The mechanistic analysis does not sufficiently explain why progressive reduction and restoration work or guide hierarchy selection.

5S0fy7cPii.one_liner: PrivAwareBench measures spontaneous privacy warnings and sensitive-content suppression when benign users disclose unnecessary private information.
5S0fy7cPii.problem: Privacy evaluations often overlook sensitive information that benign users unintentionally include in legitimate requests.
5S0fy7cPii.method: The benchmark varies exposure conditions and measures risk warnings separately from sensitive-content suppression. Human involvement and manual checks guide data construction, and a human–LLM agreement study selects the evaluation judge.
5S0fy7cPii.key_idea: Insert unintended sensitive disclosures into benign requests and score unprompted warning and suppression behaviors separately.
5S0fy7cPii.evidence: Experiments evaluate 18 representative LLMs with manually checked benchmark data and a judge selected against human assessments.
5S0fy7cPii.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical problem of benign-user disclosure and the value of systematically measuring model responses.
5S0fy7cPii.main_concern: Response-side warnings and suppression do not establish broader proactive privacy protection or justify requiring intervention from the model itself.

jffYZQ57FF.one_liner: ATF-kNN fits routed per-expert affine corrections and imputes deployment residuals with nearest neighbors in expert-readout space.
jffYZQ57FF.problem: Frozen MoE predictors can have expert-specific deployment errors that scalar black-box correction ignores.
jffYZQ57FF.method: ATF-kNN uses exposed routing probabilities and expert outputs to fit one offset and gain per expert in one step. It then imputes residuals for unlabeled deployment examples using k-nearest neighbors in the routed readout space.
jffYZQ57FF.key_idea: Gate expert-specific affine corrections with routing probabilities and infer unlabeled residuals from neighboring routed readouts.
jffYZQ57FF.evidence: Population-gain analysis and a finite-sample risk certificate accompany real and synthetic regression tests with label-budget, distribution-shift, and expert-count ablations.
jffYZQ57FF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a lightweight, interpretable correction that uses expert-level information without retraining the teacher.
jffYZQ57FF.main_concern: The kNN-imputation component inconsistently improves on the same affine correction without imputation.

EsBS8s9n6I.one_liner: An SMC-guided planner combines gradient moves, particle resampling, and latent-space cost-to-go for action-sequence search.
EsBS8s9n6I.problem: Sampling planners struggle at long horizons, while gradient-based planners can become trapped in local minima.
EsBS8s9n6I.method: The planner evolves a population of action sequences through cost-based importance weighting and resampling while gradient optimization updates candidate plans. A PDE-derived cost-to-go uses latent-state structure to guide population evolution.
EsBS8s9n6I.key_idea: Alternate gradient-based action-sequence moves with cost-weighted population resampling guided by a latent-space cost-to-go.
EsBS8s9n6I.evidence: Navigation and manipulation experiments use visual and proprioceptive world models, with reviewers noting evaluations on two pretrained world models.
EsBS8s9n6I.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the combination of population exploration and gradient optimization sensible and empirically effective on the tested tasks.
EsBS8s9n6I.main_concern: The algorithmic contribution beyond existing gradient-guided particle weighting and resampling remains unclear.

rSi7JMrteU.one_liner: Rotation-conditioned latent prediction preserves spatial geometry while spectral invariance preserves sound semantics in ambisonic audio.
rSi7JMrteU.problem: Semantic self-supervision often treats direction as a nuisance and loses spatial geometry in audio representations.
rSi7JMrteU.method: The framework generates rotated first-order ambisonic views with known relative rotations and trains spectral invariance alongside rotation prediction. It compares partitioned invariant/equivariant representations with an unsplit seq-JEPA latent.
rSi7JMrteU.key_idea: Use analytically rotated ambisonic views to predict rotation-dependent latent changes while enforcing stability under spectral perturbations.
rSi7JMrteU.evidence: Frozen representations undergo sound-event localization and detection on real recordings, spatial captioning, retrieval, and analyses of directional and semantic structure.
rSi7JMrteU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the physically grounded use of FOA rotations to learn spatial information without direction labels.
rSi7JMrteU.main_concern: Unmatched data, views, and training components obscure whether equivariance learning itself explains the gains.

C6m1EeX7Ga.one_liner: Frozen diffusion scores regularize input-noise optimization to constrain image-space drift during reward maximization.
C6m1EeX7Ga.problem: Optimizing diffusion input noise can exploit rewards while producing unrealistic images despite noise-space constraints.
C6m1EeX7Ga.method: BIDS relates image divergence to denoising-trajectory divergence through the Data Processing Inequality and applies a practical frozen-score surrogate. The framework also supports pairwise preference optimization.
C6m1EeX7Ga.key_idea: Penalize drift during noise optimization with a surrogate computed from the frozen model's score function along denoising trajectories.
C6m1EeX7Ga.evidence: Experiments span UNet and DiT diffusion architectures, multiple rewards, distributional-drift measurements, and human preference evaluation.
C6m1EeX7Ga.claimed_gains: BIDS reduces CMMD by over 75% and achieves up to an 80.30% human preference win rate.
C6m1EeX7Ga.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a simple score-based regularizer that integrates with existing noise-optimization pipelines.
C6m1EeX7Ga.main_concern: The distinction from prior noise-optimization and reward-hacking methods remains insufficiently established.

sbsBZt3HAc.one_liner: Frozen audio-language hidden states and motion history autoregressively generate facial motion in causal conversational blocks.
sbsBZt3HAc.problem: Conversational avatars need synchronized facial motion without cascaded speech reprocessing or waiting for future audio.
sbsBZt3HAc.method: HiddenFace attaches a motion head to frozen Voila and combines its audio and text hidden states with prior motion tokens. Each 160 ms block finalizes when its hidden states become available.
sbsBZt3HAc.key_idea: Predict each facial-motion token from current frozen LALM audio-text states and past motion tokens without future-state refinement.
sbsBZt3HAc.evidence: Held-out real dyadic conversations test speaking and listening motion under 160 ms block-causal conditions, with ablations and a blinded human study.
sbsBZt3HAc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the small, fast motion head and frozen-backbone interface for bounded-latency conversational animation.
sbsBZt3HAc.main_concern: Missing direct comparisons with closely related LALM-based motion systems leave the contribution insufficiently isolated.

5aEQxcBV3m.one_liner: Ordered blood-pressure prototypes refine latent PPG features to counter predictions drifting toward normal pressure.
5aEQxcBV3m.problem: Long-tailed blood-pressure data cause PPG-to-ABP models to suppress hypertensive peaks and raise hypotensive troughs.
5aEQxcBV3m.method: OPLR orders Low, Normal, and High prototypes in latent space and applies routing-guided prototype-token refinement before decoding. Normality Bias Index and TailBias diagnose regime-dependent drift and extreme-regime bias.
5aEQxcBV3m.key_idea: Impose ordered pressure-regime prototypes and route latent tokens through prototype-guided refinement before waveform decoding.
5aEQxcBV3m.evidence: Subject-wise calibration-free PulseDB evaluation and external transfer to MIMIC-IV and Queensland assess reconstruction and normality bias.
5aEQxcBV3m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that normality bias is an important failure in noninvasive blood-pressure reconstruction and value explicitly measuring it.
5aEQxcBV3m.main_concern: Insufficient comparison and positioning against imbalanced-regression and structured-representation methods weaken the claimed methodological contribution.

LcL0U29j3d.one_liner: Tokenwise density-ratio decisions and support-based whitening segment overhead imagery using frozen DINOv3 features.
LcL0U29j3d.problem: Training-free few-shot segmentation can lose accuracy through coarse decision units and poorly adapted feature geometry.
LcL0U29j3d.method: FROST removes positional components from frozen tokens, whitens support-estimated within-class scatter under shrinkage, and scores tokens by a density ratio. A Bayes-rule zero threshold produces token-level labels without dataset-specific tuning.
LcL0U29j3d.key_idea: Refine frozen token geometry with support-derived whitening, then apply zero-threshold density-ratio classification independently at each token.
LcL0U29j3d.evidence: Remote-sensing evaluations cover buildings, land cover, drone imagery, and floods, alongside component studies, oracle analyses, and same-backbone comparisons.
LcL0U29j3d.claimed_gains: The component study attributes 13.5 mIoU to decision granularity and 5.1 to feature refinement.
LcL0U29j3d.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value strong results across diverse remote-sensing tasks and detailed analyses of decision granularity.
LcL0U29j3d.main_concern: Unmatched pipeline controls prevent attributing comparative gains specifically to decision granularity or feature refinement.

mWzUTxY6q2.one_liner: Claim-relation graphs and temporal agreement matrices distinguish coordinated coalitions from apparent consensus in multi-agent debates.
mWzUTxY6q2.problem: Identical final answers cannot reveal whether agents independently agree or privately coordinate.
mWzUTxY6q2.method: LATTICE grounds messages into atomic claims, labels directed cross-agent relations, and aggregates time-windowed agent matrices with fixed composite weights. Paired sessions without coalitions provide negative controls.
mWzUTxY6q2.key_idea: Aggregate typed claim relations and temporal evidence-use patterns into agent-pair scores, checking inferred coalition structure against matched no-coalition sessions.
mWzUTxY6q2.evidence: Experiments use 40 constructed dossiers, five agents, fixed two-agent coalitions, and paired negative controls to compare public-information detectors.
mWzUTxY6q2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value examining claim-level interactions beyond final-answer agreement to detect coordination.
mWzUTxY6q2.main_concern: Evidence-inconsistent coalition instructions may confound coordination detection with shared reasoning errors and limit generalization to subtler coalitions.

Qr4G7V4zPW.one_liner: Privileged hints create easier benchmark variants whose accuracy trends forecast performance when small models otherwise score near zero.
Qr4G7V4zPW.problem: Near-zero downstream accuracy leaves small-model scaling studies without enough signal to extrapolate larger-model performance.
Qr4G7V4zPW.method: Hinted scaling laws fit accuracy as a function of model scale and hint strength across easier benchmark variants. Hinting also widens model accuracy gaps for more efficient ranking.
Qr4G7V4zPW.key_idea: Introduce graded privileged hints and extrapolate the resulting smooth accuracy surface across hint levels and model scales.
Qr4G7V4zPW.evidence: Tests use the Delphi pretraining ladder and post-trained model families on GSM8K, AIME, and HLE.
Qr4G7V4zPW.claimed_gains: Fits using at most 10^{20} FLOPs predict a 10^{23}-FLOP model's 25.9% GSM8K accuracy within 3 percentage points, while median forecasting error across settings falls from 21 percentage points to 4.3.
Qr4G7V4zPW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value hinting as a way to extract scaling and ranking signal from difficult benchmarks.
Qr4G7V4zPW.main_concern: Excluding all-zero settings and selecting evaluation cases using larger-model outcomes weakens evidence for the intended forecasting regime.

bmoi1ddcvA.one_liner: DDMC applies path-space Metropolis–Hastings correction to denoising diffusion proposals and combines them with local MALA moves.
bmoi1ddcvA.problem: Learned diffusion proposals can misrepresent target distributions and mode weights despite providing useful global moves.
bmoi1ddcvA.method: DDMC includes forward and reverse discrete-SDE path densities in a Metropolis–Hastings acceptance ratio. It trains denoisers on locally convergent MALA samples and combines corrected global diffusion moves with local MALA sampling.
bmoi1ddcvA.key_idea: Correct learned diffusion trajectories with a forward–reverse path-density acceptance ratio to preserve the target despite imperfect denoisers.
bmoi1ddcvA.evidence: Tests cover Gaussian mixtures, particle systems, a 550-dimensional Bayesian neural-network posterior, and LJ-38 funnel occupancy compared with parallel tempering.
bmoi1ddcvA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate exactness despite denoiser error and experiments demonstrating corrected mode weights on difficult targets.
bmoi1ddcvA.main_concern: Reviewers question methodological novelty and positioning relative to existing path-space diffusion MCMC methods.

1nMLwisvt5.one_liner: SNRDD and AVI-inspired sufficient conditions connect projected Bellman equation solvability with convergence of Q-learning variants.
1nMLwisvt5.problem: The relationship between projected Bellman equation solutions and convergence of linear Q-learning or approximate value iteration remains incompletely characterized.
1nMLwisvt5.method: The paper derives two sufficient conditions for projected Bellman equation solutions, including strictly negatively row-dominating diagonal structure. It uses SNRDD to unify tabular, linear, and regularized Q-learning convergence and compares these guarantees with AVI.
1nMLwisvt5.key_idea: Use a row-dominating diagonal condition to establish contraction-based guarantees for projected Bellman solvability and Q-learning convergence.
1nMLwisvt5.evidence: Theoretical analyses and constructive examples under epsilon-greedy behavior policies compare PBE solvability, Q-learning convergence, and AVI convergence.
1nMLwisvt5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the rigorous, unified convergence perspective across Q-learning variants.
1nMLwisvt5.main_concern: Reviewers question practical applicability because the sufficient conditions and fixed sampling assumptions may be restrictive and stability alone does not ensure useful policies.

OBJMVeBfSf.one_liner: Behavioral fingerprints of generated images train shadow-model predictors to infer hidden diffusion fine-tuning hyperparameters.
OBJMVeBfSf.problem: Black-box access to generated images may reveal training choices that model providers keep hidden.
OBJMVeBfSf.method: The method queries targets with fixed prompts and summarizes semantic, perceptual, and low-level image statistics. Predictors trained on shadow models with known recipes infer the target's fine-tuning hyperparameters.
OBJMVeBfSf.key_idea: Map image-statistic fingerprints from fixed prompt probes to hyperparameters using supervised predictors trained on shadow-model recipes.
OBJMVeBfSf.evidence: Evaluation covers 297 LoRA models, model-level splits, permutation tests, feature ablations, and transfer across architectures, base weights, and fine-tuning data.
OBJMVeBfSf.claimed_gains: LoRA rank recovery reaches 85.4% exact accuracy and 100% within one grid step, while complete-recipe recovery reaches 9.8% versus 0.21% uniform chance, a 48× increase.
OBJMVeBfSf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find convincing evidence that generated images retain recoverable traces of fine-tuning settings and appreciate statistical controls.
OBJMVeBfSf.main_concern: Reviewers question generalization beyond the evaluated recipe space because prior-knowledge assumptions and the mechanism of rank recovery remain unresolved.

tJhJtqVaAv.one_liner: S²GSR searches symmetry-typed expression graphs with path-conditioned sub-expression targets guiding neural Monte Carlo tree search.
tJhJtqVaAv.problem: Fixed symbolic libraries restrict expressivity, while unrestricted symbolic search wastes effort on physics-violating expressions and receives late behavioral feedback.
tJhJtqVaAv.method: S²GSR encodes symmetry constraints in local expression-graph typing rules and compares completed sub-expressions with position-specific semantic targets. These signals guide neural Monte Carlo tree search over free-form compositions.
tJhJtqVaAv.key_idea: Enforce symmetry through expression types and propagate behavioral targets along expression paths to guide sub-expression search.
tJhJtqVaAv.evidence: Polynomial and non-polynomial symmetry-constrained systems and ODEBench evaluate symbolic recovery and trajectory reconstruction, with symmetry experiments using 100 seeds.
tJhJtqVaAv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate enforcing physical constraints by construction while retaining free-form symbolic search and learned guidance.
tJhJtqVaAv.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty relative to existing symmetry-aware symbolic search and semantic backpropagation.

IeYyISsoBe.one_liner: A music transformer's anticipation stream interleaves performance and score events, with staged training reducing autoregressive exposure bias.
IeYyISsoBe.problem: Rhythm quantization has limited paired training data and accumulates errors during whole-song autoregressive transcription.
IeYyISsoBe.method: The Anticipatory Music Transformer receives performances through its anticipated control stream and learns interleaved performance–score event pairs without adding parameters. A curriculum progresses through teacher forcing, score-token dropout, and DAgger.
IeYyISsoBe.key_idea: Reuse the music model's anticipation mechanism for performance-to-score transcription and progressively expose training to model-generated contexts.
IeYyISsoBe.evidence: The study evaluates 59 ASAP test performances with task-specific baselines and matched controls using random initialization and same-size text-model pretraining.
IeYyISsoBe.claimed_gains: Music pretraining adds 13.80 strict-note F1 points over random initialization and 14.62 over text pretraining; the model reaches 19.68% strict note F1 and 77.72% inter-onset-interval F1 versus 8.96% and 67.81% for the strongest task-specific baseline.
IeYyISsoBe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate parameter-free adaptation and controlled evidence that music-specific pretraining benefits rhythm quantization.
IeYyISsoBe.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the DAgger stage provides enough additional benefit to justify the training pipeline.

KJlx4wRnPJ.one_liner: SDLMs draw semantically related token corruptions from a nonnegative low-rank kernel for tractable posterior-aware revision.
KJlx4wRnPJ.problem: Masking and uniform token replacement discard semantic clues and limit how diffusion language models decide when to revise tokens.
KJlx4wRnPJ.method: SDLMs use a nonnegative low-rank corruption kernel to sample plausible token alternatives and evaluate the exact training loss at linear vocabulary cost. SHARP adds predictor–corrector sampling that reallocates revisions toward tokens likely to change.
KJlx4wRnPJ.key_idea: Factor semantic token-replacement probabilities into a low-rank kernel so revision timing can use the full posterior over related alternatives.
KJlx4wRnPJ.evidence: The paper supplies tractability and revision-timing analyses and generation comparisons against matched MDLM and GIDD baselines.
KJlx4wRnPJ.claimed_gains: SDLM exceeds the MAUVE of matched MDLM and GIDD baselines with 4× fewer steps.
KJlx4wRnPJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the tractable semantic-corruption formulation and strong empirical generation results.
KJlx4wRnPJ.main_concern: Existing ablations do not isolate the value of the specific kernel-construction choices beyond the general low-rank family.

fZtudyugpW.one_liner: An occlusion-derived spatial mixing radius links target geometric scale to the best readout depth in vision transformers.
fZtudyugpW.problem: Using the output block by convention can discard geometry at scales better represented in earlier transformer layers.
fZtudyugpW.method: The study measures a label-free mixing radius from token responses to an occluded input patch and compares it with target ground scale. Layer-wise probes, intermediate blurring, and narrowed late attention test the relationship between mixing and geometric retention.
fZtudyugpW.key_idea: Measure token mixing length through patch occlusion and relate it to target spatial scale to explain depth-dependent geometric retention.
fZtudyugpW.evidence: Experiments span 32 backbones, overhead imagery and indoor photographs, with nine matched-backbone retention comparisons and blur and attention-window interventions.
fZtudyugpW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the extensive empirical study linking optimal feature depth to target spatial scale and the targeted interventions.
fZtudyugpW.main_concern: Reviewers question the generality and applicability boundaries of the scale–depth relationship beyond its strongest overhead-imagery calibration.

LWSqfIC1tr.one_liner: Tracing goal influence through policies distinguishes failures recoverable by activation steering, last-layer rewiring, or neither intervention.
LWSqfIC1tr.problem: Similar goal-misgeneralizing behavior can conceal different failures in how an agent represents and uses the intended goal.
LWSqfIC1tr.method: The study traces goal information through agents and classifies failures by whether policies follow, read, or ignore it. It tests activation steering and retraining only final layers as recoveries matched to those failure depths.
LWSqfIC1tr.key_idea: Diagnose whether goal information guides the policy, influences it without guiding behavior, or remains unused, then test corresponding interventions.
LWSqfIC1tr.evidence: Eight visual navigation and manipulation tasks, including robot control, use representation analysis, steering, rewiring, and matched non-misgeneralizing controls.
LWSqfIC1tr.claimed_gains: Steering raises goal reach from 16.0% to 95.3%, while rewiring raises it from 31.6% to 84.3% in the corresponding failure settings.
LWSqfIC1tr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that goal misgeneralization is an important problem and that mechanistic diagnosis can inform recovery.
LWSqfIC1tr.main_concern: Reviewers raised clarity concerns about terminology and notation, although one reviewer marked the clarity issue addressed.

OkYo9giOg0.one_liner: SSA combines deterministic high-score retrieval with proxy-guided residual sampling and inclusion-probability correction for sparse attention.
OkYo9giOg0.problem: Extreme attention sparsity forces a trade-off between discarded residual mass under retrieval and high variance under sampling.
OkYo9giOg0.method: SSA attends deterministically to high-scoring tokens and samples the remainder using proxy attention scores. Inclusion-probability correction estimates attention mass outside the retrieval set, unifying top-k, top-p, and hybrid selection.
OkYo9giOg0.key_idea: Retain high-score tokens deterministically and estimate residual attention through score-guided samples weighted by inverse inclusion probabilities.
OkYo9giOg0.evidence: Theory and optimized GPU kernels accompany RULER, LongBench, LOFT, and AIME comparisons across five models ranging from 3B to 27B parameters.
OkYo9giOg0.claimed_gains: At 50× sparsity, RULER-HARD accuracy rises from 72.5% to 83.7% at 32K and from 69% to 76.8% at 128K over the strongest baseline.
OkYo9giOg0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the accuracy gains at aggressive sparsity and the combination of theory and multi-model evaluation.
OkYo9giOg0.main_concern: Reviewers agree that matched sparsity and isolated attention timings do not establish end-to-end efficiency against other sparse implementations.

29jmwOC9Gk.one_liner: OSWorld-Pro annotates sequential computer-use subgoals and uses human-aligned judges to expose progress, failure locations, and wasted actions.
29jmwOC9Gk.problem: End-state computer-use evaluation hides how agents fail during long workflows and which capabilities need improvement.
29jmwOC9Gk.method: OSWorld-Pro decomposes tasks into annotated subgoals and uses LLM judges to assess their fulfillment. Its process labels distinguish targeting, feasibility, advancement, and completion to diagnose action failures.
29jmwOC9Gk.key_idea: Score intermediate subgoal progression against human annotations to distinguish process failures hidden by final task-success labels.
29jmwOC9Gk.evidence: The benchmark contains over 300 tasks, over 2800 subgoals, and over 67,000 human annotations, with independent review and coverage of multiple applications and desktops.
29jmwOC9Gk.claimed_gains: Claude Opus 5 achieves 75.7% on OSWorld-Pro versus 83.4% on OSWorld.
29jmwOC9Gk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the substantial annotation effort and diagnostic information beyond final task success.
29jmwOC9Gk.main_concern: Reviewers agree that strict sequential subgoal-targeting rules may penalize valid backtracking, repairs, or alternative execution orders.

4Idj4dQE5E.one_liner: TeleTune edits textual agent skills using offline action-prediction errors and retains edits that improve held-out prediction.
4Idj4dQE5E.problem: User telemetry lacks explicit goals, cannot be replayed for optimization, and may interleave tasks without boundaries.
4Idj4dQE5E.method: TeleTune builds workflows and decision-level skills from offline logs, proposes library edits from action-prediction errors, and accepts edits using held-out prediction accuracy. At inference, it supplies the library and workflow-retrieved demonstrations covering task subgoals.
4Idj4dQE5E.key_idea: Use held-out action prediction as an offline acceptance signal for edits to a textual workflow and skill library.
4Idj4dQE5E.evidence: WorkArena and Online-Mind2Web experiments include live task execution, multiple model backbones, component ablations, and synthetic task interleaving.
4Idj4dQE5E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate learning reusable agent procedures without repeated environment interaction and the live execution evaluations.
4Idj4dQE5E.main_concern: Reviewers agree that successful demonstrations and synthetic interruptions only partially represent noisy, naturally interleaved user telemetry.

Zy6RUiDAl1.one_liner: Nested causal-effect optimization separates finite-sample uncertainty from non-identifiability to inform whether additional observations can resolve decisions.
Zy6RUiDAl1.problem: Causal-effect bounds combine sampling uncertainty with structural non-identifiability without showing whether more observational samples can identify the best action.
Zy6RUiDAl1.method: The framework constructs confidence sets over observational distributions and partitions effect bounds through max-min and min-max optimization. Neural causal models approximate the decomposition to guide action selection and data collection.
Zy6RUiDAl1.key_idea: Intersect and unite causal identified sets across plausible observational distributions using nested max-min and min-max optimization.
Zy6RUiDAl1.evidence: Partial-identification theory and neural causal-model experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets support the proposed uncertainty decomposition.
Zy6RUiDAl1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate connecting causal partial identification with practical decisions about collecting more samples or measuring additional variables.
Zy6RUiDAl1.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the theoretical guarantees and numerical approximations justify claims about uncertainty that additional data cannot remove.

m3fGmzpnqc.one_liner: GFT aligns student and reference activations along answer-loss gradient directions, with student-context KL regularization stabilizing generation.
m3fGmzpnqc.problem: Token-level imitation penalizes alternative reasoning trajectories even when they support the same correct answer.
m3fGmzpnqc.method: GFT replays student and reference reasoning through the same model and uses reference-answer gradients to guide directional activation alignment across decoder layers. KL regularization on student-generated contexts mitigates late-training generation collapse.
m3fGmzpnqc.key_idea: Project student–reference activation differences onto answer-sensitive gradient directions and aggregate alignment losses across decoder layers.
m3fGmzpnqc.evidence: Experiments cover GSM8K, MATH Intermediate Algebra, and MATH Precalculus on Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3-1.7B, and Qwen3-4B.
m3fGmzpnqc.claimed_gains: The best GFT configuration exceeds SFT by 0.8–3.6 percentage points on GSM8K and by 7–33 points on the two MATH subjects.
m3fGmzpnqc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clearly specified same-model replay mechanism and use of reference solutions without an external teacher.
m3fGmzpnqc.main_concern: Reviewers agree that missing matched answer-only supervision baselines prevent isolating the benefit of reference-guided activation alignment.

Ke9xZ8xIbw.one_liner: Diffusion-derived RGB gain-bias transformations adjust lighting while a noise-aware estimate of the input anchors image structure.
Ke9xZ8xIbw.problem: Diffusion-based low-light reconstruction can change scene structure and synthesize details absent from the observed image.
Ke9xZ8xIbw.method: A noise-aware structure estimate is derived from the input, and a short frozen Stable Diffusion trajectory provides a normal-light reference. Global and local RGB gain-bias transformations transfer its photometric statistics, with a globally anchored trust region constraining local corrections.
Ke9xZ8xIbw.key_idea: Projecting diffusion output into RGB gain-bias transformations restricts the generative prior to photometry while rendering from observation-derived structure.
Ke9xZ8xIbw.evidence: LOLv1 enhancement results compare the structure estimate, global regression, spatial trust-region correction, unconstrained local gains, and alternative reference sources.
Ke9xZ8xIbw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the value of separating photometric guidance from structural reconstruction to limit diffusion-induced content changes.
Ke9xZ8xIbw.main_concern: The evidence does not sufficiently establish what reliable photometric information the frozen diffusion prior adds beyond simpler enhancement or reference sources.

ukqlWeHmSb.one_liner: PACS selects diffusion-language-model canvas lengths by predictability and supervises tokens just before confidence-guided revelation.
ukqlWeHmSb.problem: Random-mask SFT mismatches diffusion decoding in both visible reference context and attention-visible generation length.
ukqlWeHmSb.method: PACS uses the model's predictability to choose each example's attention-visible canvas length. It then supervises reference tokens immediately before their confidence-guided revelation along the corresponding trajectory.
ukqlWeHmSb.key_idea: Predictability selects the training canvas and token-supervision timing to match the contexts encountered during confidence-guided decoding.
ukqlWeHmSb.evidence: Reasoning and code-generation benchmarks, including MATH500 and HumanEval, compare SFT methods and analyze context visibility, canvas extent, and compute budgets.
ukqlWeHmSb.claimed_gains: PACS reports gains of up to 12.84 percentage points over vanilla SFT on individual benchmarks and the highest mean accuracy among compared SFT methods.
ukqlWeHmSb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard the decoding-aware training idea as intuitive and well motivated, with reported improvements across benchmarks.
ukqlWeHmSb.main_concern: The canvas-search overhead is substantial, while gains over cheaper alternatives at matched compute are modest or insufficiently established.

oaiiIZuomP.one_liner: Checkpoint comparisons and activation steering diagnose and mitigate answer-content loss triggered by response-form instructions.
oaiiIZuomP.problem: Instruction-tuned models can obey tone or format constraints while losing substantial answer content.
oaiiIZuomP.method: The study tests response-form prompts, including nonrestrictive primers, and compares OLMo post-training stages. It identifies an activation direction whose addition induces collapse and whose subtraction restores content while preserving constraint adherence.
oaiiIZuomP.key_idea: Subtract an activation direction associated with response collapse to recover content under form constraints.
oaiiIZuomP.evidence: Experiments across seven models include controlled prompt ablations, OLMo checkpoint comparisons, and bidirectional activation interventions across two model families.
oaiiIZuomP.claimed_gains: Everyday constraints on tone, formatting, and delivery cut comprehensiveness by up to 45% across seven models.
oaiiIZuomP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the nonrestrictive-prompt collapse results and activation-steering mitigation useful for understanding practical instruction-following failures.
oaiiIZuomP.main_concern: Checkpoint comparisons do not isolate reward objectives sufficiently to support the claimed root-cause attribution.

g8eIA76cUD.one_liner: Repeated training continuations estimate capability-emergence probabilities and guide targeted data interventions from saved checkpoints.
g8eIA76cUD.problem: Scaling laws do not predict whether a particular training run will acquire a capability or whether intervention can change its outcome.
g8eIA76cUD.method: The training committor estimates finite-horizon capability-emergence probability by repeatedly restarting training from a checkpoint. Branches under alternative interventions compare targeted training-data pulses and their durations.
g8eIA76cUD.key_idea: Estimate a checkpoint's finite-horizon capability hitting probability through reseeded training continuations and compare intervention-conditioned branches.
g8eIA76cUD.evidence: Small-transformer tasks and natural-text language-model training compare committor predictions with loss or weight statistics and test capability-aligned data interventions.
g8eIA76cUD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see value in applying the committor concept to training checkpoints and capability emergence.
g8eIA76cUD.main_concern: Unclear presentation of the continuation protocol and estimated probability makes the predictive claims difficult to interpret.

WfQKvcg6Ua.one_liner: A clipped empirical denoiser makes sampling-step sensitivity explicit for certified diffusion privacy accounting.
WfQKvcg6Ua.problem: Neural denoisers have intractable per-example sensitivity, hindering privacy analysis of diffusion sampling.
WfQKvcg6Ua.method: The paper constructs a training-free clipped empirical denoiser whose steps admit Gaussian-mechanism accounting. Privacy-loss distributions certify bounds for full-data or output-wise subsampled sampling, while an Edgeworth approximation provides a diagnostic.
WfQKvcg6Ua.key_idea: Clip an empirical denoiser to bound per-example sensitivity and compose denoising-step privacy losses with a certified accountant.
WfQKvcg6Ua.evidence: Gaussian DP and f-DP analyses support certified privacy-loss-distribution bounds, with generation experiments and comparisons against Edgeworth and central-limit approximations.
WfQKvcg6Ua.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the formal sampling-privacy analysis and careful distinction between certified bounds and approximations.
WfQKvcg6Ua.main_concern: The experiments omit a public-model-only baseline, leaving the contribution of private data to generation quality unclear.

JUgAEHSCri.one_liner: Agent-maintained notes guide selective retrieval from a complete experiment log and update jointly with each proposed program.
JUgAEHSCri.problem: Ancestor-only contexts discard useful discovery evidence, while full experimental histories create long and redundant prompts.
JUgAEHSCri.method: LabBook retains a complete experiment log and a compact memory that guides retrieval and solution generation. One agent combines retrieved evidence with its notes to produce the next program and updated memory.
JUgAEHSCri.key_idea: Keep all experiments in a log while jointly updating compact retrieval-guiding memory and the next candidate program.
JUgAEHSCri.evidence: Evaluation covers 49 Frontier-CS problems with two backbones and nine additional mathematical, systems, and heuristic-design tasks against evolutionary baselines.
JUgAEHSCri.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the simple memory-and-retrieval design and evaluation across diverse tasks and two backbones.
JUgAEHSCri.main_concern: The contribution beyond existing memory-equipped agents remains unclear because close comparisons and decisive component evidence are insufficient.

uLDuoLNj9H.one_liner: Loss-masked informative backstories suppress memorization and preserve in-context learning in transformers trained on toy dynamical systems.
uLDuoLNj9H.problem: Late-stage memorization of training systems can degrade previously acquired in-context learning.
uLDuoLNj9H.method: The paper prepends informative backstories to next-token training examples from interleaved linear dynamical systems and masks the backstory loss. The added context makes original targets predictable in context, reducing incentives to memorize training systems.
uLDuoLNj9H.key_idea: Supply predictive backstory context without supervising its tokens, reducing the incentive to store training-system behavior in model weights.
uLDuoLNj9H.evidence: Toy-world transformer experiments compare masked, unmasked, and uninformative backstories, assess memorization against a pseudoinverse predictor, and test associative recall.
uLDuoLNj9H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the controlled separation of memorization and in-context learning and the demonstrated suppression of late-stage ICL degradation.
uLDuoLNj9H.main_concern: The narrow deterministic toy setting leaves uncertain how the intervention and findings transfer to real language models.

GAcUNDlz0s.one_liner: Soft confidence-weighted position selection isolates decoding-order effects in masked diffusion language models under matched call budgets.
GAcUNDlz0s.problem: Most-confident-first decoding rarely receives controlled comparisons separating position order from token counts and revision.
GAcUNDlz0s.method: The study varies a single confidence-strength parameter from confidence-free selection to hard ranking, separating position selection, time grids, and token revision. It compares quality and diversity under equal model-call budgets.
GAcUNDlz0s.key_idea: Sample commitment positions with adjustable confidence weighting while controlling tokens committed per call and revision.
GAcUNDlz0s.evidence: Two 124M checkpoints and LLaDA-8B-Base are evaluated with GPT-2-large perplexity, bigram diversity, MAUVE, and diversity-matched comparisons.
GAcUNDlz0s.claimed_gains: Soft order lowers scorer perplexity by about 12% at temperature 1.0 and 32 calls on the 124M model and by 11–23% at 16–64 calls on LLaDA-8B-Base, while one-shot revision yields a further 31% reduction with a diversity trade-off.
GAcUNDlz0s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the matched-call controls and separation of selection order, revision, and quality-diversity effects.
GAcUNDlz0s.main_concern: Scorer perplexity and limited practical-model controls do not establish better generation quality in realistic use.

SGGmsRFBIS.one_liner: AxisKV spatially pools distant video-cache states and quantizes recent states according to their different information requirements.
SGGmsRFBIS.problem: Uniform autoregressive-video cache compression ignores the different spatial information requirements of recent and distant temporal positions.
SGGmsRFBIS.method: Persistent, position-matched interventions probe compression, eviction, and cache replacement. AxisKV then collapses distant states spatially while applying quantization to recent states.
SGGmsRFBIS.key_idea: Allocate compression axes by temporal position: pool distant states into spatial summaries and quantize recent states.
SGGmsRFBIS.evidence: Intervention and compression experiments on Self-Forcing and related autoregressive video generators compare AxisKV with matched-memory uniform pooling and quantization.
SGGmsRFBIS.claimed_gains: At 8× cache compression on Self-Forcing, AxisKV outperforms matched-memory uniform pooling and remains usable at 12×, where uniform quantization has no valid operating point.
SGGmsRFBIS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled positional analysis and simple training-free compression strategy.
SGGmsRFBIS.main_concern: The fixed positional allocation generalizes poorly to CausVid, where aesthetic and image quality degrade substantially.

bdTrnsb4Ou.one_liner: CoFiRA allocates calibrated means, variable-sized real KV subsets, or exact attention to video regions according to estimated fidelity needs.
bdTrnsb4Ou.problem: Video-transformer attention remains broadly distributed, limiting sparse selectors and binary exact-versus-summary compensation.
bdTrnsb4Ou.method: CoFiRA estimates regional demand using query-conditioned contribution and within-cluster KV variation, then assigns a calibrated mean, nested real KV representatives, or exact attention. A packed runtime executes variable-capacity routes on device.
bdTrnsb4Ou.key_idea: Assign each attention region a representation capacity using query-conditioned contribution and within-cluster key-value variation.
bdTrnsb4Ou.evidence: HunyuanVideo T2V 13B experiments include comparable-compute representation ablations, allocation controls, and detailed runtime analysis.
bdTrnsb4Ou.claimed_gains: On HunyuanVideo T2V 13B, CoFiRA achieves a 2.27× end-to-end speedup while reaching 33.09 dB PSNR.
bdTrnsb4Ou.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the intermediate representation capacities and experimental support for region-specific allocation.
bdTrnsb4Ou.main_concern: The specific representative-selection rule lacks convincing final-video evidence of an advantage over simpler sampling alternatives.

3ugQho99no.one_liner: GraDiC differentiates gradient-space diversity with respect to response weights to credit underrepresented directions during LLM post-training.
3ugQho99no.problem: Reinforcement-learning post-training can concentrate updates on redundant solution directions and reduce output diversity.
3ugQho99no.method: GraDiC analyzes GRPO through the rollout-gradient Gram matrix and measures gradient coverage with the order-2 Vendi Score. Differentiating that score with respect to response update weights produces closed-form influence scores for credit assignment.
3ugQho99no.key_idea: Reweight verified responses using their marginal contribution to order-2 Vendi diversity of normalized training-gradient directions.
3ugQho99no.evidence: Mathematical-reasoning experiments at two model scales compare diversity-aware baselines and ablate Vendi order and gradient features alongside local first-order analysis.
3ugQho99no.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the mathematical connection between gradient diversity and response-level advantage reweighting.
3ugQho99no.main_concern: The evaluation does not clearly isolate whether the specific gradient-diversity credit rule produces broader reasoning coverage beyond existing methods.

FTvDguvMAE.one_liner: Recovered approximate signature vectors reveal convolutional hyperparameters and channel counts for architecture-agnostic CNN extraction.
FTvDguvMAE.problem: Existing hard-label cryptanalytic CNN extraction requires detailed architectural information unavailable in realistic black-box settings.
FTvDguvMAE.method: The attack infers convolution settings and channel counts from approximate signature vectors, accounts for sequential linear operations, and extends layer recovery to convolution followed by max pooling.
FTvDguvMAE.key_idea: Infer convolutional architecture from patterns in recovered approximate signature vectors rather than requiring it as prior knowledge.
FTvDguvMAE.evidence: Layer-recovery experiments cover small CNNs including LeNet, non-square kernels, pooling, and batch normalization, using true preceding layers and model gradients.
FTvDguvMAE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize reduced architecture assumptions and tests across varied convolution and pooling configurations.
FTvDguvMAE.main_concern: Experiments use privileged gradients and true preceding layers, so they do not demonstrate an end-to-end hard-label black-box attack.

HDeeHC6So7.one_liner: Structured residual sensitivities rank nearby PDE explanations, retain ambiguous sets, and test proposed corrections through independent re-solving.
HDeeHC6So7.problem: A computed PDE field's residual can admit multiple indistinguishable physical explanations that a single diagnosis conceals.
HDeeHC6So7.method: NearestPDE ranks coefficient, source, boundary, and geometry changes using physically scaled residual sensitivities and fits revisions under physical bounds. Split-conformal calibration supplies dictionary-conditional coverage, and independent re-solves test corrections.
HDeeHC6So7.key_idea: Match residuals to structured physical perturbations while retaining indistinguishable explanations as sets and checking corrections by re-solving.
HDeeHC6So7.evidence: Controlled identifiable and collinear cases, matched selector baselines, public-source repairs, and independent one-dimensional transfer re-solves test diagnosis and correction.
HDeeHC6So7.claimed_gains: Re-evaluated tests recover all 1,980 identifiable cases and flag all 240 collinear controls, achieve 92.97% certified acceptance in study B under its 108-rule audit, and improve 1,820/1,824 legacy transfer cases.
HDeeHC6So7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers particularly value retaining ambiguous explanations and validating diagnoses through independent re-solves.
HDeeHC6So7.main_concern: Structured search costs more than OMP without consistently improving diagnosis or correction across regimes.

W9qoaGJdCJ.one_liner: BORDER separates local skill distillation from global experience-guided rollouts and gates supervision to limit interference across task streams.
W9qoaGJdCJ.problem: Agent self-improvement methods developed in homogeneous settings may transfer harmful experience across interleaved domains without labels.
W9qoaGJdCJ.method: BORDER extracts local skills from successful interactions and curates reusable global rules separately from instance details. Verified local skills provide gated on-policy distillation, while global skills guide rollouts whose environment feedback drives RL updates.
W9qoaGJdCJ.key_idea: Route local successful experience into gated token-level distillation and reusable global rules into reinforcement-learning exploration.
W9qoaGJdCJ.evidence: Experiments span two backbones, three benchmarks, and two streaming settings, with component and reduced-data ablations.
W9qoaGJdCJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the decomposition of experience reuse and interference control well motivated and supported by broad main comparisons.
W9qoaGJdCJ.main_concern: Ablations and learning analyses do not sufficiently isolate the mechanisms responsible for transfer gains and generalization losses.

ZdxKV3FJxn.one_liner: Expert-authored financial tasks use weighted derivation rubrics to evaluate auditable research workflows beyond final-answer accuracy.
ZdxKV3FJxn.problem: Finance benchmarks under-measure source choices, assumptions, and calculations needed to audit a financial-research answer.
ZdxKV3FJxn.method: BigFinanceBench pairs open-ended tasks with reference answers and point-weighted rubrics decomposing derivations into independently checkable steps. Partial-credit scoring localizes failures across analyst workflows.
ZdxKV3FJxn.key_idea: Score independently checkable derivation steps with weighted rubrics rather than relying only on final-answer correctness.
ZdxKV3FJxn.evidence: The benchmark contains 928 expert-authored items and 36,241 rubric points, with evaluation of ten frontier and open-weight agents.
ZdxKV3FJxn.claimed_gains: The best evaluated system reaches only 58.8% rubric score.
ZdxKV3FJxn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the auditable-workflow focus and detailed expert-led dataset and rubric construction.
ZdxKV3FJxn.main_concern: Derivation-level scoring needs stronger validation of auditability and robustness to alternative legitimate methodologies.

WUUreagouA.one_liner: Programmatic composition combines verified atomic coding problems into deeper tasks checked by the same verifier used during evaluation.
WUUreagouA.problem: Human curation and model-based generation make coding-benchmark construction expensive.
WUUreagouA.method: CoDepth composes existing verified problems into level-N tasks without language-model generation or validation. It retains a task only when every atomic problem remains unsolved and a joint reference solution passes the evaluation checker.
WUUreagouA.key_idea: Compose verified atomic problems and retain only combinations with unsolved components and a passing joint reference solution.
WUUreagouA.evidence: Experiments cover multi-bug repair, proof completion, complexity analysis, and clone equivalence, plus rejection-sampling fine-tuning of Qwen3.5-9B.
WUUreagouA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple, inexpensive programmatic construction and its applicability across coding domains.
WUUreagouA.main_concern: Missing budget-matched controls leave composition-specific difficulty and training gains confounded with inference or training workload.

r1BBilmoGV.one_liner: Off-GLADIUS minimizes a smoothed, debiased Bellman residual and links optimization error to offline value-estimation error.
r1BBilmoGV.problem: Offline Bellman residual minimization lacks established guarantees connecting optimization convergence to value-function accuracy.
r1BBilmoGV.method: Off-GLADIUS transfers a minimax optimization analysis to offline RL and proves a local metric-subregularity inequality for the soft Bellman fixed point. Under realizability and single-policy concentrability, residual excess risk yields a finite-sample value-error bound.
r1BBilmoGV.key_idea: Combine debiased smoothed Bellman residual minimization with a local residual-to-value inequality under partial data coverage.
r1BBilmoGV.evidence: Convergence and value-error proofs accompany CartPole-v1, Acrobot-v1, LunarLander-v3, and tabular FrozenLake experiments with CQL, OptiDICE, and BRM comparisons.
r1BBilmoGV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the residual-to-value analysis and the simple objective without pessimism penalties, density ratios, or target networks.
r1BBilmoGV.main_concern: Evaluation on small discrete-action control tasks is too narrow to establish broader offline-RL competitiveness and stability.

VXgBbdfD0d.one_liner: A shared road model propagates geometry and friction edits through vehicle dynamics, camera motion, and reconstructed driving scenes.
VXgBbdfD0d.problem: Road edits require corresponding changes in vehicle motion and inter-vehicle clearance to produce coherent driving counterfactuals.
VXgBbdfD0d.method: TerrainForge connects reconstructed scene deformation to four-wheel vehicle dynamics through a unified road representation. It propagates road and friction changes through multi-vehicle episodes and trains a screening surrogate from simulated ego-response outcomes.
VXgBbdfD0d.key_idea: Drive scene deformation and vehicle dynamics with the same edited road representation so motion and camera views respond consistently.
VXgBbdfD0d.evidence: Validation uses CarSim and reconstructed Waymo scenes, multi-vehicle tests across 18 episodes, and 15,758 simulated road edits across 983 braking episodes.
VXgBbdfD0d.claimed_gains: Recomputing surrounding-vehicle responses changes predicted ego–lead distance by median peak differences of 1.52 m for crests and 1.41 m for sags across 18 episodes.
VXgBbdfD0d.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the coherent coupling of road geometry, vehicle response, and rendering.
VXgBbdfD0d.main_concern: Fixed-control playback and ego-only screening labels limit conclusions about realistic multi-vehicle safety outcomes.

hb8ZpFcUzY.one_liner: Learnable latent tokens aggregate utterance-wide audio information into a quantized bottleneck whose selected slots support speech edits.
hb8ZpFcUzY.problem: Frame-aligned audio-codec tokens make global speech attributes difficult to analyze and manipulate.
hb8ZpFcUzY.method: LATTE appends a fixed set of learnable tokens to audio features and retains only those tokens for quantization and decoding. Swapping selected latent positions between utterances changes attributes such as speaker identity or background noise.
hb8ZpFcUzY.key_idea: Quantize globally aggregating latent slots and edit audio by swapping attribute-relevant slots between utterances.
hb8ZpFcUzY.evidence: Low-bitrate speech reconstruction, voice-conversion, and denoising experiments include importance-ranked, random, and least-important slot controls for voice conversion.
hb8ZpFcUzY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value linking latent-slot analysis to actual interventions and the informative matched-budget speaker-editing controls.
hb8ZpFcUzY.main_concern: The editing advantage over existing audio representations remains unproven without matched external baselines and stronger intervention controls.

lxDom0zsmA.one_liner: Behavior-distribution metrics measure how simulated human-partner fidelity changes with web pretraining compute and domain adaptation.
lxDom0zsmA.problem: Plausible LLM simulations can fail to reproduce human behavior patterns needed for effective practice.
lxDom0zsmA.method: The study defines and validates distributional fidelity metrics from behavioral features, then evaluates domain adaptation and scaling with webtext pretraining compute. It compares simulation-fidelity trends with other skill domains.
lxDom0zsmA.key_idea: Compare simulated and human behavioral-feature distributions across pretraining scales and adaptation settings.
lxDom0zsmA.evidence: Two simulation tasks involving user and patient utterances support analyses of fidelity gaps, adaptation, and pretraining-compute scaling.
lxDom0zsmA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard simulation fidelity as a practically important question and value quantitative behavioral evaluation.
lxDom0zsmA.main_concern: Aggregate behavior frequencies can match while responses remain wrong for individual contexts, undermining the metric's claimed conditional fidelity.

tEwr6dq6X9.one_liner: Shared world tokens receive future-video supervision during training and provide the action policy's sole visual-language context.
tEwr6dq6X9.problem: VLA policies lack explicit scene-evolution supervision, while world-action models retain costly video generation during deployment.
tEwr6dq6X9.method: A World Adapter converts VLM features into tokens shared by the action expert and a jointly trained future-video denoiser with only a coarse layout cue. Removing the video branch at deployment retains the trained policy interface.
tEwr6dq6X9.key_idea: Force action prediction and future-video denoising through one shared token interface, then discard the denoiser at deployment.
tEwr6dq6X9.evidence: A 2B backbone without embodied action pretraining is evaluated on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, SIMPLER, and Galaxea R1 Pro manipulation.
tEwr6dq6X9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the shared predictive interface, removal of the video branch at inference, and simulation plus real-world evaluation.
tEwr6dq6X9.main_concern: Matched controls do not sufficiently isolate the benefit of video supervision beyond existing predictive representation learning.

0W6Okvjbxs.one_liner: Formulates multi-turn agent-to-agent privacy extraction as a mixed-motive game where adversarial service agents complete tasks while eliciting protected data.
0W6Okvjbxs.problem: Existing contextual-integrity privacy benchmarks evaluate static single-turn requests, overlooking strategic multi-turn information elicitation during cooperative agent-to-agent interactions.
0W6Okvjbxs.method: The paper introduces a multi-turn benchmark between a User Agent and a Service Agent modeled as a mixed-motive two-player game. Both agents cooperate toward task completion while the adversarial Service Agent strategically negotiates across turns to extract contextually protected user attributes.
0W6Okvjbxs.key_idea: Model multi-turn user-to-service agent dialogue as a mixed-motive game balancing cooperative task completion against adversarial elicitation of contextually protected user data.
0W6Okvjbxs.evidence: Evaluated on a multi-turn User Agent and Service Agent negotiation benchmark built from user requests labeled with required, optional, and protected attributes.
0W6Okvjbxs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling mixed-motive service agents that complete user tasks while collecting unnecessary private data captures a realistic and underexplored agentic privacy threat.
0W6Okvjbxs.main_concern: Counting authorization of required fields as task success does not verify actual service completion, and optimizing attacker prompts separately per conversation length confounds horizon comparisons.

Nav6xykspG.one_liner: Modulates length-related updates in LLM preference post-training using per-context marginal token utility rather than global length suppression.
Nav6xykspG.problem: Preference post-training methods typically penalize or normalize response length globally, ignoring that additional tokens improve quality in some contexts while hurting or adding nothing in others.
Nav6xykspG.method: The authors define marginal token utility to estimate the context-specific quality gain associated with additional response tokens. They integrate this signal into a marginal-utility-guided preference objective that scales length-related learning per context rather than uniformly removing length influence.
Nav6xykspG.key_idea: Estimate context-specific quality gain per additional token and modulate length-related preference optimization updates by this marginal token utility instead of applying global length debiasing.
Nav6xykspG.evidence: Training-data analysis of context-dependent length-quality relationships and experiments across language models and preference-alignment benchmarks against length-debiasing baselines.
Nav6xykspG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find reframing response length from a uniform optimization bias to a context-dependent marginal utility insightful, lightweight, and empirically effective over SamPO.
Nav6xykspG.main_concern: Estimating marginal token utility from only four or five candidate responses per prompt without independent human validation risks capturing reward-model length bias and noisy linear approximations.

x7eAMFALle.one_liner: Models Best-of-N jailbreaking with thermally activated per-prompt safety barriers to extrapolate attack success across prompt, completion, and temperature budgets.
x7eAMFALle.problem: Power-law fits for Best-of-N jailbreaking exhibit drifting exponents, mistake finite-dataset effects for crossovers, and neglect joint dependence on prompt augmentations (N), completions (M), and temperature (T).
x7eAMFALle.method: The paper introduces a physical trap model assigning each prompt a baseline safety level and each augmentation a random thermally activated barrier, characterizing the two-budget (N, M) and temperature attack surface with five interpretable parameters. Fitted on small budgets (N ≤ 100), the model extrapolates attack success rates to larger budgets and unseen temperatures.
x7eAMFALle.key_idea: Parameterize Best-of-N jailbreaking via per-prompt baseline safety levels and random thermally activated augmentation barriers to predict attack success across (N, M, T) budgets.
x7eAMFALle.evidence: Extrapolation experiments from N ≤ 100 to N = 10⁴ across five aligned models, unseen generation temperatures, held-out adversarial prompts, and two automated judges.
x7eAMFALle.claimed_gains: Five fitted parameters collapse five distinct models onto a shared scaling function and extrapolate attack success rates from N ≤ 100 to N = 10⁴ and across unseen temperatures.
x7eAMFALle.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating N and M sampling budgets at the per-prompt level and testing out-of-range budget and temperature extrapolation beyond aggregate power-law curve fitting.
x7eAMFALle.main_concern: Reviewers point to mathematical inconsistencies in the marginal-variance assumptions, unmodeled automated-judge error floors at low jailbreak rates, and limited mechanistic validation beyond one model and prompt set.

SUsOuZ5Opq.one_liner: Extends a Transformer with nested top-k routers so deeper layers process only an exact learned fraction of sequence positions.
SUsOuZ5Opq.problem: Subword tokenizers are trained once separately from language models and cannot adapt compute allocation dynamically across predictable versus informative sequence positions.
SUsOuZ5Opq.method: The Multi-Level Transformer (MLT) pairs a shallow Transformer reading all positions with one or more nested deep levels that process only an exact router-selected fraction ρ of positions via top-k routing, reducing to a dense Transformer at ρ = 1. Trained end-to-end with only the language-modeling objective on raw bytes or tokens, MLT also supports finetuning from pretrained dense Transformers.
SUsOuZ5Opq.key_idea: Route an exact fraction ρ of sequence positions from shallow to nested deeper Transformer layers via learned top-k selection under standard language-modeling supervision.
SUsOuZ5Opq.evidence: Evaluated in two- and three-level architectures across model sizes, languages, raw bytes, subword tokens, DNA sequences (per reviews), and dense-to-MLT finetuning.
SUsOuZ5Opq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the minimal architecture without auxiliary compression-ratio losses and well-controlled ablations spanning multiple domains and languages.
SUsOuZ5Opq.main_concern: Training relies on non-causal top-k routing that leaks future information and mismatches the separate causal router used at inference, while baseline compression settings are adapted to MLT.

o6hj2Tx0h9.one_liner: Guides and verifies inference-time LLM math reasoning using Wikidata concept-DAG scaffolds paired with SymPy and topological membership checks.
o6hj2Tx0h9.problem: LLM mathematical derivations navigate an implicit conceptual space without explicit relational structure, leading to premise drift, calculation errors, and unproductive reasoning branches.
o6hj2Tx0h9.method: TopoMath constructs a directed acyclic graph from Wikidata's mathematical taxonomy and projects each problem onto a compact scaffold of grounded anchors, taxonomic paths, shared ancestors, and local neighbors to guide generation. A dual-verification loop combining SymPy symbolic execution with topological concept-membership checks then flags computational errors and conceptual drift for targeted revision.
o6hj2Tx0h9.key_idea: Project math problems onto a Wikidata concept-DAG scaffold for guided generation, then trigger targeted revision via SymPy symbolic execution and topological neighborhood membership checks.
o6hj2Tx0h9.evidence: Evaluated across six benchmarks from standard to Olympiad-level mathematics and three LLM backbones against direct inference and inference-time reasoning baselines.
o6hj2Tx0h9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the modular, training-free pipeline connecting structured concept graphs with symbolic and conceptual verification across standard and competition math benchmarks.
o6hj2Tx0h9.main_concern: Ablations do not show that gains stem from graph topology rather than extra concept names or multi-sample revision, as removing the scaffold lowers accuracy only slightly.

mqntLSg7p9.one_liner: Recovers stationary moving or rescaled PDE coordinate frames via complexity-regularized typed program search without future trajectory data.
mqntLSg7p9.problem: Accurate PDE field fitting alone fails to uniquely identify canonical moving or rescaled coordinate frames in which solutions become stationary, particularly without future solution trajectories.
mqntLSg7p9.method: Typed frame search jointly fits explicit coordinate-frame and profile programs to PDE residuals and prescribed initial and boundary data using independent validation and frame-complexity regularization. A compositional beam-search extension synthesizes multi-primitive coordinate programs from existing primitives without pre-registering target laws.
mqntLSg7p9.key_idea: Jointly fit typed coordinate-transformation and stationary-profile programs to PDE and initial-boundary constraints with complexity regularization, without observing future trajectories.
mqntLSg7p9.evidence: Conditional identifiability and selection guarantees within a finite candidate bank, plus evaluations on 28 configurations across 14 PDE families (10 seeds), compositional pair/triple structures, unseen profiles, and 2D affine flows.
mqntLSg7p9.claimed_gains: Recovers 96.8% of canonical frames (271/280) with median relative L2 error 1.43 × 10⁻⁶, while beam search recovers 420/420 pair programs in median 2.20 CPU seconds (versus 3.64 seconds for degree-two continuous fitting), 168/180 triple programs (179/180 exhaustively), and all 50 unseen-profile and 60 2D affine frames.
