mqntLSg7p9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value recovering explicit, interpretable coordinate transformations without future trajectories and commend the systematic ablations across diverse PDE families.
mqntLSg7p9.main_concern: Discovery is confined to a hand-crafted transformation grammar tested primarily on synthetic PDEs, with limited evidence of out-of-grammar generalization or downstream numerical-solver benefits.

l6YTxzQgFc.one_liner: Bottom-up text clustering that iteratively applies LLM-selected merge, keep, or recluster operations to fine-grained embedding micro-clusters.
l6YTxzQgFc.problem: Embedding-space text clustering struggles with multi-level semantic granularity, severe cluster-size imbalance, and ambiguous local boundaries.
l6YTxzQgFc.method: LSHC initializes fine-grained micro-clusters in embedding space to preserve small minority clusters and queries an LLM to select among MERGE, KEEP, and RECLUSTER operations on candidate pairs. Iteratively merging similar micro-clusters, keeping distinct neighbors separate, and locally reclustering mixed-semantics clusters produces multi-resolution partitions while curbing upward error propagation.
l6YTxzQgFc.key_idea: Initialize fine-grained embedding micro-clusters and iteratively prompt an LLM to merge, keep separate, or locally recluster candidate pairs across resolutions.
l6YTxzQgFc.evidence: Evaluated across six text clustering benchmarks, including highly imbalanced intent datasets such as Massive-Intent and MTOP-Intent, with RECLUSTER ablations.
l6YTxzQgFc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining scalable embedding-space clustering with local LLM structural operations—especially corrective reclustering—is intuitive and effective on imbalanced datasets like MTOP-Intent.
l6YTxzQgFc.main_concern: Ablations do not separate LLM operation selection from local spectral clustering or center-boundary sampling, and RECLUSTER splits prior clusters in ways that violate strict nested dendrogram hierarchies.

H3ooCxZiAX.one_liner: Automated safety-supervision synthesis pipeline, policy-customizable prompt guardrail models, and fine-grained benchmark for text-to-image moderation.
H3ooCxZiAX.problem: Existing text-to-image safety guardrails require expensive human annotation and remain bound to static safety policies rather than adapting to customizable norms over open-ended visual scenes.
H3ooCxZiAX.method: TIPGuard builds a largely automated synthesis pipeline with targeted human refinement to generate diverse policy-grounded safety supervision for realistic text-to-image prompts and trains deployment-tailored guardrail models. It also introduces TipGuardBench to evaluate multi-category, fine-grained prompt safety judgments across customizable policies.
H3ooCxZiAX.key_idea: Automatically synthesize policy-grounded permitted and prohibited visual-scene prompts with human-in-the-loop policy refinement to train customizable text-to-image prompt guardrails.
H3ooCxZiAX.evidence: Evaluated across TipGuardBench and external safety benchmarks, alongside human-judgment agreement checks on synthesized annotations.
H3ooCxZiAX.claimed_gains: The synthesized text-to-image guardrail dataset achieves 90% agreement between synthetic annotations and human judgments.
H3ooCxZiAX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical focus on policy-customizable text-to-image moderation, explicit permitted-versus-prohibited boundary rules, and the systematic data-synthesis pipeline.
H3ooCxZiAX.main_concern: Evaluations omit essential baselines—including the unadapted base model, the teacher labeler in-context, and prior T2I/policy guards—and only test prompt-label classification rather than end-to-end generated-image safety.

K0bXcwvAWR.one_liner: Trains RL flow policies without target data by regressing velocity fields onto critic action gradients as a fixed-point iteration.
K0bXcwvAWR.problem: Flow-matching policies can represent multimodal Boltzmann optimal distributions in maximum-entropy RL, but standard flow matching requires target action samples unavailable in online RL.
K0bXcwvAWR.method: Fixed-point Flow Matching (FFM) applies a target flow identity to cast actor updates as a data-free fixed-point iteration, regressing the flow velocity field onto critic action gradients evaluated at the policy's own actions. The authors prove that the optimal Boltzmann policy is the unique fixed point of this iteration.
K0bXcwvAWR.key_idea: Regress the flow policy's velocity field onto critic action gradients at policy-sampled actions so fixed-point iteration targets the optimal Boltzmann policy without expert data.
K0bXcwvAWR.evidence: Theoretical proof of unique fixed-point optimality and experiments on online RL from scratch and offline-to-online flow-policy fine-tuning (74 tasks across two settings per reviews).
K0bXcwvAWR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate avoiding sampler backpropagation and adjoint simulation through a clean critic-gradient regression formulation supported by broad multi-task experiments.
K0bXcwvAWR.main_concern: Fixed-point consistency does not establish contraction or convergence from arbitrary policies, and missing target-only ablations leave FFM's advantage over closely related score-matching RL methods (QSM, QAM) unclear.

171jtCccTc.one_liner: Combines sheaf message passing and recurrence to predict protein sequences from molecular dynamics trajectories.
171jtCccTc.problem: Single-backbone inverse folding ignores conformational changes needed to design proteins that undergo specific motions.
171jtCccTc.method: SPINET represents residue interactions with cellular sheaves within each frame, integrates frames recurrently, and predicts all amino acids in one pass.
171jtCccTc.key_idea: Represents each trajectory frame with cellular-sheaf residue interactions and recurrently integrates these representations for sequence prediction.
171jtCccTc.evidence: Evaluations on mdCATH and ATLAS compare static and ensemble baselines and test predicted-sequence structural compatibility against target and decoy conformations.
171jtCccTc.claimed_gains: On mdCATH, SPINET achieves 56.7% top-1 recovery versus 44.5% for the strongest static baseline and 40.7% for the strongest ensemble baseline.
171jtCccTc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that trajectory-conditioned inverse folding is a meaningful extension with strong sequence recovery and useful structural evaluation.
171jtCccTc.main_concern: Reviewers most often note that missing frame-order and matched-input controls leave temporal dynamics' contribution unisolated.

CpPTXbK9Xv.one_liner: Allocates multi-turn RL rollouts through process-scored tree branching, prefix reuse, and conservative path termination.
CpPTXbK9Xv.problem: Uniform independent trajectory sampling wastes multi-turn RL budget on dead ends while underexploring promising intermediate states.
CpPTXbK9Xv.method: PATR scores partial trajectories with task-appropriate process feedback, branches selectively from promising states, reuses prefixes, and stops degenerate paths while remaining compatible with standard policy optimization.
CpPTXbK9Xv.key_idea: Scores partial trajectories with process feedback and selectively branches promising states while reusing prefixes and stopping degenerate paths.
CpPTXbK9Xv.evidence: Experiments on FrozenLake and SWE-Bench include multiple model scales and a Tree-Random control for quality-aware allocation.
CpPTXbK9Xv.claimed_gains: PATR improves performance by up to +5.0 points on SWE-Bench and +9.3 points on FrozenLake.
CpPTXbK9Xv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that process-guided rollout allocation is simple, practical, and compatible with existing GRPO-style optimization.
CpPTXbK9Xv.main_concern: The main concern is that quality-guided branching biases rollout gradients because expanded states are overrepresented and no probability reweighting is applied.

Wyc7yOkk9W.one_liner: Turns online algorithm-configuration trials into reusable edit–response rules through hypothesis-guided local experiments.
Wyc7yOkk9W.problem: Online configuration trials reveal contextual parameter-edit effects that are rarely converted into transferable tuning knowledge under finite budgets.
Wyc7yOkk9W.method: RULER retrieves edit–response rules as hypotheses, reassesses their applicability, plans targeted experiments, and updates supporting or contradicting evidence across problem instances.
Wyc7yOkk9W.key_idea: Distills parameter-edit outcomes into falsifiable, context-dependent edit–response rules that guide subsequent targeted configuration experiments.
Wyc7yOkk9W.evidence: Experiments cover four problem–solver settings under matched evaluation budgets, with additional matched wall-clock comparisons on larger TSP instances.
Wyc7yOkk9W.claimed_gains: RULER reduces the reference gap by an average of 10.7% relative to the strongest baseline under matched evaluation budgets across four problem–solver settings.
Wyc7yOkk9W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicitly accumulating contextual edit–response evidence is a useful mechanism for reusing optimization knowledge.
Wyc7yOkk9W.main_concern: The main concern is that the learned rules and experimental roles may largely recombine existing experience-reuse and LLM-guided optimization techniques.

4Cwy2W8JRB.one_liner: Transfers skill-level supervision to counterfactual observation–instruction pairs for compositional VLA generalization.
4Cwy2W8JRB.problem: Fine-tuned VLAs struggle to recombine demonstrated skills, and counterfactual instruction pairs lack compatible demonstrated action targets.
4Cwy2W8JRB.method: CRAFT holds observations fixed while changing instructed skill combinations and transfers supervision from demonstrated executions through reusable skill representations.
4Cwy2W8JRB.key_idea: Supervises counterfactual instruction pairs with reusable skill representations instead of unavailable observation-specific action targets.
4Cwy2W8JRB.evidence: Experiments span three VLA models, two simulation benchmarks, and a real robot, evaluating demonstrated and undemonstrated skill combinations.
4Cwy2W8JRB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the problem and skill-representation solution are well motivated, with large and consistent compositional-generalization gains.
4Cwy2W8JRB.main_concern: Reviewers most often criticize selecting and reporting checkpoints on the same undemonstrated-combination rollouts, which biases the central generalization result.

V7swqEUYUN.one_liner: Privatizes rare policy switching to attain root-K regret with general value-function approximation.
V7swqEUYUN.problem: It was unknown whether private reinforcement learning with general function approximation can attain the canonical root-K regret rate.
V7swqEUYUN.method: Priv-LazyGOLF applies AboveThreshold to detect Bellman inconsistency and select optimistic feasible hypotheses for finite Bellman-complete classes with bounded Bellman–Eluder dimension.
V7swqEUYUN.key_idea: Uses AboveThreshold both to detect sufficient Bellman inconsistency and to select an optimistic feasible replacement while switching policies rarely.
V7swqEUYUN.evidence: The paper proves joint differential privacy, high-probability regret and switching bounds, and an extension to broader problems with decomposable losses.
V7swqEUYUN.claimed_gains: Priv-LazyGOLF achieves Õ(√K) regret with only logarithmically many policy switches in K under (ε,δ)-joint differential privacy.
V7swqEUYUN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that privately protecting both switching times and hypothesis choices gives a sound improvement over prior private-RL regret rates.
V7swqEUYUN.main_concern: Reviewers most often see the construction as a straightforward combination of known sparse-switching and privacy tools, with limited practical applicability.

j1lPZbMh0Y.one_liner: Learns recurrent graph price policies offline for informative, low-latency iterative combinatorial auctions.
j1lPZbMh0Y.problem: Iterative combinatorial auctions incur costly rounds, while Bayesian one-step pricing requires repeated online inference and can undervalue informative queries.
j1lPZbMh0Y.method: FastCombo formulates single-minded auction clearing as a POMDP and trains a recurrent bidder–item graph policy over complete trajectories for single-pass online price updates.
j1lPZbMh0Y.key_idea: Assigns credit to price queries for future decisions they enable, replacing online Bayesian optimization with one neural-network forward pass.
j1lPZbMh0Y.evidence: Evaluation includes a controlled one-item experiment and four Combinatorial Auction Test Suite domains with multiple training seeds and paired statistical protocols.
j1lPZbMh0Y.claimed_gains: In a one-item experiment, all five trained policies reduce expected rounds from 1.85 to 1.65 relative to the tested Bayesian one-step rule.
j1lPZbMh0Y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the theory cleanly motivates informative queries and that the learned opening and online computational savings are carefully evaluated.
j1lPZbMh0Y.main_concern: Reviewers most often note that FastCombo does not reduce rounds on CATS, where Bayesian pricing uses fewer rounds in three of four domains.

Vo56I4M3eF.one_liner: Learns review-criticism checklists whose granularity maximizes correlated reviewer agreement to reduce lottery error.
Vo56I4M3eF.problem: Small review committees can miss issues that a larger eligible reviewer pool would raise, producing reviewer lottery error.
Vo56I4M3eF.method: An LLM-assisted pipeline builds a tree of coarsened atomic review claims and selects the checklist granularity that maximizes theoretically motivated correlated agreement.
Vo56I4M3eF.key_idea: Selects a coarsening of atomic review claims by maximizing theoretically motivated correlated agreement among reviewers.
Vo56I4M3eF.evidence: The method is tested with LLM-simulated reviews on NeurIPS 2021 and ICLR 2022 data and a human study with 20 participants.
Vo56I4M3eF.claimed_gains: The checklist reduces three-reviewer MSE by 58% on NeurIPS and 21% on ICLR in LLM simulations, and lowers human-study ranking MSE from 0.48 to 0.22.
Vo56I4M3eF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learned checklists address an important problem through a systematic framework evaluated in both simulations and a human study.
Vo56I4M3eF.main_concern: Reviewers most often warn that checklist benefits are confounded by allowing reviewers to consider more issues or spend more effort.

X6nNsGtNkW.one_liner: Predicts team-level quality and cost offline, then routes optimal-transport candidates under runtime constraints.
X6nNsGtNkW.problem: Individual-agent suitability does not capture complementarity, redundancy, and team-size effects in multi-agent reasoning.
X6nNsGtNkW.method: TeamRoute's Experience Brain models role, pairwise, and cardinality factors, while its Rational Scheduler generates transport-guided candidates and applies the frozen predictor under budgets and quality tolerances.
X6nNsGtNkW.key_idea: Decodes context-dependent role, pairwise, and cardinality factors into team quality and resource estimates for frozen-predictor routing.
X6nNsGtNkW.evidence: Experiments across diverse reasoning benchmarks include structured-predictor ablations, unseen team combinations, transport-guided generation, and a conditional quality-loss analysis.
X6nNsGtNkW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating offline team-outcome learning from constraint-aware runtime routing is sensible and supported by targeted ablations.
X6nNsGtNkW.main_concern: Reviewers most often question whether routing drives the gains, citing unmatched baselines, strong fixed-team results, and missing realized cost measurements.

UpBrIKHuk1.one_liner: Learns controllers and Lyapunov certificates offline with finite-sample decrease guarantees or explicit refusal.
UpBrIKHuk1.problem: It is unclear how many offline expert demonstrations are needed to certify a learned controller's decrease behavior on an unknown true system.
UpBrIKHuk1.method: For control-affine systems, the method jointly learns a Lyapunov certificate and drift predictor, synthesizes feedback with a soft CLF-QP, and uses a one-sided warning with encounter-coverage assumptions.
UpBrIKHuk1.key_idea: Penalizes expert decrease deficits and harmful directional drift errors to bound true-system certificate violations from one offline batch.
UpBrIKHuk1.evidence: The paper derives finite-sample bounds, matching minimax dependence on a constructed family, and impossibility results for inferring positive coverage from expert data.
UpBrIKHuk1.claimed_gains: For fixed certificate and affine predictor classes, the bound scales as 1/(ν_enc N) at zero effective warning slack.
UpBrIKHuk1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the directional warning and finite-sample analysis are technically careful and target an interesting certified-deployment problem.
UpBrIKHuk1.main_concern: Reviewers most often emphasize that the deployment bound depends on unverifiable encounter coverage, making offline certificates vacuous without external information.

TurDIcpW2S.one_liner: Compiles unseen temporal-logic specifications into fixed linear decoders over predictive state representations for zero-shot runtime monitoring.
TurDIcpW2S.problem: Autonomously deployed vision and VLA policies need runtime safety monitors that generalize zero-shot to new formal properties without retraining or horizon-exponential cost.
TurDIcpW2S.method: The monitor learns a single predictive state representation (PSR) capturing probabilities of short candidate futures given observation history. At runtime, any temporal-logic formula is compiled from its syntax into a fixed weight vector, turning monitoring into a constant-cost inner product independent of formula horizon.
TurDIcpW2S.key_idea: Compiles temporal-logic formulas into fixed linear readout vectors over a learned predictive state representation, enabling constant-time zero-shot runtime monitoring.
TurDIcpW2S.evidence: Theoretical certification bounds and empirical comparisons against autoregressive monitors across multiple sensor modalities.
TurDIcpW2S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the separation between a single learned predictive representation and a syntax-compiled constant-cost monitor for unseen STL specifications.
TurDIcpW2S.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the linearity/span assumption of PSR operators holds under repeated composition in practice and note unclear novelty over combining linear PSRs with formula progression.

8ccQY4vhzc.one_liner: Learns stack-stability state representations by testing them against simulated physical perturbations during training.
8ccQY4vhzc.problem: Physics simulators require unavailable parameters like friction coefficients to assess stack stability, while visual classifiers predict binary labels without modeling how failures unfold.
8ccQY4vhzc.method: StackProbe learns a state representation from images and records by testing it under varied physical perturbations and supervising responses against high-fidelity simulator outcomes during training. At inference, it predicts whether, when, and how a stack will fail without running a simulator.
8ccQY4vhzc.key_idea: Supervises learned visual state representations during training via continuation testing under simulated physical perturbations to predict failure occurrence, timing, and mode.
8ccQY4vhzc.evidence: Evaluated on two simulation benchmarks and data from a deployed industrial palletizing system, plus theoretical bounds and continuation-testing ablations.
8ccQY4vhzc.claimed_gains: StackProbe reduces missed-failure rates by over 32% compared with the strongest learned baseline and improves industrial collapse prediction average precision by at least 6.0 percentage points.
8ccQY4vhzc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that physically grounded continuation-testing supervision is well validated by controls and theory for failure-aware state learning.
8ccQY4vhzc.main_concern: Reviewers note that the real-world industrial evaluation only tests terminal collapse via frozen features rather than perturbation responses, and question novelty relative to prior temporal-consistency methods.

RuS19L6RIE.one_liner: Shows two-layer transformers converge to single-layer or two-layer sorting algorithms based on initialization, with only the latter length-generalizing.
RuS19L6RIE.problem: Two-layer transformers trained to near-zero loss on fixed-length sorting exhibit drastically different length-generalization behaviors that training performance alone cannot predict.
RuS19L6RIE.method: The authors analyze two-layer, one-head transformers trained on sorting and minimum-finding, steering convergence between single-attention and two-attention-layer solutions via weight initialization. They identify rare input patterns whose frequency grows with sequence length as the driver of the generalization gap.
RuS19L6RIE.key_idea: Uses controlled weight initialization to steer two-layer transformers between single-layer and two-layer algorithmic circuits and analyzes their behavior on length-dependent rare inputs.
RuS19L6RIE.evidence: Supported by controlled initialization experiments and targeted interventions on sorting, minimum-finding, and coin-denomination tasks in small transformers.
RuS19L6RIE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that demonstrating how initialization selects between distinct internal algorithms with opposite length-generalization patterns is an insightful challenge to simplicity bias.
RuS19L6RIE.main_concern: Reviewers note the study is limited to toy two-layer, single-head setups on synthetic sorting tasks and relies on indirect visualizations rather than direct weight-level mechanistic proofs.

N6NJJ8TPda.one_liner: Fine-tunes distilled autoregressive video generators on their own adversarial rollouts using a frozen self-teacher.
N6NJJ8TPda.problem: Autoregressive video generators propagate small input-image perturbations across long horizons, degrading later frames.
N6NJJ8TPda.method: The authors propose teacher-guided on-policy adversarial fine-tuning using an efficient attack surrogate to generate adversarial rollouts during training. A frozen self-teacher with clean-image access provides corrective supervision along the student's rollouts, with regularization to preserve clean generation quality and zero added inference cost.
N6NJJ8TPda.key_idea: A frozen self-teacher supervises the student's own adversarial rollouts to suppress long-horizon perturbation propagation without changing inference cost.
N6NJJ8TPda.evidence: Evaluations use white-box PGD attacks (PGD20, PGD40, late-block PGD10) and VBench-I2V on a distilled autoregressive video model.
N6NJJ8TPda.claimed_gains: Reduces mean latent perturbation response by 22.3-31.4% overall and 14.5% in late frames under late-targeting attacks, with near-unchanged clean VBench-I2V scores.
N6NJJ8TPda.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the evaluation protocol is unusually thorough, testing white-box adaptive and late-block attacks on a fixed confirmation set.
N6NJJ8TPda.main_concern: Reviewers question the dual-use threat model (weakening protective anti-animation perturbations) and note significant clean-input drift alongside single-model scope.

AbBdbGsUXQ.one_liner: Proposes CALIPER, using unlabelled clean reference data to estimate feature variation and selectively correct embeddings under product shift.
AbBdbGsUXQ.problem: Frozen foundation models lose accuracy under sensor or processing product shifts, while existing test-time adaptation methods often introduce errors on unaffected images.
AbBdbGsUXQ.method: The authors analyze product shifts on satellite imagery and introduce CALIPER, which uses unlabelled clean reference data to estimate expected feature variation and decide whether and how much to correct each embedding while keeping the encoder and classifier fixed. They evaluate CALIPER alongside 13 test-time adaptation methods across eight encoders.
AbBdbGsUXQ.key_idea: Estimating expected feature variation from unlabelled clean reference data gates and scales per-embedding corrections so unaffected inputs remain undisturbed.
AbBdbGsUXQ.evidence: Experiments across eight encoders on m-EuroSAT and m-BigEarthNet under synthetic degradations and real Level-1C vs. Level-2A Sentinel-2 atmospheric correction shifts.
AbBdbGsUXQ.claimed_gains: CALIPER recovers 46% of accuracy lost to synthetic degradations on m-EuroSAT (versus 35% for PEA among 13 TTA baselines) and 18% of micro-F1 loss under real Level-1C shift.
AbBdbGsUXQ.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers value the practical problem framing and the clean evaluation methodology that separately tracks fixed errors and newly introduced overturns.
AbBdbGsUXQ.main_concern: Reviewers criticize untuned baseline hyperparameters (leaving methods like SAR, EATA, and TCA nearly inactive) and modest gains on real Level-1C shifts compared to synthetic degradations.

00EdGSSJO6.one_liner: Interpolates pretrained heuristic decisions with a safe reference rule via a feasibility calibrator for chance-constrained contextual optimization.
00EdGSSJO6.problem: Directly enforcing chance constraints in contextual optimization often incurs a steep optimality loss to achieve statistical feasibility.
00EdGSSJO6.method: The authors propose a pretrain-then-calibrate framework that takes any pretrained heuristic decision rule and interpolates it with an almost-surely feasible reference rule using a model-agnostic feasibility calibrator (instantiated with conformal, DKW, and Gaussian schemes) to obtain finite-sample feasibility and optimality guarantees.
00EdGSSJO6.key_idea: Calibrating a one-dimensional interpolation between a pretrained decision rule and a safe reference rule provides model-agnostic chance-constraint feasibility without retraining.
00EdGSSJO6.evidence: Theoretical feasibility guarantees for four calibrators and empirical evaluations on synthetic and real-world contextual optimization tasks.
00EdGSSJO6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the pretrain-then-calibrate interpolation framework simple, modular, computationally light, and practically effective at reducing constraint violations.
00EdGSSJO6.main_concern: Reviewers note incremental theoretical novelty over existing conformal/DKW calibration, potential conservatism from requiring a known always-feasible reference rule, and incomplete optimality-feasibility frontier comparisons.

Cb53xcJeBc.one_liner: Evaluates formal statement equivalence in Lean 4 via SemantEq by auditing proof terms for restricted chains of allowed rewrites.
Cb53xcJeBc.problem: Full logical equivalence trivially holds between any two provable mathematical statements (P <-> True <-> Q), making it unreliable for evaluating autoformalization.
Cb53xcJeBc.method: The authors introduce SemantEq, a relation requiring statements to transform into each other only through allowed logical rearrangements and library equation rewrites, audited directly on Lean 4 proof terms rather than tactic scripts, with both search-based (SemantEq-Eval) and LLM-assisted (SemantEq-ProofAudit) variants.
Cb53xcJeBc.key_idea: Auditing elaborated Lean 4 proof terms for chains of restricted logical and definitional rewrite bridges prevents provers from exploiting P <-> True <-> Q.
Cb53xcJeBc.evidence: Evaluations on the ProofNetVerif test split with adjudicated labels and adversarial non-equivalent pairs comparing against BEq+.
Cb53xcJeBc.claimed_gains: SemantEq-Eval reaches 100% precision and 65.6% recall on ProofNetVerif under adjudicated labels, compared with 95.8% precision and 61.8% recall for BEq+.
Cb53xcJeBc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper tackles a real flaw in logical-equivalence autoformalization metrics and praise the detailed Lean 4 proof-term audit.
Cb53xcJeBc.main_concern: Reviewers note that bridge admissibility lacks formal semantic justification, SemantEq still requires reference formalizations and isn't tested in an RL loop, and closely related works (LeanScorer, ASSESS) are missing.

9zOmf1SpFD.one_liner: Shows network depth improves training-time scaling exponents on spectrally difficult tasks via predictor-norm growth in deep linear networks.
9zOmf1SpFD.problem: Whether increasing network depth can improve training-time neural scaling exponents has remained theoretically unsettled.
9zOmf1SpFD.method: By analyzing gradient flow in deep linear networks and reparameterizing time by the predictor norm, the authors classify when depth improves asymptotic training-time scaling exponents versus leaving them invariant.
9zOmf1SpFD.key_idea: Reparameterizes training time by predictor-norm growth to show that depth accelerates effective learning rates only on spectrally difficult tasks where the target norm diverges.
9zOmf1SpFD.evidence: Closed-form theoretical analysis of deep linear networks under squared loss, complemented by numerical experiments on image-derived and nonlinear ReLU tasks.
9zOmf1SpFD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the precise theoretical classification and the predictor-norm time reparameterization resolving prior disagreements.
9zOmf1SpFD.main_concern: Reviewers note that continuous-time gradient flow on linear networks ignores discrete-time learning-rate stability limits and provides only thin qualitative evidence for nonlinear networks.

Vj7w5LiBae.one_liner: Introduces a same-particle operando microscopy benchmark testing whether learned battery dynamics transfer across charging rates and temperatures.
Vj7w5LiBae.problem: Machine-learned physical simulators are rarely tested under operating-condition shifts with particle identity held fixed.
Vj7w5LiBae.method: The authors collect 544 hours of operando optical microscopy movies (527 new) tracking 22 graphite particles across rates and temperatures plus 24 published NMC cathode particles. They evaluate forecasters stepping in time versus stepping in charge passed.
Vj7w5LiBae.key_idea: Benchmarks distribution-shift transfer with fixed particle identity using same-particle operando microscopy movies and tests charge-stepped versus time-stepped forecasting.
Vj7w5LiBae.evidence: Paired particle-level evaluations on 22 graphite particles and 24 NMC particles against same-particle replay and mean baselines.
Vj7w5LiBae.claimed_gains: In graphite, stepping in charge passed yields a skill gain of 0.42 at short horizons and 0.51 at long horizons.
Vj7w5LiBae.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the scarce same-particle operando dataset and careful paired evaluation with strong baselines.
Vj7w5LiBae.main_concern: Reviewers note confounding between charging rate and cell history in the single-cell graphite recordings, heavy reliance on 100+ pages of appendices, and unclear downstream utility of image forecasting.

duV1JcuVSM.one_liner: Represents task fine-tuning updates as coordinates in fixed bases derived from the pretrained model's weights.
duV1JcuVSM.problem: Independent parameter updates from fine-tuning lack a shared, interpretable representation space for comparing and composing task behaviors.
duV1JcuVSM.method: MODEM expresses parameter updates in fixed singular bases of the pretrained weights, analyzing adaptation fidelity, relational geometry, and path-aware task composition.
duV1JcuVSM.key_idea: Parameterize task fine-tuning updates as small trainable matrices between fixed singular bases of the pretrained model weights.
duV1JcuVSM.evidence: Studies include a controlled MNIST generation experiment, ViT image classification, and GPT-2 NLP evaluations.
duV1JcuVSM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framing of model updates as an interpretable, composable embedding space interesting.
duV1JcuVSM.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing comparisons and citations to identical fixed-basis parameterizations like SVFT and LoRA-XS, plus weak empirical advantages over full fine-tuning.

eQTM6f4X17.one_liner: Adapts a pretrained ECG world model with a differentiable soft-segmentation clinical measurement loss for text-to-ECG synthesis.
eQTM6f4X17.problem: Text-to-ECG generators produce plausible waveforms that miss subtle diagnostic morphologies and clinical measurements.
eQTM6f4X17.method: CARP adapts a pretrained ECG world model using rectified-flow training augmented with a differentiable soft-segmentation loss aligning clinical waveform measurements between generated and target ECGs.
eQTM6f4X17.key_idea: Supervise rectified-flow ECG generation from a pretrained world model with a differentiable soft-segmentation loss over clinical waveform measurements.
eQTM6f4X17.evidence: Evaluations span MIMIC-IV-ECG, external PTB-XL and HEEDB datasets, and downstream rare-condition data augmentation.
eQTM6f4X17.claimed_gains: Across MIMIC-IV-ECG, PTB-XL, and HEEDB, CARP has the lowest error on 21/24 clinical measurements, and ablations show that without world model pretraining, real-to-synthetic AUPRC falls 55.2%.
eQTM6f4X17.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clinically targeted measurement loss and strong out-of-domain downstream utility for rare ECG conditions.
eQTM6f4X17.main_concern: Reviewers note that the pretraining ablation (8 vs. 32 epochs) confounds world-model priors with optimization budget, and one reviewer flagged discrepancies in the anonymous code repository.

4xD7zNm38e.one_liner: Trains individualized LLM student simulators via pooled domain training followed by per-student LoRA specialization.
4xD7zNm38e.problem: Existing student models either track state without responding to natural-language guidance or prompt LLMs that fail to mimic individual student errors.
4xD7zNm38e.method: StudentSim performs two-stage training (pooled domain SFT then per-student specialization) on sparse learner records and introduces StudentSimEval measuring behavioral fidelity (F) and guidance responsiveness (R).
4xD7zNm38e.key_idea: Combine pooled domain fine-tuning with per-student LoRA specialization to model both individual error patterns and responses to tutor guidance.
4xD7zNm38e.evidence: Evaluations cover 60 real students across chess, L2 English writing, and mathematics, plus a downstream RL tutor training experiment.
4xD7zNm38e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the 60-student multi-domain dataset and the closed-loop downstream RL tutor experiment.
4xD7zNm38e.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty beyond two-stage LoRA personalization and point out that the R metric measures reaching canonical answers rather than student-specific guidance responses.

ZxSqNLKyhH.one_liner: Introduces an ordered multi-goal continuous VLN benchmark and a flow-proposer plus latent world-model VLM controller.
ZxSqNLKyhH.problem: Existing continuous vision-and-language navigation (VLN) benchmarks focus on single-goal route following rather than intent-driven, multi-stage household errands with ordered landmarks.
ZxSqNLKyhH.method: ErrandVLN pairs 65,134 continuous trajectories across 913 Isaac Sim scenes with 502,233 role-conditioned instructions and unseen splits. VLN-JEPA combines a continuous trajectory proposer (TP-Flow), an action-conditioned latent world model (NaviLat) predicting future latents without pixel decoding, and a 2.35B VLM controller.
ZxSqNLKyhH.key_idea: Pairs a continuous multi-stop navigation benchmark with a controller that scores flow-proposed trajectories via action-conditioned JEPA latent rollouts without pixel decoding.
ZxSqNLKyhH.evidence: Evaluated on ErrandVLN unseen splits and transferred to R2R-CE (augmenting JanusVLN), with ablations.
ZxSqNLKyhH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the large-scale continuous multi-goal VLN benchmark with unseen scene, path, and instruction-style splits to be a useful evaluation resource.
ZxSqNLKyhH.main_concern: Reviewers point out unmatched baseline comparisons (fine-tuned VLN-JEPA vs. zero-shot baselines, depth vs. RGB) and lack of evidence that role-conditioned phrasing adds reasoning difficulty.

mtqSFJTgJC.one_liner: Encodes single-cell transcriptomes as discrete programme-axis states via factorized vector quantization and additive gene-resolved decoding.
mtqSFJTgJC.problem: Single-cell latent models trade off preserving fine-grained cellular variation against providing biologically interpretable gene-programme representations.
mtqSFJTgJC.method: LEXA combines programme-factorized vector quantization with scaffold-guided gene responsibility and an additive gene-resolved decoder so each cell selects one discrete state per programme axis.
mtqSFJTgJC.key_idea: Pairs programme-factorized discrete codebooks with scaffold-guided gene assignments and additive gene-resolved decoding.
mtqSFJTgJC.evidence: Pretraining on CELLxGENE and evaluations on held-out PBMC datasets and an external COVID-19 cohort against continuous, discrete, and gene-programme baselines.
mtqSFJTgJC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the discrete programme-state formulation conceptually interesting and appreciate the broad evaluation of retention, interpretability, and stability.
mtqSFJTgJC.main_concern: It is unclear whether discretization improves biological interpretability over continuous programme models, and cell-type classification trails continuous baselines.

LQfh4VMUAM.one_liner: Distills geospatial models into Matryoshka-nested coordinate embeddings with a chunked penalty for post-training spatial scale adjustment.
LQfh4VMUAM.problem: Geographic implicit neural representations are mainly tested on random holdouts, obscuring their failure to generalize spatially far from labeled observations.
LQfh4VMUAM.method: MIND distills multiple pretrained geospatial models into contiguous nested embedding chunks ordered from coarse to fine spatial variation, allowing downstream models to truncate chunks or apply a Chunked Penalty without retraining. CoordBench pairs this with 52 datasets and 78 targets across random and regional holdouts.
LQfh4VMUAM.key_idea: Uses Matryoshka-nested multi-teacher distillation and a Chunked Penalty to tune the spatial smoothness of coordinate-only geographic embeddings at test time.
LQfh4VMUAM.evidence: Evaluated on CoordBench (52 datasets, 78 targets) under random, regional, and buffered-exclusion spatial holdouts.
LQfh4VMUAM.claimed_gains: MIND with the Chunked Penalty achieves the highest aggregate regression and classification performance among tested INRs (exact numbers not stated in abstract).
LQfh4VMUAM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the CoordBench spatial-split benchmark and the practical problem of adjusting geospatial embedding granularity.
LQfh4VMUAM.main_concern: Reviewers note that teacher AEF is excluded from baseline and concatenation controls, raising attribution and leakage concerns, and request a truncated PCA baseline.

kSIb3I524l.one_liner: Measures finite-distance neighborhood loss return (critical sharpness) along reference-model gradients for black-box membership inference.
kSIb3I524l.problem: Existing membership inference attacks evaluate loss or Hessian curvature only at the input example, missing neighborhood loss-geometry signals.
kSIb3I524l.method: SharpMIA defines critical sharpness as the distance one must walk from an example before the loss returns to its initial value. To enable offline black-box attacks without target gradients, it approximates the walking direction by averaging gradients from reference models trained without the target sample and fuses the score with Hessian curvature.
kSIb3I524l.key_idea: Approximates finite-distance neighborhood loss-return distance using reference-model gradient directions for offline black-box membership inference.
kSIb3I524l.evidence: Evaluated on vision benchmarks including CIFAR-100 against 11 baseline attacks, plus white-box vs. black-box correlation checks.
kSIb3I524l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that neighborhood critical sharpness and its reference-gradient black-box approximation (Spearman 0.978-0.990) are interesting and well tested.
kSIb3I524l.main_concern: Reviewers note critical sharpness underperforms Hessian trace standalone and lacks controlled ablations isolating its contribution from calibration and combiner components.

foulTd1ZUb.one_liner: Learns a Doob h-function from binary clean-sample evaluations to guide frozen diffusion models toward hard constraints.
foulTd1ZUb.problem: Existing constrained diffusion guidance methods require differentiable measurement operators, paired conditional data, or per-step rollouts of the base model.
foulTd1ZUb.method: The method trains a lightweight head per constraint via squared-error regression on forward-noised binary labels to estimate the Doob h-function (probability a noisy sample denoises into the constraint set). Its gradient provides exact guidance without normalizing step sizes across samples.
foulTd1ZUb.key_idea: Estimates the Doob h-function via squared-error regression on forward-noised binary evaluations of clean samples and uses its unnormalized log-gradient for guidance.
foulTd1ZUb.evidence: Evaluated on CIFAR-10 class/attribute constraints, QM9 molecular property filters, and Stable Diffusion 1.5, plus a matched-budget ablation comparing unnormalized vs. equalized steps.
foulTd1ZUb.claimed_gains: Equalizing step sizes costs 17.0 to 18.5 satisfaction points on CIFAR-10; guidance is >50x cheaper than rejection sampling at 1.7% base rate, raises QM9 Lipinski satisfaction from 54.3% to 96.8%, and lifts Stable Diffusion 1.5 from 7.2% to 60.0%.
foulTd1ZUb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Doob h-transform formulation is theoretically coherent and yields low-cost inference.
foulTd1ZUb.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over standard noisy-state classifier guidance and overly simple experimental constraints (such as digit/class labels and basic filters).

Ktya9054vX.one_liner: Trains LLMs with hardware-in-the-loop RL and anti-hacking verification on Snapdragon Adreno GPUs to optimize OpenCL kernels.
Ktya9054vX.problem: LLM kernel optimization benchmarks and RL environments focus heavily on NVIDIA CUDA, lacking executable verification and noisy-device protocols for mobile OpenCL GPUs.
Ktya9054vX.method: The authors release OpenCLKernelBench (100 tasks) and OpenCLOC (620 GitHub kernels) with test cases and host code, and train Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct via hardware-in-the-loop RLVR using device-noise mitigation and reward-hacking checks on Adreno GPUs.
Ktya9054vX.key_idea: Combines executable OpenCL benchmarks with hardware-in-the-loop RLVR, interleaved timing noise reduction, and no-op/copy reward-hacking checks on mobile GPUs.
Ktya9054vX.evidence: Trained and evaluated on Snapdragon Adreno mobile GPUs starting from Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct.
Ktya9054vX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the OpenCL datasets, execution verification infrastructure, and practical focus on mobile GPU kernel optimization.
Ktya9054vX.main_concern: The paper lacks ablations isolating the noise/anti-hacking interventions, omits comparisons to SFT/best-of-N or frontier models, and shows limited cross-device transfer.

VXVNeA9o6K.one_liner: Tracing root observation, hypothesis preference, and final selection reveals how non-root competition disrupts agentic incident diagnosis.
VXVNeA9o6K.problem: Final-answer accuracy cannot show whether RCA agents retrieve root telemetry, consider the root, favor it, or lose it among plausible alternatives.
VXVNeA9o6K.method: The study aligns incident-side signal conditions with retrieved telemetry, diagnostic states, and final answers across OpenRCA trajectories. It then evaluates three targeted agent designs intended to reduce interference from competing non-root signals.
VXVNeA9o6K.key_idea: Separating root observation from cross-hypothesis preference and final selection localizes where diagnostic trajectories diverge under partial observability.
VXVNeA9o6K.evidence: The analysis covers 335 OpenRCA queries, and three targeted agent designs are evaluated on 22 queries.
VXVNeA9o6K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the finer-grained diagnostic-state analysis clarifies RCA failures beyond final accuracy and motivates designs against non-root interference.
VXVNeA9o6K.main_concern: Reviewers find the three agent designs too heuristic and insufficiently evaluated to establish general improvements or a strong partial-observability contribution.

rDUtl0qhQA.one_liner: WUIRL reconstructs wildfire building-ignition pathways by pairing a PPO pathway-selection policy with a physical ignition model.
rDUtl0qhQA.problem: Static damage-prediction models cannot reconstruct the unrecorded temporal pathways by which wildfires expose and ignite buildings in the wildland–urban interface.
rDUtl0qhQA.method: Wildland–Urban Interface Reinforcement Learning (WUIRL) decouples route selection from combustion physics: a PPO policy selects heat-exposure pathways from burning vegetation, neighboring structures, and external sources, while a physical ignition model determines each building's response.
rDUtl0qhQA.key_idea: Pairs a PPO policy that selects sequential heat-exposure pathways with a fixed physical ignition simulator to reconstruct building ignition trajectories.
rDUtl0qhQA.evidence: Evaluated on wildfire reconstruction against Random and Greedy baselines using final damage and coarse timing observations.
rDUtl0qhQA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the distinctive sequential formulation that decouples RL pathway selection from a transparent physical ignition model.
rDUtl0qhQA.main_concern: Reconstructed ignition pathways cannot be directly validated due to non-identifiability from final damage data, and baselines are restricted to Random and Greedy.

d1pmSSrhf2.one_liner: EVALBENCH separates target identifiability, static score–error ranking (M1), and active PDE program-search error (M2) with risk certificates.
d1pmSSrhf2.problem: Reference-free scores for PDE program search are commonly judged on fixed candidate banks, which may not predict whether they improve solutions during active search.
d1pmSSrhf2.method: EVALBENCH evaluates reference-free PDE scores across three stages—identifiability, static rank agreement (M1), and active-search error (M2)—under fixed proposers/fitters and distribution shifts, alongside conditional transfer bounds and simultaneous risk certificates.
d1pmSSrhf2.key_idea: Decouples specification identifiability, static score–error ranking, and active-search program error in a controlled PDE benchmark with calibrated risk certificates.
d1pmSSrhf2.evidence: Experiments across seven identifiable 1D PDE targets, a Keller–Segel scale-family control, a ten-operator development study, and theoretical transfer/risk bounds.
d1pmSSrhf2.claimed_gains: Five combined or resampled scores reach median Spearman M1 of 0.813–0.817 versus 0.417 for raw residual, while held-out scoring yields a median paired log10 error ratio of -0.0036 (95% CI [-0.032, 0.003]) in active search against the 0.817-M1 baseline.
d1pmSSrhf2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the three-stage decomposition, rigorous paired-seed methodology, and transparent reporting of negative results.
d1pmSSrhf2.main_concern: The central ranking-to-search claim compares active selectors that already have nearly identical M1, and most selectors solve the same easy-or-unsolved tasks, limiting benchmark discriminative power.

kmRuupKhqt.one_liner: HARP uses VLM hindsight reflection to generate subtask corrections for high-level robot policies, paired with FLUTE best-of-N foresight selection.
kmRuupKhqt.problem: Pretrained robot policies need to autonomously learn from mistakes and risky decisions in new scenarios without human-in-the-loop corrections.
kmRuupKhqt.method: HARP prompts a VLM to reflect in hindsight on robot rollouts, converting identified mistakes and risks into subtask-level language corrections that update a high-level policy guiding a low-level controller; at inference, FLUTE applies best-of-N selection with a VLM foresight critic.
kmRuupKhqt.key_idea: Uses VLM hindsight reflection to synthesize subtask-level corrections for high-level policy updates and a VLM foresight critic for best-of-N execution.
kmRuupKhqt.evidence: Evaluated on robot route/manipulation tasks against behavior-cloning policies, residual RL, and a modified YAY Robot baseline, with qualitative behavioral visualizations.
kmRuupKhqt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear complementary design of HARP hindsight training and FLUTE test-time selection, as well as the clear presentation and visualizations.
kmRuupKhqt.main_concern: Policies are adapted and tested on the same routes without held-out generalization tests, and ablations do not isolate hindsight reasoning from generic VLM supervision.

9IBvNRXDB2.one_liner: Constructs fixed three-regular spectral-expander masks that exactly represent any ReLU network with polylogarithmic depth overhead.
9IBvNRXDB2.problem: It has remained open whether fixed, constant-degree sparse masks with a uniform spectral gap can universally approximate ReLU networks with bounded depth overhead.
9IBvNRXDB2.method: Using auxiliary Ramanujan graphs, the authors construct a task-independent three-regular mask at every power-of-two width n >= 32, repeated across layers, that achieves a width-independent spectral gap and supports permutation routing, plus a shuffle-exchange variant and a pruning-robust block version.
9IBvNRXDB2.key_idea: Constructs a repeated three-regular mask combining a width-independent spectral gap with permutation routing to simulate arbitrary ReLU networks exactly.
9IBvNRXDB2.evidence: Purely theoretical proofs of exact ReLU representation with linear width and polylogarithmic depth overhead (logarithmic for shuffle-exchange) and pruning survival in block masks.
9IBvNRXDB2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers consider the exact-representation theorem on a fixed degree-three expander mask technically clean and value the distinction between expansion and routing.
9IBvNRXDB2.main_concern: The custom constructed mask family is disconnected from practical random/Ramanujan masks used in pruning, and formal definitions and positioning relative to expander universality work need tightening.

MfGbNWGAaO.one_liner: Runs iterative sparse-plus-low-rank pruning first, then quantizes kept weights once with per-row elastic-bucket codebooks and refits the low-rank correction.
MfGbNWGAaO.problem: Training-free LLM compression methods that combine pruning, quantization, and low-rank repair suffer accuracy loss when quantizing inside the pruning loop or omit quantization altogether.
MfGbNWGAaO.method: QUENCH executes an iterative sparse-plus-low-rank procedure first so the low-rank correction can update the sparse mask, then quantizes surviving weights once using unweighted per-row learned codebooks (elastic-bucket quantization, EBQ), and finally refits the low-rank correction.
MfGbNWGAaO.key_idea: Defer per-row codebook quantization until after iterative sparse-plus-low-rank mask refinement, then refit the low-rank correction so unweighted quantization suffices.
MfGbNWGAaO.evidence: Evaluated on LLaMA-2 and LLaMA-3-8B with 2:4 sparsity and 3-bit/4-bit weights (WikiText2 perplexity, fixed-mask and activation-weighting controls) against EoRA, LeanQuant, and ApiQ.
MfGbNWGAaO.claimed_gains: On LLaMA-3-8B (2:4 sparsity, 3-bit), quantizing once after the loop gives WikiText2 perplexity 12.09 ± 0.13 vs 16.74 ± 0.19 inside the loop, and the final correction shrinks the unweighted EBQ vs LeanQuant gap from 15.1 to 0.1 perplexity points.
MfGbNWGAaO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that systematically studying compression-order interactions and activation-weighting trade-offs yields a clear, training-free pipeline with strong quality-compression results.
MfGbNWGAaO.main_concern: Conceptual novelty over prior alternating sparse-plus-low-rank methods (HASSLE-free, 3BASiL, OATS) is limited, direct comparisons to HASSLE-free/3BASiL are missing, and models are restricted to older LLaMA-2/3.

iCm5m0InpY.one_liner: Amortizes Wasserstein KL gradient flow by regressing a diffusion model's bridge denoiser onto self-generated replay-buffer updates without density evaluation.
iCm5m0InpY.problem: Amortizing Langevin/Wasserstein KL descent into diffusion samplers typically requires evaluating the intractable current model density or score and expensive fresh energy evaluations.
iCm5m0InpY.method: WASABI derives first-order bridge-interpolant drift updates that translate Wasserstein KL descent steps into density-free regression targets using unbiased, empirically low-variance estimators. A fixed-point loop alternates teacher-guided regression updates with sample generation, reusing energy-gradient evaluations via a replay buffer.
iCm5m0InpY.key_idea: Translate Wasserstein KL gradient steps into density-free bridge-denoiser regression updates trained via a frozen-teacher fixed-point loop with an energy-gradient replay buffer.
iCm5m0InpY.evidence: Supported by first-order Wasserstein transport derivations and experiments on alanine dipeptide and interacting particle system benchmarks.
iCm5m0InpY.claimed_gains: On alanine dipeptide, outperforms reported baselines using an estimated 3.3 times fewer energy evaluations.
iCm5m0InpY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that connecting Wasserstein gradient flow to density-free bridge-denoiser updates is a conceptually strong and substantive theoretical framework.
iCm5m0InpY.main_concern: Practical training deviates from theory by downweighting covariance (lambda_t < 1), reusing stale replay samples, and using approximate denoisers without proving convergence or isolating architectural choices on alanine dipeptide.

wVDXJeIQE6.one_liner: Predicts local geometric offsets and doubly stochastic routing matrices for end-to-end trainable soft ordering in point-cloud state space models.
wVDXJeIQE6.problem: Fixed geometric hard orderings for 3D point clouds cannot be optimized by the task loss, forcing state space models to adapt to suboptimal token sequences.
wVDXJeIQE6.method: Geometry-guided Conservative Soft Ordering (GCSO) predicts a local offset for each scan position in a geometric base order using token features and coordinates, centering continuous weights over neighboring tokens. These weights are organized into a nonnegative doubly stochastic routing matrix so every scan position receives one unit of assignment and every source token contributes one unit of participation.
wVDXJeIQE6.key_idea: Replaces discrete hard token ordering with feature-conditioned local offsets and a nonnegative doubly stochastic routing matrix optimized end to end by the task loss.
wVDXJeIQE6.evidence: Evaluated on point-cloud shape classification and part segmentation, including ModelNet40 and ScanObjectNN against Mamba-based baselines with ablations.
wVDXJeIQE6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the motivation is clear, the doubly stochastic conservative routing construction is mathematically well defined, and the experimental results on ScanObjectNN are strong.
wVDXJeIQE6.main_concern: Reviewers question the technical distinction from prior differentiable scanning methods like DM3D and Sinkhorn-based soft sorting, and note that evaluation is limited to small object-level datasets.

ImKOctG8Ly.one_liner: Benchmarks 20 intrinsic motivation objectives in a biomechanical fruit-fly simulator to test whether skill learning reproduces spontaneous fly exploration.
ImKOctG8Ly.problem: The computational mechanisms by which animals generate autonomous, intrinsically motivated behavior and advance neural representations of future actions without external rewards remain poorly understood.
ImKOctG8Ly.method: The authors build a hierarchical agent whose policy selects from a discrete library of fixed low-level motor primitives inside a neuromechanical digital twin of Drosophila (NeuroMechFlyv2) and train it without external reward across 20 curiosity, entropy, and competency objectives. Frozen policies are evaluated in a virtual tethered-ball assay to compare locomotor statistics and decode future turn directions against whole-brain fly recordings.
ImKOctG8Ly.key_idea: Trains a hierarchical policy over discrete motor primitives in a biomechanical fly simulator across 20 intrinsic objectives and compares locomotor diversity and turn-direction decoding to real fly data.
ImKOctG8Ly.evidence: Benchmarks 20 intrinsic motivation algorithms (including DIAYN, CSF, and Random-DIAYN controls) in NeuroMechFlyv2 against whole-brain Drosophila recordings in a virtual tethered-ball assay.
ImKOctG8Ly.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining a biomechanically realistic fruit-fly simulator with a 20-objective intrinsic motivation benchmark is a valuable setup for testing normative models of autonomous behavior.
ImKOctG8Ly.main_concern: Reviewers point out that holding a single random discrete skill fixed throughout a rollout lacks biological support and may confound prospective turn decoding with persistent skill-level turning biases.

ObZm39LTHi.one_liner: Disentangles LLM trajectories into typed dependency graphs to retrieve domain-specific knowledge externally while distilling generalizable reasoning into SLM weights.
ObZm39LTHi.problem: Existing LLM-SLM collaboration methods do not systematically decide which LLM-provided information should be internalized into small-model parameters versus stored externally for retrieval.
ObZm39LTHi.method: KSplit uses typed dependency graphs to separate LLM-generated trajectories into domain-specific knowledge and generalizable reasoning capabilities. Domain-specific facts are stored in an external repository for on-demand retrieval, while generalizable reasoning operations are distilled into the SLM parameters.
ObZm39LTHi.key_idea: Decomposes LLM trajectories via typed dependency graphs to store domain-specific knowledge externally and distill generalizable reasoning operations into SLM weights.
ObZm39LTHi.evidence: Evaluated across five tasks including OpenBookQA and QuaRel using Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct as the student model, with reversed-placement (KR vs RK) and Graph-R vs Bag-R comparisons.
ObZm39LTHi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the question of what to internalize versus retrieve in LLM-SLM collaboration is well motivated and that separating knowledge from reasoning via typed dependency graphs is reasonable.
ObZm39LTHi.main_concern: Reviewers note that statistical support for the proposed placement over the reversed configuration is weak across tasks (positive only on OpenBookQA) and all experiments use only a single 3B student model.

HVSEqgG4ir.one_liner: Stores complete structured interaction logs externally so coding agents can query long-horizon environment history programmatically.
HVSEqgG4ir.problem: Long-horizon LLM agents face a context-management tradeoff where retaining full observation histories hurts retrieval while compression drops critical details.
HVSEqgG4ir.method: PRO-LONG saves the complete structured interaction trajectory to external files and gives a minimal coding agent programmatic tools (e.g., Python) to search and inspect past states across steps and episodes.
HVSEqgG4ir.key_idea: Persist full structured environment logs externally and let a coding agent query history on demand with programmatic code execution instead of compressing context.
HVSEqgG4ir.evidence: Evaluated on ARC-AGI-3 and NetHack across multiple model families (GPT, Claude, Kimi) and agent harnesses (Codex, Claude Code, Mini-SWE) with cost and truncation ablations.
HVSEqgG4ir.claimed_gains: Reaches up to 2.2x the scores of a base coding agent on NetHack.
HVSEqgG4ir.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the approach is simple, transparent, easy to audit across models and harnesses, and achieves strong token-cost efficiency on ARC-AGI-3.
HVSEqgG4ir.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over prior external programmatic-context agents and argue ablations show most gains stem from Python tool access and short recent logs rather than long-horizon or cross-episode memory.

yQUjLyRLkW.one_liner: Applies envelope regression to split features into four orthogonal subspaces and penalizes only the shared predictive-sensitive overlap.
yQUjLyRLkW.problem: Fair regression with multivariate sensitive attributes often discards useful predictive signal when penalizing all sensitive-associated feature variation indiscriminately.
yQUjLyRLkW.method: Fair Envelope Regression Models (FERM) decompose feature variation into predictive-only, shared predictive-sensitive, sensitive-only, and residual subspaces via envelope methodology, excluding response-immaterial sensitive directions and applying a tunable penalty solely to the shared component.
yQUjLyRLkW.key_idea: Use envelope subspace decomposition to isolate the shared predictive-sensitive feature component and apply fairness regularization exclusively to that overlap.
yQUjLyRLkW.evidence: Provides asymptotic consistency, fairness, and variance-reduction proofs plus simulations and two small real-data healthcare experiments (including MEPS).
yQUjLyRLkW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the four-way predictive-sensitive subspace decomposition is intuitive, interpretable, and backed by solid asymptotic theoretical analysis.
yQUjLyRLkW.main_concern: Reviewers criticize weak empirical validation (only two small healthcare datasets with questionable payment-based sensitive attributes), limited baseline comparisons, and evaluating fairness solely via the optimized R^2_S proxy.

OKIFOUrhbD.one_liner: Segments demonstrations into subgoals and trains variable-horizon flow-matching VLA policies aligned to each subgoal's temporal boundary.
OKIFOUrhbD.problem: Hierarchical Vision-Language-Action policies with fixed-horizon action chunks often ignore intermediate Chain-of-Thought subgoals and over-rely on visual inputs.
OKIFOUrhbD.method: TARA heuristically segments demonstrations into subgoals using visual and behavioral cues (such as velocity zero-crossings) and trains flow-matching policies to predict variable-length action chunks aligned to the remaining steps of each subgoal.
OKIFOUrhbD.key_idea: Align flow-matching VLA action-chunk horizons dynamically with heuristically segmented subgoal boundaries so low-level actions match intermediate reasoning traces.
OKIFOUrhbD.evidence: Evaluated on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, OOD-90 steerability benchmarks, and small real-world robot trials.
OKIFOUrhbD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree temporal misalignment between fixed action chunks and reasoning subgoals is a relevant VLA issue and that aligning chunk horizons to subgoals is straightforward and intuitive.
OKIFOUrhbD.main_concern: Reviewers argue experiments fail to isolate temporal alignment from next-subgoal chaining supervision (which accounts for a large LIBERO drop when removed) and note fragile heuristic segmentation and limited real-world trials.

IIVZN386PT.one_liner: Introduces PersistQA, a 3,299-question long-video benchmark diagnosing person identity grounding, frame sampling, and evidence reading in VLMs.
IIVZN386PT.problem: Aggregate accuracy on long-video QA benchmarks conceals whether VLMs fail to sample relevant frames, mislink a person's identity across scenes, or misread supplied visual evidence.
IIVZN386PT.method: PersistQA provides 3,299 eight-option questions over 409 videos linking a person across moments, paired with controlled diagnostics comparing CLIP identity features, explicit VLM identity checks, and single-frame evidence insertion.
IIVZN386PT.key_idea: Decompose long-video person-QA errors using controlled identity-pair tests and fixed-budget single-frame evidence insertion over 3,299 eight-option questions.
IIVZN386PT.evidence: Evaluated 27 open-weight and closed-source models, frozen CLIP features, and a human no-look-back baseline on 3,299 questions over 409 videos.
IIVZN386PT.claimed_gains: Best open-weight and closed-source models score 27.2% and 29.3% vs. 60% human baseline; CLIP separates same/different person pairs at 85.2% vs. 50.6-62.6% for VLMs; 8 uniform frames miss ~53% of answer windows, inserting one evidence frame adds 4.3-9.7 percentage points, yet 61-78% remain wrong even with evidence provided.
IIVZN386PT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree PersistQA targets an underexplored identity-grounding gap and uses informative fixed-budget frame-insertion diagnostics across a wide model suite.
IIVZN386PT.main_concern: Reviewers warn that adversarial text-only filtering uses evaluated model families (confounding difficulty) and that ground-truth person-linkage verification and human baseline details are insufficiently specified.

C8Nh9RcFD4.one_liner: Combines syntactic width pruning, consensus/execution-gated depth stopping, and contrastive meta-aggregation to prevent LLM aggregator poisoning.
C8Nh9RcFD4.problem: Unconditional test-time search expansion wastes compute and suffers from aggregator poisoning when corrupted candidate traces degrade synthesis below single-pass CoT.
C8Nh9RcFD4.method: RESOLVE preserves shared context across branches while applying syntactic width pruning to filter invalid candidates, adaptive depth stopping via reasoning consensus or code execution feedback, and contrastive meta-aggregation over divergent rationales.
C8Nh9RcFD4.key_idea: Gate out malformed reasoning branches syntactically, stop sampling dynamically via consensus or execution feedback, and synthesize remaining traces via contrastive meta-aggregation.
C8Nh9RcFD4.evidence: Evaluated across six benchmarks (including HumanEval and LiveCodeBench) and four LLM backbones against CoT, SC, ToT, and GoT.
C8Nh9RcFD4.claimed_gains: Standard GoT collapses from 70.4% to 64.9% on HumanEval due to aggregator poisoning (RESOLVE numeric gains not stated in abstract).
C8Nh9RcFD4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree aggregator poisoning is an interesting practical failure mode and that combining candidate filtering with adaptive stopping is clearly presented and broadly tested.
C8Nh9RcFD4.main_concern: Reviewers flag an unfair coding evaluation where RESOLVE uses held-out/private evaluation unit tests for early stopping while main baselines do not, with verifier-matched gains shrinking to 0.61 percentage points.

7WibQaet8v.one_liner: Formulates online time-series conformal calibration as a multi-step stochastic control problem solved via dynamic programming.
7WibQaet8v.problem: Existing online conformal prediction methods adjust miscoverage myopically from past errors, often producing overly wide or infinite prediction intervals under poorly calibrated forecasters.
7WibQaet8v.method: Bellman Conformal Inference (BCI) wraps any multi-step time-series forecaster and solves a one-dimensional stochastic control problem via dynamic programming at each step to allocate miscoverage across future horizons while minimizing average interval length.
7WibQaet8v.key_idea: Solve a finite-horizon 1D dynamic program over multi-step forecast interval-length curves to trade off miscoverage budget and interval width online.
7WibQaet8v.evidence: Proves long-term coverage under arbitrary shifts and near-optimality under approximate calibration, and evaluates empirically on classical (GARCH) and neural (Transformer/LSTM) forecasters.
7WibQaet8v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree casting multi-step online conformal calibration as a model-agnostic stochastic control problem solved by dynamic programming is a compelling formulation.
7WibQaet8v.main_concern: Reviewers flag a mismatch between open-loop action vectors in the efficiency proof and feedback policies in the Bellman recursion, a gap between approximate-calibration theory and poorly calibrated empirical gains, and missing recent online conformal baselines.

2acqQMu2fI.one_liner: Wraps Tweedie plug-in diffusion inverse solvers with three training-free modules that steer sampling toward smaller low-noise likelihood-guidance norms.
2acqQMu2fI.problem: Tweedie plug-in diffusion inverse solvers exhibit large reconstruction quality variance across noise realizations, with poor perceptual quality correlated with high low-noise likelihood-guidance norms.
2acqQMu2fI.method: Norm-Controlled Likelihood Guidance (NCLG) is a training-free three-module wrapper that monitors likelihood-score norms and steers sampling trajectories toward lower-norm regions while keeping the pretrained diffusion prior intact, supported by a low-noise score-error certificate.
2acqQMu2fI.key_idea: Use low-noise likelihood-guidance norm as a trajectory diagnostic and steer Tweedie plug-in diffusion inverse sampling toward smaller likelihood norms without retraining.
2acqQMu2fI.evidence: Theoretical certificate under a multi-modal Tweedie model and experiments across four pixel-space host solvers on FFHQ and ImageNet-256 (48 main comparisons).
2acqQMu2fI.claimed_gains: Improves host solvers across all reported rows on FFHQ and ImageNet-256 (exact numbers not stated in abstract).
2acqQMu2fI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the low-noise likelihood-norm diagnostic is an interesting observation and the plug-and-play wrapper consistently improves LPIPS across four host solvers under matched compute.
2acqQMu2fI.main_concern: Reviewers question the theoretical proof (the discrepancy floor does not vanish as claimed), note weak causal linkage between norm reduction and LPIPS gains, and cite high runtime/memory overhead (~5.5x slower on DPS) and pixel-space-only testing.

u1FnZ6SYcq.one_liner: Evolves and max-min selects quality-constrained system prompt ensembles, sampling one prompt uniformly per query for creative generation.
u1FnZ6SYcq.problem: Preference-aligned LLMs suffer from mode collapse, while existing test-time diversity methods often fail to deliver single responses that are simultaneously high-quality, diverse, and novel.
u1FnZ6SYcq.method: SEPO frames creative generation as three-objective distributional optimization, evolves candidate system prompts offline, applies greedy max-min selection under a quality constraint to pick behaviorally distinct prompts, and uniformly samples one prompt at inference.
u1FnZ6SYcq.key_idea: Evolve candidate system prompts offline, select a quality-constrained subset via greedy max-min behavioral separation, and uniformly sample one prompt per inference call.
u1FnZ6SYcq.evidence: Evaluated across four creative generation tasks and three open-weight models against four test-time baselines using LLM-judge, embedding, and n-gram metrics.
u1FnZ6SYcq.claimed_gains: All three scores (quality, diversity, novelty) fall within 30% of their best observed values in 91.7% of scenarios versus 58.3% for the strongest baseline.
u1FnZ6SYcq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree separating quality, diversity, and novelty into explicit distribution-level objectives is a clear, useful framing backed by comprehensive evaluation metrics.
u1FnZ6SYcq.main_concern: Reviewers note a disconnect between the three-objective formalism and the multi-heuristic pipeline (novelty is not directly optimized), high offline proposal cost (~640 per dataset), missing iterative prompt-optimization baselines, and unclear base-prompt construction.

5YnwBAih55.one_liner: Evaluates static LLM-generated curricula with 1,428 human learners against Bayesian pedagogy across formal and naturalistic concept-learning tasks.
5YnwBAih55.problem: Prior work on AI tutoring focuses on interactive dialogue, leaving unclear how much of LLM teaching effectiveness comes from structuring a static curriculum in advance.
5YnwBAih55.method: The authors compare pre-generated LLM curricula against Bayes-optimal teaching models on tractable concept-learning tasks and test spontaneous concept decomposition on compositional and naturalistic scientific/mathematical subjects with human learners.
5YnwBAih55.key_idea: Isolate static curriculum generation from interactive tutoring by comparing LLM-chosen example sequences and concept decompositions against Bayesian pedagogy in human learning experiments.
5YnwBAih55.evidence: Evaluated with 1,428 human learners across four concept-learning settings spanning formal Bayesian-tractable tasks and naturalistic science/math subjects.
5YnwBAih55.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree separating static curriculum design from interactive dialogue and combining Bayesian pedagogy benchmarks with a 1,428-participant human study is well-motivated and informative.
5YnwBAih55.main_concern: Reviewers note that decomposed curricula include more content and practice (confounding organization with quantity), regressions omit within-participant and shared-curriculum random effects, and prompts supply ordered objectives.

L4ySmVeOMN.one_liner: Evolves archives of diverse scientific problems using adaptive semantic descriptors and solver-transferability fitness objectives.
L4ySmVeOMN.problem: Autonomous scientific discovery requires AI systems to invent diverse new problems with reusable solutions rather than only solving human-curated benchmarks.
L4ySmVeOMN.method: Psi-Evolve combines evolutionary computation with adaptive semantic descriptors, mutations, and transfer-based selection objectives to build problem archives whose induced solvers zero-shot transfer across a domain and warm-start downstream LLM solution search.
L4ySmVeOMN.key_idea: Evolve problem archives under adaptive semantic descriptors and select problems by how well their induced solvers transfer zero-shot to other problems in the domain.
L4ySmVeOMN.evidence: Evaluated across three mathematical domains with multiple seeds, ablations, a blinded expert study, and open-sourced code/data.
L4ySmVeOMN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree autonomous problem discovery guided by solver transferability and adaptive semantic exploration is a meaningful direction supported by multi-domain experiments and an expert study.
L4ySmVeOMN.main_concern: Reviewers stress that zero-shot evaluation relies on oracle best-of-100 solver selection (omitting archive and selection costs), solver transferability does not guarantee scientific value, and some baseline implementations had defects.

pto0V097j0.one_liner: Introduces AgentVidBench, a multi-hop video QA benchmark with tool-agnostic evidence milestones for trajectory evaluation of MLLM agents.
pto0V097j0.problem: Existing video QA benchmarks emphasize single-step global queries and final-answer accuracy without verifying whether MLLM agents actually acquire the multi-hop visual evidence needed.
pto0V097j0.method: AgentVidBench pairs 100 multi-hop spatial, temporal, and causal video questions over 71 videos with step-by-step solution traces and tool-agnostic evidence milestones to score both final accuracy and intermediate evidence acquisition.
pto0V097j0.key_idea: Evaluate multi-hop MLLM video agents using tool-agnostic evidence milestones extracted from solution traces alongside final-answer accuracy.
pto0V097j0.evidence: Evaluated 12 proprietary and open-source MLLMs in single-turn and agentic workflows on 100 questions across 71 videos, plus a 20-question human-alignment check.
pto0V097j0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree extending video-agent evaluation beyond final answers to tool-agnostic evidence milestones is well-motivated and diagnostically useful across agent interfaces.
pto0V097j0.main_concern: Reviewers note the small dataset size (100 questions over 71 videos with sparse spatial/causal coverage), lack of video-free or option-order controls, text-only milestone judging, and overlap with prior trajectory benchmarks like MINERVA.

NHlR0tUeNg.one_liner: Predicts a single clip-shared color flow from aggregated video color statistics for temporally consistent single-reference video color transfer.
NHlR0tUeNg.problem: Frame-wise video color transfer causes flickering under motion or lighting shifts, whereas global linear clip transforms lack expressiveness for complex reference palettes.
NHlR0tUeNg.method: TCFlow aggregates global color statistics across a content video clip via a color aggregator and predicts one clip-shared meta-flow (trained via function-space distillation) to map the video's color distribution to a single reference image without optical flow or test-time optimization.
NHlR0tUeNg.key_idea: Aggregate clip-wide color statistics to predict one shared flow transformation across all frames, decoupling global color mapping from per-frame variations without optical flow.
NHlR0tUeNg.evidence: Evaluated across multiple video benchmarks with discrepant/random reference assignments, aggregation ablations, and supplementary videos.
NHlR0tUeNg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree using a single clip-shared flow predicted from aggregated statistics is a clear, coherent mechanism for reducing flickering without optical flow or test-time optimization.
NHlR0tUeNg.main_concern: Reviewers flag a mathematical flaw in claiming one invertible clip flow aligns every frame's distinct distribution identically, insufficient comparison to recent methods (ColorFM, PETAL, SA-LUT), and weak temporal metrics.

dMk01nffgV.one_liner: Establishes matching minimax regret horizon exponents and three sharp ambiguity radii for single-trajectory distributionally robust average-reward RL.
dMk01nffgV.problem: Statistical limits and structural solvability thresholds for online single-trajectory distributionally robust average-reward RL over f-divergence balls remain uncharacterized.
dMk01nffgV.method: Using transition deletion cost and asymptotic divergence slope, the authors define three sharp radii separating weak communication and Bellman solvability, and prove matching minimax policy-regret exponents via a Bellman-dominion completion upper bound and revealing-state lower bounds.
dMk01nffgV.key_idea: Characterize f-divergence robust average-reward MDPs via three exact transition-deletion/creation radii and prove tight T^(1/2) and T^(2/3) minimax policy-regret rates via Bellman completion.
dMk01nffgV.evidence: Purely theoretical analysis on tabular MDPs with rectangular f-divergence uncertainty sets and bounded structural parameters.
dMk01nffgV.claimed_gains: Minimax policy regret is O-tilde(sqrt(T)) when transition creation is impossible and delta < delta_bell(P), O-tilde(T^(2/3)) with creation for communicating nominal MDPs and 0 < delta < theta_f(1), and zero at delta >= theta_f(1).
dMk01nffgV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the structural separation of the three exact ambiguity radii and the matching horizon-exponent rate proofs for single-trajectory robust RL are technically substantive.
dMk01nffgV.main_concern: Reviewers find the notation-heavy presentation hard to read, question the operational meaning of policy regret versus cumulative-reward regret, and note restrictive rectangularity and unmatched instance-parameter dependencies.

aWeTP9FH13.one_liner: Detects compromised multi-agent invocations via context-predicted benign activations and steers them token-by-token using learned attack deviations.
aWeTP9FH13.problem: Pruning defenses break multi-agent collaboration, while static benign-prototype activation defenses ignore context-dependent activation shifts and fail to correct malicious outputs.
aWeTP9FH13.method: CompassGuard predicts expected benign activations from each agent's execution context to detect anomalies, and trains a Deviation Estimator on paired clean/attacked executions to estimate and subtract attack-induced deviations token by token during generation without pruning edges.
aWeTP9FH13.key_idea: Separate context-conditioned benign activation prediction for detection from paired-execution attack-deviation estimation for token-wise activation subtraction.
aWeTP9FH13.evidence: Evaluated across six benchmarks under homogeneous and heterogeneous multi-agent roles with component ablations.
