aWeTP9FH13.claimed_gains: Attains 97.9% average detection F1 and reduces average attack success rate from 17.7% to 5.2% relative to the prior activation-based defense.
aWeTP9FH13.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree separating context-aware detection from activation correction while preserving multi-agent topology addresses a real limitation and achieves strong detection and ASR reductions.
aWeTP9FH13.main_concern: Reviewers flag evaluation-code inconsistencies (excluding invalid outputs and test instances, counting directly attacked agents in ASR), lack of adaptive-attacker tests, and limited novelty over existing activation-steering defenses.

DtGr3M1Z20.one_liner: Guides LLM agent experience extraction and utility updates using a Trajectory Quality Loss and paired rollouts with and without retrieval.
DtGr3M1Z20.problem: Experience-based LLM agent learning typically relies only on final binary task outcomes, ignoring intermediate execution quality when extracting and scoring reusable experiences.
DtGr3M1Z20.method: TQG-Exp defines a Trajectory Quality Loss combining completion and process quality, runs paired rollouts with and without retrieved experiences to extract task-level and task-type-level experiences, and updates experience utility from paired quality differences for utility-and-relevance retrieval.
DtGr3M1Z20.key_idea: Score agent trajectories with a joint outcome-and-process Trajectory Quality Loss and update experience utilities from paired with-versus-without-retrieval rollout differences.
DtGr3M1Z20.evidence: Evaluated on ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld with two backbone LLMs against ReasoningBank, MemP, MemRL, and DELTAMEM.
DtGr3M1Z20.claimed_gains: Improves Avg.@3 over the strongest baseline by 4.50 (abstract truncated after first number).
DtGr3M1Z20.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree incorporating process-level trajectory quality into experience bank optimization is simple, well-motivated, and yields strong results across three agent benchmarks.
DtGr3M1Z20.main_concern: Reviewers point out that ablations without successful trajectory retrieval perform comparably to MemRL (confounding process feedback with trajectory demonstrations), alongside hyperparameter sensitivity and missing reproducibility/split details.

rE7vVQPXt1.one_liner: Compresses VLM visual tokens training-free by greedily selecting maximum residual-energy tokens orthogonal to selected spatial or SVD video subspaces.
rE7vVQPXt1.problem: Long visual token sequences impose heavy memory and inference costs on Vision-Language Models due to spatial and temporal redundancy.
rE7vVQPXt1.method: RESET is a text-independent, FlashAttention-compatible token compression method that iteratively picks image tokens with highest residual energy orthogonal to previously selected tokens, and for videos projects current frames orthogonal to an SVD-compressed historical subspace.
rE7vVQPXt1.key_idea: Select visual tokens by maximum residual energy orthogonal to previously chosen spatial tokens and, for videos, orthogonal to an SVD-compressed historical reference subspace.
rE7vVQPXt1.evidence: Evaluated across multiple VLM backbones, compression ratios, and image plus online/offline video understanding benchmarks with component ablations.
rE7vVQPXt1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree RESET is simple, training-free, text-independent, FlashAttention-compatible, and thoroughly evaluated across multiple VLM backbones and image/video benchmarks.
rE7vVQPXt1.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over classical QRCP and reconstruction-based methods like ApET without isolating specific design choices, and question performance on information-dense documents and long-term video memory.

peMXLCiQYA.one_liner: Models single-cell perturbations as norm-preserving latent rotations composed via Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff, with flow matching for unseen perturbations.
peMXLCiQYA.problem: Predicting non-additive interactions of genetic and chemical perturbation pairs before measuring them is difficult because combinatorial space grows quadratically.
peMXLCiQYA.method: OpPert represents each perturbation as a block-diagonal SO(4) rotation of cell latents, composes pairs via Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff using the Lie bracket as an unsupervised non-additivity score, and trains a flow-matching model to generate rotations for unseen perturbations.
peMXLCiQYA.key_idea: Parameterize perturbations as latent rotations whose Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff Lie bracket predicts pairwise non-additive interactions from single-perturbation operators alone.
peMXLCiQYA.evidence: Evaluated on three genetic screens (Norman, K562, RPE1), a small-molecule screen, and RT-qPCR wet-lab validation of predicted Belinostat targets in MCF7 cells.
peMXLCiQYA.claimed_gains: Achieves 81-88% directional accuracy on held-out evaluations across the Norman, K562, and RPE1 genetic screens.
peMXLCiQYA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the norm-preserving rotation parameterization elegant and note strong empirical gains over additive shifts plus wet-lab validation.
peMXLCiQYA.main_concern: Reviewers point out a mismatch between claims and results—disabling the Lie bracket barely changes pair accuracy (92.4% vs. 92.9%)—and an inconsistency where the written objective has zero gradient with respect to the bracket coefficient.

f7naFYZQIg.one_liner: Pretrains an any-spectral Earth observation backbone using sensor-configuration-aware dynamic band tokenization and dual-teacher dense distillation.
f7naFYZQIg.problem: Multimodal Earth observation foundation models struggle to fuse arbitrary sensor band combinations adaptively and often learn weakly discriminative dense features.
f7naFYZQIg.method: ScalSpectra introduces Spectral-Aware Dynamic Band Tokenization (SADBT), which derives a spectral-adaptive query from optical wavelength or SAR polarization/orbit descriptors for patch-wise band fusion, paired with dual-teacher pretraining combining an EMA local-structure teacher and a frozen visual-prior semantic teacher.
f7naFYZQIg.key_idea: Fuse arbitrary spectral bands using a query conditioned on the full observed sensor descriptor set while distilling dense features from EMA structural and frozen semantic teachers.
f7naFYZQIg.evidence: Evaluated on GeoBench segmentation and classification, change detection, source-only domain generalization, and synthetic-to-real height estimation.
f7naFYZQIg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the configuration-aware band fusion motivation convincing and appreciate the broad evaluation across remote-sensing tasks with frozen-backbone probing.
f7naFYZQIg.main_concern: Reviewers highlight missing essential baselines and attributions—especially DINOv3 (the teacher), Panopticon, DOFA++, and DEO—and unclear methodological differentiation and compute transparency.
